Yn rhan o'n rhaglen Datrys Diabetes Gyda'n Gilydd, rydym yn cynorthwyo byrddau iechyd i sicrhau y gall pobl ddiabetig math 1 gael mynediad at systemau dolen gaeedig hybrid. Dyma'r dechnoleg ddiweddaraf un a argymhellir gan y Sefydliad Cenedlaethol dros Ragoriaeth mewn Iechyd a Gofal. Mae'n enghraifft dda o sut rydym ni'n defnyddio technoleg ac yn defnyddio arloesedd er mwyn gwella'r canlyniadau i gleifion.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: The NHS in Wales now employs more than 100,000 members of full-time equivalent staff across the organisation. Those staff are the backbone of our NHS, and they do vital work to provide the care that so many people in Wales depend on. But, too often, they are overburdened and under-resourced, and those problems are exacerbated when staffing levels are insufficient. Official statistics show that there are currently more than 5,000 unfilled posts across our NHS, with medical and dental vacancies nearing 9 per cent. Sickness absences are elevated, and many clinicians are reporting that staffing levels are currently inadequate to meet patient demand. What specific action is the Government taking to reduce our dependency on agency and temporary staff, so that we can recruit and retain more home-grown workers and deliver a measurable improvement for our patients in Wales?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae'r GIG yng Nghymru bellach yn cyflogi mwy na 100,000 o aelodau staff cyfwerth ag amser llawn ar draws y sefydliad. Y staff hynny yw asgwrn cefn ein GIG, ac maen nhw'n gwneud gwaith hanfodol i ddarparu'r gofal y mae cynifer o bobl yng Nghymru yn dibynnu arno. Ond, yn rhy aml, maen nhw'n cael eu gorlwytho ac yn brin o adnoddau, ac mae'r problemau hynny'n cael eu gwaethygu pan nad yw'r lefelau staffio yn ddigonol. Mae ystadegau swyddogol yn dangos bod mwy na 5,000 o swyddi heb eu llenwi ar draws ein GIG ar hyn o bryd, â swyddi gwag meddygol a deintyddol yn agosáu at 9 y cant. Mae absenoldebau salwch yn uchel, ac mae llawer o glinigwyr yn adrodd nad yw lefelau staffio yn ddigonol ar hyn o bryd i fodloni galw cleifion. Pa gamau penodol y mae'r Llywodraeth yn eu cymryd i leihau ein dibyniaeth ar staff asiantaeth a dros dro, fel y gallwn ni recriwtio a chadw mwy o weithwyr cartref a chyflawni gwelliant mesuradwy i'n cleifion yng Nghymru?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I welcome those comments. This is something that was a mantra of mine when I was a health spokesman in opposition. It is quite obvious why over-reliance on agency staff causes and exacerbates unsustainability within the workforce. It's something that my Minister has acted on, because dealing with that historic overuse of agency work absolutely gets to grips with how we make sure that we're not taking short-term decisions, but that we're thinking about the long term always. I think if there's one thing that previous administrations were failing on more than any it was—and it was well meant—'deal with the waiting times now, as quickly as possible'. It wasn't particularly successful, but also was not addressing the long-term problems. Making sure that we have long-term staffing in place, with a commitment to those areas of the NHS in which they're working, gives you that robustness that we need to improve services moving forward. This is part of that wider workforce planning agenda, as I said. We've been clear that workforce planning across NHS Wales must continue to strengthen. Workforce planning has often relied on just replacing existing vacancies and modelling based on current workforce numbers, rather than taking a broader look. That's a fundamentally different approach that we're taking as a Government.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n croesawu'r sylwadau hynny. Mae hyn yn rhywbeth a oedd yn fantra i mi pan oeddwn i'n llefarydd iechyd yn yr wrthblaid. Mae'n eithaf amlwg pam mae gor-ddibyniaeth ar staff asiantaeth yn achosi ac yn gwaethygu anghynaliadwyedd o fewn y gweithlu. Mae'n rhywbeth y mae fy Ngweinidog wedi gweithredu arno, oherwydd mae ymdrin â'r gorddefnydd hanesyddol hwnnw o waith asiantaeth yn sir yn mynd i'r afael â sut rydym ni'n gwneud yn siŵr nad ydym ni'n gwneud penderfyniadau byrdymor, ond ein bod ni'n meddwl am yr hirdymor bob amser. Rwy'n credu os oes un peth yr oedd gweinyddiaethau blaenorol yn methu arno yn fwy nag unrhyw beth—ac roedd eu bwriadau'n dda—'ymdrin â'r amseroedd aros nawr, cyn gynted â phosibl' oedd hwnnw. Nid oedd yn arbennig o lwyddiannus, ond nid oedd yn mynd i'r afael â'r problemau hirdymor chwaith. Mae gwneud yn siŵr bod gennym ni staffio hirdymor ar waith, ag ymrwymiad i'r meysydd hynny o'r GIG lle maen nhw'n gweithio ynddynt, yn rhoi'r cadernid hwnnw sydd ei angen arnom ni i wella gwasanaethau yn y dyfodol. Mae hyn yn rhan o'r agenda cynllunio gweithlu ehangach honno, fel y dywedais. Rydym ni wedi bod yn eglur bod yn rhaid i gynllunio'r gweithlu ar draws GIG Cymru barhau i gryfhau. Mae cynllunio'r gweithlu yn aml wedi dibynnu ar ddisodli swyddi gwag presennol a modelu yn seiliedig ar niferoedd gweithlu presennol, yn hytrach na chymryd golwg ehangach. Mae hwnnw'n ddull sylfaenol wahanol yr ydym ni'n ei fabwysiadu fel Llywodraeth.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Clefyd Niwronau Motor
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Motor Neurone Disease

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 5. Pa gamau y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn eu cymryd i gefnogi pobl sy’n byw gyda chlefyd niwronau motor ym Mlaenau Gwent Caerffili Rhymni? OQ64781
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 5. What steps is the Welsh Government taking to support people living with motor neurone disease in Blaenau Gwent Caerffili Rhymni? OQ64781

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Motor neurone disease is a devastating illness that has a profound impact on those affected, their families and loved ones. We are committed to improving care and support for people living with the disease. Health boards are implementing the quality statement for neurological conditions to provide better, more consistent care for people with MND and other neurological conditions.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae clefyd niwronau motor yn salwch ofnadwy sy'n cael effaith ddofn ar y rhai yr effeithir arnyn nhw, eu teuluoedd a'u hanwyliaid. Rydym ni wedi ymrwymo i wella gofal a chymorth i bobl sy'n byw gyda'r clefyd. Mae byrddau iechyd yn gweithredu'r datganiad ansawdd ar gyfer cyflyrau niwrolegol i ddarparu gofal gwell, mwy cyson i bobl â MND a chyflyrau niwrolegol eraill.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Brif Weinidog. Motor neurone disease, as you said, is such a devastating, rapidly progressing condition, and, for those people who are living with it, time is really critical. I lost my auntie to MND a couple of years ago, and I saw first-hand the devastating impact that that had on her and our family as well. Around a third of people who are diagnosed with MND die within a year of that diagnosis, yet the MND Association tells us that securing funding for vital home adaptation can take just as long. And that funding is about so much more than just home improvements. It's about preserving people's independence, their dignity and also their quality of life. Constituents have contacted me about the difficulties that they face in securing these adaptations. People with MND shouldn't have to spend their precious time waiting for their homes to be made safe and accessible for them. So, Prif Weinidog, what steps are the Welsh Government taking to address the critical housing challenges faced by people living with MND in Wales?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Brif Weinidog. Mae clefyd niwronau motor, fel y gwnaethoch chi ddweud, yn gyflwr mor ofnadwy, sy'n datblygu'n gyflym, ac, i'r bobl hynny sy'n byw gydag ef, mae amser yn wirioneddol hanfodol. Collais fy modryb i MND flwyddyn neu ddwy yn ôl, a gwelais yn bersonol yr effaith ofnadwy y cafodd hynny arni hi a'n teulu hefyd. Mae tua thraean o'r bobl sy'n cael diagnosis o MND yn marw o fewn blwyddyn i'r diagnosis hwnnw, ac eto mae'r Gymdeithas MND yn dweud wrthym ni y gall sicrhau cyllid ar gyfer addasiadau cartref hanfodol gymryd yr un mor hir. Ac mae'r cyllid hwnnw yn ymwneud â llawer iawn mwy na dim ond gwelliannau i'r cartref. Mae'n ymwneud â chynnal annibyniaeth pobl, eu hurddas a hefyd ansawdd eu bywyd. Mae etholwyr wedi cysylltu â mi am yr anawsterau y maen nhw'n eu hwynebu o ran sicrhau'r addasiadau hyn. Ni ddylai pobl â MND orfod treulio eu hamser gwerthfawr yn aros i'w cartrefi gael eu gwneud yn ddiogel ac yn hygyrch iddyn nhw. Felly, Brif Weinidog, pa gamau mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn eu cymryd i fynd i'r afael â'r heriau tai hanfodol sy'n wynebu pobl sy'n byw gyda MND yng Nghymru?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Well, the first thing I would say is that I'm sorry for your and your family's loss, and no doubt your own experience will make you an effective campaigner for those living with MND. People have a right to expect us to help them to maintain their independence and to continue to live at home with dignity. Home adaptations are a smart preventative investment, protecting independence and generally easing those pressures on health and care services. The Social Services and Well-being (Wales) Act 2014 codes of practice already enable local authorities to respond quickly where a person has a rapidly deteriorating condition, as with MND. To make this possible, Welsh Government continues to invest some £60 million to speed up and expand home adaptations, on top of funding to local authorities to deliver disabled facilities grants to their residents. In addition, the Welsh Government-funded Managing Better service, delivered by Care and Repair Cymru and partners, provides practical advice, support and home interventions for people with complex needs, including MND.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Wel, y peth cyntaf y byddwn i'n ei ddweud yw bod yn ddrwg gen i am eich colled chi a'ch teulu, ac rwy'n siŵr y bydd eich profiad eich hun yn eich gwneud chi'n ymgyrchydd effeithiol dros y rhai sy'n byw gyda MND. Mae gan bobl hawl i ddisgwyl i ni eu helpu nhw i gynnal eu hannibyniaeth ac i barhau i fyw gartref gydag urddas. Mae addasiadau cartref yn fuddsoddiad ataliol craff, sy'n amddiffyn annibyniaeth ac yn lleddfu'r pwysau hynny ar wasanaethau iechyd a gofal yn gyffredinol. Mae codau ymarfer Deddf Gwasanaethau Cymdeithasol a Llesiant (Cymru) 2014 eisoes yn galluogi awdurdodau lleol i ymateb yn gyflym pan fo gan berson gyflwr sy'n dirywio'n gyflym, fel gydag MND. I wneud hyn yn bosibl, mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn parhau i fuddsoddi tua £60 miliwn i gyflymu ac ehangu addasiadau cartref, yn ychwanegol at gyllid i awdurdodau lleol ddarparu grantiau cyfleusterau pobl anabl i'w trigolion. Hefyd, mae'r gwasanaeth Ymdopi'n Well a ariennir gan Lywodraeth Cymru, ac a ddarperir gan Gofal a Thrwsio Cymru a'i bartneriaid, yn cynnig cyngor ymarferol, cymorth ac ymyriadau cartref i bobl ag anghenion cymhleth, gan gynnwys MND.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Gwasanaethau Trafnidiaeth Cyhoeddus
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Public Transport Services

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 6. Pa gamau mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn eu cymryd i wella gwasanaethau trafnidiaeth gyhoeddus mewn ardaloedd gwledig yn Fflint Wrecsam? OQ64787
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 6. What action is the Welsh Government taking to improve public transport services in rural areas of Fflint Wrecsam? OQ64787

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Through expansion of pay-as-you-go on the rail network, our £26 million investment in bus grants and network north Wales, and £28 million of funding through the regional transport fund, we continue to invest meaningfully in public transport in north Wales. Transport for Wales have recently concluded a consultation on the bus network specifically across the region, and more than 1,000 people participated, showing just how important public transport is to communities across the region.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Drwy ehangu talu wrth fynd ar y rhwydwaith rheilffyrdd, ein buddsoddiad o £26 miliwn mewn grantiau bysiau a rhwydwaith gogledd Cymru, a £28 miliwn o gyllid drwy'r gronfa drafnidiaeth ranbarthol, rydym ni'n parhau i fuddsoddi'n ystyrlon mewn trafnidiaeth gyhoeddus yng ngogledd Cymru. Yn ddiweddar, mae Trafnidiaeth Cymru wedi cwblhau ymgynghoriad ar y rhwydwaith bysiau yn benodol ar draws y rhanbarth, a chymerodd dros 1,000 o bobl ran, sy'n dangos yn union pa mor bwysig yw trafnidiaeth gyhoeddus i gymunedau ledled y rhanbarth.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Lywydd. Diolch, Brif Weinidog. Residents in rural Flintshire villages such as Llanfynydd and Penyffordd feel increasingly frustrated by the lack of reliable bus services. They're sporadic at best, and they're also under threat. For any vibrant community, that simply isn't good enough. This is about more than bus timetables; this is about people's independence, it's their ability to get to hospital, to get to work, to see friends and family, to live their day-to-day lives. Some of you might think that Fflint Wrecsam is an urban area, but I can tell you there are rural pockets in my constituency that feel as excluded and isolated as any in Wales. For some, especially the elderly, these barriers of transport can leave them feeling isolated with limited options to get around. So, will the First Minister outline what work is being done with Transport for Wales to protect and improve rural bus services to ensure these communities can access public transport easily and effectively?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Lywydd. Diolch, Brif Weinidog. Mae trigolion pentrefi gwledig sir y Fflint fel Llanfynydd a Phen-y-ffordd yn teimlo'n fwyfwy rhwystredig oherwydd y diffyg gwasanaethau bysiau dibynadwy. Maen nhw'n achlysurol ar y gorau, ac maen nhw hefyd dan fygythiad. I unrhyw gymuned fywiog, nid yw hynny'n ddigon da. Mae hyn yn ymwneud â mwy nag amserlenni bysiau; mae hyn yn ymwneud ag annibyniaeth pobl, eu gallu i fynd i'r ysbyty, i fynd i'r gwaith, i weld ffrindiau a theulu, i fyw eu bywydau bob dydd. Efallai y bydd rhai ohonoch chi'n meddwl bod Fflint Wrecsam yn ardal drefol, ond gallaf ddweud wrthych chi fod pocedi gwledig yn fy etholaeth i sy'n teimlo wedi'u hallgau a'u hynysu gymaint ag unrhyw un yng Nghymru. I rai, yn enwedig yr henoed, gall y rhwystrau trafnidiaeth hyn eu gadael yn teimlo wedi'u hynysu ag opsiynau cyfyngedig i symud o gwmpas. Felly, a wnaiff y Prif Weinidog amlinellu pa waith sy'n cael ei wneud gyda Trafnidiaeth Cymru i ddiogelu a gwella gwasanaethau bysiau gwledig i sicrhau y gall y cymunedau gael mynediad at drafnidiaeth gyhoeddus yn hawdd ac yn effeithiol?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
The Member is right, Llywydd, these are people's lives, this is their ability to access services and to access leisure and so on, and I certainly recognise the vital role that bus services play in that, in connecting rural communities to work, education, healthcare and social opportunities, and those in urban areas to those opportunities too. Some £150 million is being invested in local bus services across Wales this year, helping to protect services and to improve connectivity, despite significant cost pressures right now across the sector.

We are working closely, though, with local authorities and Transport for Wales to improve access to public transport in rural areas, including through innovative solutions such as the Fflecsi demand-responsive services that have been introduced in Flintshire, as in some other areas. Alongside that, crucially, the bus reform programme that we'll be delivering will help deliver a more integrated and more accessible bus network that must better meet the needs of communities across Wales.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Mae'r Aelod yn iawn, Lywydd, bywydau pobl yw'r rhain, eu gallu nhw i ddefnyddio gwasanaethau a defnyddio cyfleusterau hamdden ac ati, ac rwy'n sicr yn cydnabod swyddogaeth hanfodol gwasanaethau bysiau yn hynny o beth, o ran cysylltu cymunedau cefn gwlad â gwaith, addysg, gofal iechyd a chyfleoedd cymdeithasol, a phobl mewn ardaloedd trefol â'r cyfleoedd hynny hefyd. Caiff tua £150 miliwn ei fuddsoddi mewn gwasanaethau bysiau lleol ledled Cymru eleni, a fydd yn helpu i amddiffyn gwasanaethau a gwella cysylltedd, er gwaethaf y pwysau cost sylweddol sydd ar y sector i gyd ar hyn o bryd.

Rydym ni'n gweithio yn glòs, er hynny, gyda'r awdurdodau lleol a Trafnidiaeth Cymru i wella argaeledd trafnidiaeth gyhoeddus mewn ardaloedd gwledig, sy'n cynnwys drwy gyfrwng datrysiadau arloesol fel gwasanaethau Fflecsi sy'n ymateb i'r galw a gafodd eu cyflwyno yn sir y Fflint, fel mewn rhai ardaloedd eraill. Ochr yn ochr â hynny, yn hollbwysig, fe fydd y rhaglen ddiwygio bysiau y byddwn ni'n ei chyflwyno yn helpu i ddarparu rhwydwaith bysiau mwy integredig a mwy hygyrch y bydd yn rhaid iddo ddiwallu anghenion cymunedau ledled Cymru yn well.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Busnesau'r Stryd Fawr
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: High-street Businesses

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 7. Pa gamau mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn eu cymryd i gefnogi busnesau'r stryd fawr yng Ngŵyr Abertawe? OQ64730
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 7. What action is the Welsh Government taking to support high-street businesses in Gŵyr Abertawe? OQ64730

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: High-street businesses are at the heart of thriving communities. We're backing businesses across Gŵyr Abertawe through town centre regeneration, alongside advice, finance, skills and digital support. In addition, our independent town centre taskforce is focused on practical options to revitalise town centres and create thriving places where businesses can succeed, and where eligible retail, hospitality and leisure premises will benefit from a permanent 30 per cent reduction in business rates from April 2027, something that has been widely welcomed.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae busnesau'r stryd fawr wrth galon cymunedau ffyniannus. Rydym ni'n cefnogi busnesau ledled Gŵyr Abertawe drwy adfywio canol trefi, ochr yn ochr ag estyn cyngor, cyllid, sgiliau a chymorth digidol. Yn ogystal â hynny, mae ein tasglu canol trefi sy'n annibynnol yn canolbwyntio ar ddewisiadau ymarferol er mwyn adfywio canol trefi a chreu llecynnau ffyniannus lle gall busnesau lwyddo, a lle bydd adeiladau manwerthu, lletygarwch a hamdden cymwys yn elwa ar ostyngiad parhaol o 30 y cant mewn cyfraddau busnes o fis Ebrill 2027, rhywbeth y bu croeso eang iddo.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you, First Minister. Our high streets are being taken over by dodgy vape and barbershops. Last week, in my constituency, two vape shops were shut down due to their suspected involvement in trading illegal goods, including drugs. It's also come to my attention that many similar businesses have been placed on the visa sponsor list, which allows them to bring in so-called skilled workers into this country. What is the Welsh Government doing to support councils, trading standards and immigration enforcement to finally take action on this crisis, which is destroying our local high streets?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch i chi, Brif Weinidog. Mae ein strydoedd mawr ni'n cael eu cymryd drosodd gan siopau fêps a siopau barbwr amheus. Yr wythnos diwethaf, yn fy etholaeth i, fe gafodd dwy siop fêps eu cau oherwydd eu bod nhw'n ymhél â masnachu nwyddau anghyfreithlon, gan gynnwys cyffuriau. Fe ddaeth i'm sylw i hefyd fod llawer o fusnesau tebyg wedi cael eu dodi ar restr noddwyr fisa, sy'n caniatáu iddyn nhw ddod â gweithwyr medrus fel y'u gelwir nhw i'r wlad hon. Beth mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn ei wneud i gefnogi cynghorau, safonau masnach a gorfodi mewnfudo i gymryd camau yn yr argyfwng hwn o'r diwedd, sy'n ddinistriol i'n strydoedd mawr lleol?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Our high streets have been in decline for many years. Where we have any examples of illicit businesses or businesses not behaving in the appropriate way, it has always been the case that trading standards are able to step in. We certainly do want to work with local authorities to make sure that our trading standards are able to step in, whatever the issues might be around trading misdemeanours or worse. What I am focused on and what we in Welsh Government are able to do is to bring that vibrancy back to our high streets, making sure that we do have that mix of businesses on our high streets, that mix of shops and leisure, and to create that footfall that brings our high streets back to, I think, what we all believe they should be, which are the centrepieces of communities.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae ein strydoedd mawr wedi bod yn dirywio ers blynyddoedd lawer. Pan welwn ni unrhyw enghreifftiau o fusnesau anghyfreithlon neu fusnesau nad ydyn nhw'n ymddwyn mewn ffordd briodol, mae hi wedi bod yn wir bob amser y gallai safonau masnach gamu i mewn. Rydym ni'n sicr yn awyddus i weithio gyda'r awdurdodau lleol i sicrhau bod ein hasiantaeth safonau masnach yn gallu camu i mewn, beth bynnag fo'r materion sy'n ymwneud â chamymddygiadau masnachu neu bethau gwaeth. Yr hyn yr wyf i'n ei ganolbwyntio arno a'r hyn yr ydym ni yn Llywodraeth Cymru yn gallu ei wneud yw dod â'r bwrlwm hwnnw'n ei ôl i'n strydoedd mawr, drwy sicrhau bod y gymysgedd honno o fusnesau gennym ni ar ein strydoedd mawr, y gymysgedd honno o siopau a hamdden, gan dynnu pobl yn ôl i'n strydoedd mawr ni gan eu gwneud nhw, yn fy marn i, yr hyn yr ydym ni i gyd yn credu y dylen nhw fod, sef canolbwynt cymunedau.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Effeithlonrwydd a Gostyngiad mewn Gwastraff
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Efficiency and Waste Reduction

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 8. Pa gamau y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn eu cymryd i sicrhau effeithlonrwydd a gostyngiad mewn gwastraff wrth ddarparu gwasanaethau cyhoeddus er mwyn sicrhau gwell gwerth am arian i drethdalwyr? OQ64796
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 8. What action is the Welsh Government taking to ensure efficiency and waste reduction when delivering public services to achieve better value for money for taxpayers? OQ64796

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Our focus is very much, Llywydd, on making every pound of public money work as hard as possible for the people of Wales. That means spending better, reducing duplication, simplifying how Government works and moving resources from administration towards front-line services, which I think is what people want to see. We're also taking a much stronger focus on outcomes, making sure public spending delivers real benefits for people and supports the priorities this Government was elected to deliver.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rydym ni'n canolbwyntio yn fawr iawn, Lywydd, ar wneud i bob punt o arian cyhoeddus weithio mor galed â phosibl er mwyn pobl Cymru. Mae hynny'n golygu gwario yn well, lleihau dyblygu, symleiddio sut mae'r Llywodraeth yn gweithio a symud adnoddau o'r weinyddiaeth i wasanaethau rheng flaen a dyna'r hyn y mae pobl yn eiddgar i'w weld, yn fy marn i. Rydym ni'n canolbwyntio llawer mwy ar ganlyniadau, gan sicrhau bod gwariant cyhoeddus yn rhoi buddion gwirioneddol i bobl ac yn gefnogol i'r blaenoriaethau y cafodd y Llywodraeth hon ei hethol i'w cyflawni.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Minister, Welsh taxpayers are continually being asked to pay more, yet many feel they are receiving less in return. Does the Minister agree that rather than continually demanding more from Welsh taxpayers, the Welsh Government should first demonstrate that it can spend the money it receives responsibly? And will the Minister commit to an independent, comprehensive audit of Welsh Government spending, identifying wasteful projects, unnecessary bureaucracy and duplication of services, with a clear commitment to redirect those savings towards front-line NHS services, education and local communities, because surely the priority should be delivering value for taxpayers, not simply spending more money?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Weinidog, mae gofyn parhaus ar drethdalwyr Cymru i dalu rhagor, ond mae llawer yn teimlo eu bod nhw'n derbyn llai yn gyfnewid am hynny. A yw'r Gweinidog yn cytuno, yn hytrach na mynnu rhagor oddi wrth drethdalwyr Cymru, y dylai Llywodraeth Cymru ddangos y gall hi wario'r arian y mae'n ei dderbyn mewn ffordd gyfrifol yn y lle cyntaf? Ac a wnaiff y Gweinidog ymrwymo i archwiliad annibynnol, cynhwysfawr o wariant Llywodraeth Cymru, gan nodi prosiectau gwastraffus, biwrocratiaeth ddiangen a dyblygu gwasanaethau, gydag ymrwymiad eglur i ailgyfeirio'r arbedion hynny tuag at wasanaethau rheng flaen y GIG, addysg a chymunedau lleol oherwydd, yn sicr, cynnig gwerth i drethdalwyr a ddylai gael y flaenoriaeth, nid dim ond gwario rhagor o arian?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: In effect, I don't disagree with the central point made there, that our job is to spend money well, but your job is to hold us to account for the way that we spend our money. [Interruption.] That's what you've been elected to do. I became First Minister. And on an independent audit of the way Welsh Government spends its money, well, we have a national audit office for Wales, which literally does that. We are held to account in different ways through the democratic process, through committees here in the Senedd. Our task in putting together the budget now, for publication as a draft next month, is to make sure that, 'Are we eking the most out of the money that we are entrusted to look after and make the most out of?' That is our job; hold us to account for it.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mewn gwirionedd, nid wyf i'n anghytuno â'r pwynt canolog a gafodd ei wneud nawr, mai ein gwaith yw gwario arian yn briodol, ond eich swydd chi yw ein dal ni i gyfrif am y ffordd yr ydym ni'n gwario ein harian. [Torri ar draws.] Dyna'r hyn y cawsoch chi eich ethol i'w wneud. Fe ddeuthum i'n Brif Weinidog. Ac o ran archwiliad annibynnol o'r ffordd y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn gwario ei harian, wel, mae swyddfa archwilio genedlaethol Gymru gennym ni, sy'n gwneud hynny'n llythrennol. Fe gawn ni ein dal i gyfrif mewn gwahanol ffyrdd drwy'r broses ddemocrataidd, trwy bwyllgorau yma yn y Senedd. Ein tasg ni wrth lunio'r gyllideb nawr, ar gyfer cyhoeddi'r drafft ohoni fis nesaf, yw gwneud yn siŵr, 'A ydym ni'n gwasgu cymaint â phosibl o'r arian a roddwyd i'n gofal ni i'w warchod a gwneud y mwyaf ohono?' Dyna yw ein gwaith ni; daliwch ni i gyfrif am hynny.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Strwythur Byrddau Iechyd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: The Structure of Health Boards

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 9. Pa ystyriaeth y mae Llywodraeth Cymru wedi'i rhoi i ddiwygio strwythur byrddau iechyd? OQ64795
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 9. What consideration has the Welsh Government given to reforming the structure of health boards? OQ64795

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Restructuring isn't an immediate priority for this Government. We are instead focused on improving delivery and outcomes, and addressing barriers to more effective institutional collaboration. To do that, we are directing health boards to shift towards prevention, community care and early intervention. We're also strengthening accountability arrangements and, crucially, we're reviewing regional joint working to support better joined-up care, which is vital. This underpins our determination to ensure that health board boundaries aren't barriers to better delivery of health and care.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Nid yw ailstrwythuro yn flaenoriaeth uniongyrchol i'r Llywodraeth hon. Yn hytrach, rydym ni'n canolbwyntio ar wella cyflawni a chanlyniadau, a mynd i'r afael â rhwystrau rhag cydweithrediad sefydliadol sy'n fwy effeithiol. I wneud hynny, rydym ni'n cyfarwyddo'r byrddau iechyd i symud tuag at atal, gofal cymunedol ac ymyrraeth gynnar. Rydym ni'n cryfhau trefniadau atebolrwydd hefyd ac, yn hollbwysig, rydym ni'n adolygu cydweithio rhanbarthol i gefnogi gofal cydgysylltiedig gwell, sy'n hanfodol. Mae hyn yn rhoi sail i'n penderfyniad i sicrhau nad yw ffiniau'r byrddau iechyd yn rhwystrau o ran darpariaeth well o iechyd a gofal.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr iawn am yr ymateb, Brif Weinidog.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you for that response, First Minister.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: We've found on at least five occasions that you've described Betsi Cadwaladr as too large, too unwieldy and too distant from the people it serves. That was when you were the spokesperson for health for Plaid Cymru in opposition. And on 2 October this year, as Prif Weinidog, you said you were essentially in the same place as when you were a health spokesperson. You said we were in the last chance saloon with Betsi Cadwaladr, and that Wales must be ready to break up Betsi, which can only mean that, in your view, it's too large. Yet in recent weeks, Plaid Cymru Members have suggested that the answer to bed closures in Powys is to merge Powys Teaching Health Board with Hywel Dda University Health Board or even with Betsi Cadwaladr. That idea was nowhere in your manifesto, so I'm seeking to put on record that this is not something that Plaid Cymru are intending to do. Diolch yn fawr iawn.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rydym ni wedi canfod i chi, ar bum achlysur o leiaf, ddisgrifio Betsi Cadwaladr fel bwrdd sy'n rhy fawr, sy'n rhy anhydrin ac sy'n rhy bell oddi wrth y bobl y mae'n rhoi gwasanaethu iddyn nhw. Pan oeddech chi'n llefarydd iechyd Plaid Cymru yn yr wrthblaid yr oedd hynny. Ac ar 2 Hydref eleni, yn Brif Weinidog, fe wnaethoch chi ddweud mai yn yr un fan yr oeddech chi â phan oeddech chi'n llefarydd dros iechyd. Roeddech chi'n dweud mai dyma'r cyfle olaf un o ran Betsi Cadwaladr, a bod rhaid i Gymru fod yn barod i ddatgymalu Betsi, ac ni all hynny ddim ond golygu bod y bwrdd yn rhy fawr, yn eich barn chi. Ond yn ystod yr wythnosau diwethaf, mae Aelodau Plaid Cymru wedi awgrymu mai'r ateb i gau gwelyau ym Mhowys yw uno Bwrdd Iechyd Addysgu Powys gyda Bwrdd Iechyd Prifysgol Hywel Dda neu gyda Betsi Cadwaladr, hyd yn oed. Nid oedd y syniad hwnnw i'w weld yn unman yn eich maniffesto chi, ac felly rwy'n ceisio rhoi ar gofnod nad yw hyn yn rhywbeth y mae Plaid Cymru yn bwriadu ei wneud. Diolch yn fawr iawn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
As I said, there are no plans for restructuring. I will refer to what I have already said. Are we looking for better partnerships? Yes. Does that mean better partnerships between health boards? Yes. Do we look for a neighbouring health board where there's capacity to do something to step in and take the pressure off another? Yes. Innovations of that kind are very, very important. Do I stand by my comment over the years as—? I declare my interest as a patient of Betsi Cadwaladr. Do I have a sense that here we have a health board whose scale is an issue that you don't get elsewhere? Yes, I think that that is true, but the answer is to see if we can work around that.

Now, I have used the words 'last chance saloon', 'they are on notice'. Call it what you like, we have to give it a go. We did not come into Government saying, 'We're going to restructure the health boards.' What we did say we would do is deliver a more sustainable NHS service and care service for the people of Wales. If it means getting to grips with the organisation and shapes of boards in the future, we'll look at that. But let's crack on with the work that we have begun as a Government now. I believe it will reap results.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Fel dywedais i, nid oes unrhyw gynlluniau ar gyfer ailstrwythuro. Fe wnaf i gyfeirio at yr hyn a ddywedais i eisoes. A ydym ni'n chwilio am bartneriaethau gwell? Ydym. A yw hynny'n golygu partneriaethau gwell rhwng byrddau iechyd? Ydy. A ydym ni'n chwilio am fwrdd iechyd cyfagos lle ceir gallu i gyflawni rhywbeth ar gyfer dod i'r adwy a thynnu'r pwysau oddi ar un arall? Ydym. Mae newid pethau fel hyn yn bwysig iawn, iawn. A wyf i'n sefyll dros y sylw a wnes i dros y blynyddoedd yn—? Rwy'n datgan buddiant am fy mod yn un o gleifion Betsi Cadwaladr. A yw'r ymdeimlad gennyf i fod bwrdd iechyd gennym ni y mae ei faint yn fater nad ydych chi'n ei weld mewn ardaloedd eraill? Ydy, rwy'n credu bod hynny'n wir, ond y datrysiad yw edrych i weld a allwn ni weithio o gwmpas hynny.

Nawr, fe wnes i ddefnyddio'r geiriau 'cyfle olaf un', 'maen nhw ar rybudd'. Beth bynnag yr hoffech chi alw hynny, mae'n rhaid i ni roi cynnig arni. Ni ddaethom ni i'r Llywodraeth gan ddweud, 'Rydym ni am ailstrwythuro'r byrddau iechyd.' Yr hyn y gwnaethon ni ei ddweud y byddwn ni'n ei wneud yw darparu gwasanaeth a gwasanaeth gofal GIG sy'n fwy cynaliadwy er mwyn pobl Cymru. Os yw hynny'n golygu mynd i'r afael â threfniadau a ffurf byrddau yn y dyfodol, fe wnawn ni edrych ar hynny. Ond gadewch i ni ddechrau gyda'r gwaith y gwnaethom ni ei ddechrau yn y Llywodraeth nawr. Rwy'n credu y bydd hyn yn medi canlyniadau.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Cartrefi Cymdeithasol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Social Homes

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 10. A wnaiff y Prif Weinidog roi'r wybodaeth ddiweddaraf am gynllun y Llywodraeth i ddarparu 20,000 o gartrefi cymdeithasol newydd erbyn 2030? OQ64783
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 10. Will the First Minister provide an update on the Government's plan to deliver 20,000 new social homes by 2030? OQ64783

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Yes. Delivering 20,000 additional social homes by 2030 is a clear priority for this Government. Some £474 million is allocated for social housing this year. Local authorities across the Clwyd constituency have been allocated almost £100 million in social housing grants funding this year, and this new Government's supplementary budget has put forward plans for an additional £20 million nationally, which I hope will attract support. Together, this will contribute to the delivery of almost 1,300 social homes in Clwyd.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Gwnaf. Mae darparu 20,000 o gartrefi cymdeithasol ychwanegol erbyn 2030 yn flaenoriaeth bendant i'r Llywodraeth hon. Cafodd tua £474 miliwn ei ddyrannu ar gyfer tai cymdeithasol eleni. Mae'r awdurdodau lleol ar draws etholaeth Clwyd wedi cael bron i £100 miliwn o gyllid grantiau ar gyfer tai cymdeithasol eleni, ac mae cyllideb atodol y Llywodraeth newydd hon wedi cyflwyno cynlluniau ar gyfer £20 miliwn ychwanegol yn genedlaethol, ac rwy'n gobeithio y bydd hynny'n ennyn cefnogaeth. Gyda'i gilydd, fe fydd hyn yn cyfrannu at gyflawni bron i 1,300 o gartrefi cymdeithasol yng Nghlwyd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch. It was really, really good to hear you speak about Clwyd then, which is the constituency that I represent and where I have used available data to calculate that there are approximately 4,000 households on waiting lists for social homes there alone. So, it's evidently clear that we've got a severe lack of affordable housing here in Wales, and the plans to build 20,000 new social homes by 2030 is amazing and really welcome. However, it's really important to note that housing need varies widely by community, and even within communities, both in terms of volume and the type needed. Could the First Minister confirm that assessments of current housing stocks and needs across the different communities will be undertaken, and give assurances that those developments are to be aligned with the specific community needs?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch. Roedd hi'n braf tu hwnt eich clywed chi'n siarad am Glwyd nawr, sef yr etholaeth yr wyf i'n ei chynrychioli ac o'r lle rwyf i wedi defnyddio'r data sydd ar gael i gyfrifo bod tua 4,000 o aelwydydd ar restrau aros am gartrefi cymdeithasol yn y fan honno'n unig. Felly, mae hi'n amlwg bod diffyg difrifol o dai fforddiadwy gennym ni yma yng Nghymru, ac mae'r cynlluniau i adeiladu 20,000 o gartrefi cymdeithasol newydd erbyn 2030 yn anhygoel ac i'w groesawu yn wirioneddol. Er hynny, mae hi'n bwysig iawn nodi bod yr angen am dai yn amrywio yn fawr rhwng cymunedau a'i gilydd, ac yn amrywio hyd yn oed mewn cymunedau, o ran y symiau a'r mathau sydd eu hangen. A wnaiff y Prif Weinidog gadarnhau y bydd asesiadau yn cael eu cynnal o stociau tai ac anghenion presennol ar draws y gwahanol gymunedau, a rhoi sicrwydd y bydd y datblygiadau hynny'n cyd-fynd ag anghenion arbennig cymuned?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I certainly recognise the demand for additional social housing, which is why, over the summer this year, we published a new version of the local housing market assessments tool and guidance. These are vital tools in understanding the local housing needs of the diverse communities within each local authority area, and they help ensure that local authorities bring forward developments that are aligned with those specific community needs. I believe that the record investment that we want to put in place demonstrates our commitment. I'll also make the point that it's not just building new homes either, and we will take an approach in a number of different ways in bringing property back into use, and so on, to address what is a problem that affects all parts of Wales and one that Government is equipped to deal with.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Yn sicr, rwy'n cydnabod y galw am dai cymdeithasol ychwanegol, a dyna pam, dros yr haf eleni, fe wnaethom ni gyhoeddi fersiwn newydd o'r offeryn a'r canllawiau i asesu'r farchnad tai leol. Mae'r rhain yn offerynnau hanfodol i ddeall anghenion tai lleol y cymunedau amrywiol ym mhob ardal mewn awdurdod lleol, ac maen nhw'n helpu i sicrhau bod yr awdurdodau lleol yn cyflwyno datblygiadau sy'n cyd-fynd â'r anghenion cymunedol neilltuol hynny. Rwy'n credu bod y buddsoddiad digynsail yr ydym ni eisiau ei roi ar waith yn dangos pa mor ymrwymedig ydym ni. Rwyf i am wneud y pwynt hefyd nad adeiladu cartrefi newydd yn unig ydyw hyn chwaith, ac fe fyddwn yn mabwysiadu dulliau mewn nifer o wahanol ffyrdd fel ailddefnyddio tai gwag, ac ati, i fynd i'r afael â'r broblem hon sy'n effeithio ar bob cwr o Gymru ac sy'n un y mae'r Llywodraeth wedi ei harfogi ar gyfer ymdrin â hi.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Yn olaf, Brif Weinidog, cwestiwn 11, Gareth Thomas.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Finally, First Minister, question 11, Gareth Thomas.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Cyn-filwyr
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Veterans

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 11. Sut mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn cefnogi iechyd meddwl cyn-filwyr yng Nghymru sy'n wynebu ymchwiliad neu erlyniad mewn perthynas â'u gwasanaeth yng Ngogledd Iwerddon? OQ64774
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 11. How is the Welsh Government supporting the mental health of veterans in Wales who face investigation or prosecution relating to their service in Northern Ireland? OQ64774

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: No veteran should feel unsupported when facing significant personal challenges. We're committed to ensuring that veterans in Wales can access the mental health support they need. Veterans are entitled to priority access to NHS care, subject to clinical need, for service-related conditions. They can also access specialist support through Veterans' NHS Wales and the NHS '111 press 2' mental health service, which provides free confidential support 24 hours a day.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Ni ddylai unrhyw gyn-filwr deimlo nad oes cefnogaeth ganddo wrth iddo wynebu heriau personol sylweddol. Rydym ni wedi ymrwymo i sicrhau y bydd cyn-filwyr yng Nghymru yn gallu cael gafael ar y cymorth iechyd meddwl y mae ei angen arnyn nhw. Mae gan gyn-filwyr hawl i fod â blaenoriaeth wrth gael gofal gan y GIG, yn amodol ar anghenion clinigol, ar gyfer cyflyrau sy'n gysylltiedig â gwasanaeth milwrol. Fe allan nhw gael mynediad at gymorth arbenigol hefyd drwy gyfrwng GIG Cymru i Gyn-filwyr a gwasanaeth iechyd meddwl '111, Pwyso 2' y GIG, sy'n darparu cymorth cyfrinachol yn rhad ac am ddim 24 awr y dydd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: First Minister, soldiers from Wales answered their country's call in Northern Ireland. Some never came home, and this Remembrance Day we will rightly honour their memory. Those deployed as part of Operation Banner witnessed violence, experienced loss and lived under constant threat. For some reason, the scars, both physical and mental, have lasted a lifetime. Today, veterans face investigation or prosecution for events that did or did not take place decades ago. They are asked to account for a split-second decision when memories have faded, records have been lost and fellow soldiers, who could speak to them, have passed away. They've lived with years of uncertainty, questioning and public scrutiny. Those who served this country deserve to know that they will not face this ordeal alone. Yet Veterans' NHS Wales receives only £8 per veteran. Will the Welsh Government review the funding of Veterans' NHS Wales, so that the Welsh veterans receive the support they deserve? And will the First Minister take this opportunity to recognise the service and sacrifice of Welsh veterans who served in Northern Ireland?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Brif Weinidog, atebodd milwyr o Gymru alwad eu gwlad yng Ngogledd Iwerddon. Ni ddaeth rhai adref, ac ar Ddydd y Cofio eleni fe fyddwn ni'n eu coffáu nhw'n briodol. Roedd y rhai a osodwyd yn rhan o Operation Banner yn dystion i drais, gan brofi colledion a byw o dan fygythiad cyson. Am ryw reswm, mae'r creithiau, corfforol a meddyliol, wedi para oes. Heddiw, mae cyn-filwyr yn wynebu ymchwiliad neu erlyniad am ddigwyddiadau a ddigwyddodd ddegawdau yn ôl. Fe ofynnir iddyn nhw roi cyfrif am benderfyniad ar eiliad pan fyddo atgofion wedi pylu, cofnodion wedi cael eu colli a chyd-filwyr, a allai siarad â nhw, wedi marw. Maen nhw wedi byw gyda blynyddoedd o ansicrwydd, cwestiynau a chraffu cyhoeddus. Mae'r rhai a wasanaethodd y wlad hon yn haeddu cael gwybod na fyddan nhw'n gorfod wynebu'r profiad caled hwn ar eu pennau eu hunain. Ond dim ond £8 y mae GIG Cymru i Gyn-filwyr yn ei gael am bob cyn-filwr. A wnaiff Llywodraeth Cymru adolygu cyllid GIG Cymru i Gyn-filwyr, fel bydd cyn-filwyr Cymru yn cael y gefnogaeth y maen nhw'n ei haeddu? A wnaiff y Prif Weinidog achub ar y cyfle hwn i gydnabod gwasanaeth ac aberth cyn-filwyr Cymru a roddodd wasanaeth milwrol yng Ngogledd Iwerddon?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I recognise absolutely those who have served in the armed forces and those who lost their lives in combat, of course. We are fully committed as a Government to the covenant, which we owe to those who have served in the armed forces. It is important for us to know, when we offer services to veterans, that those services are sustainable. That is part of building the sustainable NHS that I mentioned. On those mental pressures, if you like, that veterans face, as I say, there are those priority services. We have a continued focus on rolling out veteran-friendly GP accreditation, which I think is important. I will remind you also that the programme for government that we have commits to an open access, 'no wrong door' approach to mental health, and veterans very much are able to access this.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n cydnabod yn llwyr y rhai sydd wedi rhoi gwasanaeth yn y lluoedd arfog a'r rhai a gollodd eu bywyd mewn brwydrau, wrth gwrs. Rydym ni'n gwbl ymrwymedig yn y Llywodraeth i'r cyfamod sy'n nodi ein dyletswydd i'r rhai a fu'n gwasanaethu yn y lluoedd arfog. Mae hi'n bwysig i ni wybod, pan fyddwn ni'n cynnig gwasanaethau i gyn-filwyr, bod y gwasanaethau hynny'n gynaliadwy. Dyna ran o her adeiladu'r GIG cynaliadwy yr oeddwn i'n sôn amdano. O ran y pwysau meddyliol hynny, os mynnwch chi, y mae cyn-filwyr yn eu hwynebu, fel dywedais i, mae yna wasanaethau blaenoriaeth ar gael yn hynny o beth. Rydym ni'n canolbwyntio yn barhaus ar gyflwyno achrediad meddygon teulu sy'n gyfeillgar i gyn-filwyr, sy'n bwysig yn fy marn i. Rwyf i am eich atgoffa chi hefyd fod y rhaglen lywodraethu sydd gennym ni'n ymrwymo i ddull mynediad agored, 'dim drws anghywir' at iechyd meddwl, ac mae cyn-filwyr yn gallu cael mynediad at hyn yn sicr iawn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Brif Weinidog.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you, First Minister.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Cwestiynau nawr i'r Cwnsler Cyffredinol. Cwestiwn 1, Catherine Cullen.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Questions now to the Counsel General. Question 1, Catherine Cullen.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Plant Mabwysiedig
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Adopted Children

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 1. Pa gyngor cyfreithiol y mae'r Cwnsler Cyffredinol wedi'i roi i Lywodraeth Cymru ynghylch hawliau cyfreithiol plant mabwysiedig i geisio cymorth arbenigol os bydd eu hanghenion yn parhau i oedolaeth? OQ64742
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 1. What legal advice has the Counsel General provided to the Welsh Government regarding the legal rights of adopted children to seek specialist support when their needs continue into adulthood? OQ64742

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I thank the Member for this question. Adopted people in Wales may request an assessment for adoption support services. Where needs continue into adulthood, they may also access wider health and social care support under the relevant statutory frameworks. We continue to work with partners to support adopted people throughout their lives.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n diolch i'r Aelod am y cwestiwn hwn. Fe all rhai a gafodd eu mabwysiadu yng Nghymru ofyn am asesiad ar gyfer gwasanaethau cymorth mabwysiadu. Pan fydd anghenion yn parhau i oedran oedolyn, fe allan nhw gael gafael ar gymorth iechyd a gofal cymdeithasol yn fwy eang hefyd yn ôl y fframweithiau statudol perthnasol. Rydym ni'n dal ati i weithio gyda phartneriaid i gefnogi plant mabwysiedig ar hyd eu hoes.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Counsel General, for many adopted young people, turning 18 does not mean their need for support disappears; in fact, it can be the point when they need it the most. Adopted young people can face complex challenges around identity, trauma, attachment and mental health, yet as they transition into adulthood, the support available to them can become fragmented, leaving them struggling to navigate adult services at the time they need it. We wouldn't expect a young person to suddenly overcome the impact of early childhood traumas just because they've reached a certain age. So, will the Counsel General clarify whether existing Welsh legislation provides sufficient protection for adopted young people into adulthood, and whether the Government is considering introducing a statutory duty to ensure continuing specialist support up until the age of 25?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Gwnsler Cyffredinol, i lawer o bobl ifanc a fabwysiadwyd, nid yw cyrraedd 18 oed yn golygu bod eu hangen am gymorth yn diflannu; mewn gwirionedd, fe all hwnnw fod yr oedran pan fydd eu hangen amdano ar ei fwyaf. Fe all pobl ifanc fabwysiedig wynebu heriau cymhleth ynglŷn â hunaniaeth, archoll, ymlyniad ac iechyd meddwl, ond wrth iddyn nhw drosglwyddo i fod yn oedolion, fe all y gefnogaeth sydd ar gael iddyn nhw fod yn fratiog, gan eu gadael nhw ag anawsterau wrth lywio trwy wasanaethau i oedolion ar yr adeg y mae angen hynny arnyn nhw. Ni fyddem ni'n disgwyl i unigolyn ifanc oresgyn effaith archoll plentyndod cynnar ar amrantiad dim ond am ei fod wedi dod i ryw oedran arbennig. Felly, a wnaiff y Cwnsler Cyffredinol egluro a yw deddfwriaeth bresennol Cymru yn cynnig amddiffyniad digonol i bobl ifanc a fabwysiadwyd wrth ddod yn oedolion, ac a yw'r Llywodraeth yn ystyried cyflwyno dyletswydd statudol i sicrhau parhad cymorth arbenigol hyd at 25 oed?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: The legislative framework recognises that the impact of adoption may well continue throughout a person's life, as the Member recognises, and it does provide mechanisms for adopted people to access certain support services beyond childhood. Local authorities may assess adopted adults for adoption support services and, where appropriate, co-ordinate this with broader assessments under the Social Services and Well-being (Wales) Act 2014. Adult adopted persons may also access support through health, well-being and social care services where they meet the relevant statutory criteria. We continue to work with local authorities, the National Adoption Service and adoption partners to support adopted people and their families across Wales. It's very much a matter for local authorities primarily to ensure that these services are available—that is a hard fact, they should be available everywhere—but also it's their duty to ensure that people know about the access to these very important services. The current framework allows adopted persons to access support through both adoption legislation and, where relevant, as I've said, the wider adult social care framework. Local authorities are able to co-ordinate assessments where individuals have complex or overlapping needs.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae'r fframwaith deddfwriaethol yn cydnabod y gall effaith mabwysiadu barhau ar hyd oes unigolyn, fel mae'r Aelod yn ei gydnabod, ac mae'r fframwaith yn darparu mecanweithiau i bobl fabwysiedig allu cael gafael ar wasanaethau cymorth arbennig wedi plentyndod. Fe all awdurdodau lleol asesu oedolion mabwysiedig ar gyfer gwasanaethau cymorth mabwysiadu a chydlynu hyn, pan fo hynny'n briodol, ag asesiadau mwy eang yn unol â Deddf Gwasanaethau Cymdeithasol a Llesiant (Cymru) 2014. Fe all oedolion mabwysiedig gael mynediad at gymorth drwy wasanaethau iechyd, llesiant a gofal cymdeithasol pan fyddan nhw'n bodloni'r meini prawf statudol perthnasol. Rydym ni'n parhau i weithio gyda'r awdurdodau lleol, y Gwasanaeth Mabwysiadu Cenedlaethol a phartneriaid mabwysiadu i gefnogi pobl fabwysiedig a'u teuluoedd nhw ledled Cymru. Mater i'r awdurdodau lleol yn bennaf yw sicrhau bod y gwasanaethau hyn ar gael—mae honno'n ffaith anodd, fe ddylen nhw fod ar gael ym mhobman—ond mae hi'n ddyletswydd arnyn nhw hefyd i sicrhau bod pobl yn gwybod am argaeledd y gwasanaethau pwysig iawn hyn. Mae'r fframwaith presennol yn caniatáu i bobl fabwysiedig gael gafael ar gymorth drwy ddeddfwriaeth fabwysiadu, a phan fo hynny'n berthnasol, fel dywedais i, y fframwaith gofal cymdeithasol i oedolion yn fwy eang. Mae'r awdurdodau lleol yn gallu cydlynu asesiadau pan fo unigolion ag anghenion cymhleth neu sy'n gorgyffwrdd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I'd like to thank the Member for raising this question and raise a similar issue. Too often, foster children leaving care are not aware of their rights. I recently hosted care-experienced campaigner Sam Gardner to give a question and answer session with Senedd Members here. Sam shared his experience of the foster system, moving between 15 different foster placements and having to research and advocate for his own rights. Sam has six asks of the Welsh Government, and one is for young people leaving care to be made aware of their legal and local entitlement in a clear and accessible way. Currently, this information is a postcode lottery, leaving some care leavers more vulnerable to homelessness or problems with unsupported mental health. What legal advice could the Counsel General give to the Welsh Government on ensuring that there is a legal obligation to make sure that care leavers are aware of their rights and the support services that they can access?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Fe hoffwn i ddiolch i'r Aelod am godi'r cwestiwn hwn a chodi mater tebyg. Yn rhy aml, nid yw plant maeth sy'n gadael gofal yn ymwybodol o'u hawliau nhw. Yn ddiweddar, fe groesawais i Sam Gardner sy'n ymgyrchydd â phrofiad o ofal ar gyfer cynnal sesiwn holi ac ateb gydag Aelodau'r Senedd yma. Fe rannodd Sam ei brofiad ef o'r system faeth, gan symud rhwng 15 lleoliad maeth gwahanol a gorfod ymchwilio ac eiriol dros ei hawliau ei hun. Mae gan Sam chwe chais i Lywodraeth Cymru, ac un yw i bobl ifanc sy'n gadael gofal gael eu gwneud yn ymwybodol o'u hawliau cyfreithiol a lleol mewn ffordd sy'n eglur a dealladwy. Ar hyn o bryd, mae'r wybodaeth hon yn golygu loteri cod post, sy'n golygu bod rhai pobl sy'n gadael gofal yn fwy agored i ddigartrefedd neu broblemau gydag iechyd meddwl heb unrhyw gefnogaeth. Pa gyngor cyfreithiol y gallai'r Cwnsler Cyffredinol ei roi i Lywodraeth Cymru o ran sicrhau bod rhwymedigaeth gyfreithiol i sicrhau bod y rhai sy'n gadael gofal yn ymwybodol o'u hawliau a'r gwasanaethau cymorth a allai fod ar gael iddyn nhw?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I thank the Member for that question. Adoption support services include advice and information, and local authorities are required to maintain arrangements to provide those services to adopted people and others affected by adoption. The statutory framework places duties on local authorities to provide information, advice and adoption support services. Those duties are intended to help adopted people understand and access the support available to them. Local authorities must appoint adoption support services advisers, whose role includes providing information about available support services and how those services may be accessed.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n diolch i'r Aelod am y cwestiwn yna. Mae gwasanaethau cymorth mabwysiadu yn cynnwys cyngor a gwybodaeth, ac mae hi'n ofynnol i'r awdurdodau lleol gynnal trefniadau i ddarparu'r gwasanaethau hynny i bobl fabwysiedig ac eraill yr effeithir arnyn nhw yn dilyn mabwysiadu. Mae'r fframwaith statudol yn dodi dyletswyddau ar yr awdurdodau lleol i ddarparu gwybodaeth, cyngor a gwasanaethau cymorth mabwysiadu. Bwriad y dyletswyddau hynny yw cynorthwyo pobl fabwysiedig i ddeall a chael gafael ar y cymorth sydd ar gael iddyn nhw. Mae'n rhaid i'r awdurdodau lleol benodi cynghorwyr gwasanaethau cymorth mabwysiadu, y mae eu swyddogaeth nhw'n cynnwys darparu gwybodaeth am y gwasanaethau cymorth sydd ar gael a sut y gellir mynd at y gwasanaethau hynny.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Tynnwyd cwestiwn 2 [OQ64747] yn ôl. Cwestiwn 3, Jane Dodds.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Question 2 [OQ64747] has been withdrawn. Question 3, Jane Dodds.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Gwasanaethau Cyhoeddus Datganoledig
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Devolved Public Services

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 3. Pa asesiad y mae'r Cwnsler Cyffredinol wedi'i wneud o ddigonolrwydd pwerau cyfreithiol Gweinidogion Cymru i ymyrryd mewn gwasanaethau cyhoeddus datganoledig? OQ64735
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 3. What assessment has the Counsel General made of the adequacy of Welsh Ministers’ legal powers to intervene in devolved public services? OQ64735

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: The Welsh Ministers have a range of legal powers to intervene in devolved public services, and the use of those powers would be assessed on a case-by-case basis. We are committed to working in partnership to secure effective delivery of public services.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae gan Weinidogion Cymru ystod o bwerau cyfreithiol i ymyrryd gyda'r gwasanaethau cyhoeddus a gafodd eu datganoli, ac fe fyddai'r defnydd o'r pwerau hynny'n cael ei asesu ar gyfer pob achos unigol. Rydym ni wedi ymrwymo i weithio mewn partneriaeth er mwyn sicrhau darpariaeth effeithiol o wasanaethau cyhoeddus.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr iawn am yr ymateb.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much for that repsonse.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: You very kindly responded to my questions on this issue before, but what I'm really specifically asking about is what powers the Welsh Government should have in order to intervene in health boards when there is a real challenge to the services that are being delivered. In England, the Secretary of State, since January 2024, has been able to call in NHS service changes and decide on them. In Scotland, major service changes require ministerial approval. Even in Wales, Ministers appointed commissioners to take over the South Wales Fire and Rescue Service, and can direct or challenge school closures. Yet, in Powys, families are simply being asked to accept community beds closing and care moving further from home, and the Government says it cannot weigh in and look at the merits of this decision. Cwnsler Cyffredinol, what advice would you give the Welsh Government on how Wales can gain those powers—the powers that England and Scotland have? Diolch yn fawr iawn.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Fe wnaethoch chi ymateb yn garedig iawn i'm cwestiynau i ar y mater hwn yn flaenorol, ond yr hyn yr wyf i'n holi ynglŷn ag ef yn benodol iawn yw pa bwerau y dylai Llywodraeth Cymru fod yn eu cael i ymyrryd mewn byrddau iechyd pan fo her wirioneddol i'r gwasanaethau sy'n cael eu darparu. Yn Lloegr, mae'r Ysgrifennydd Gwladol, ers mis Ionawr 2024, wedi gallu galw am newidiadau i wasanaethau'r GIG a phenderfynu arnyn nhw. Yn yr Alban, mae angen cymeradwyaeth weinidogol pan fydd newidiadau mawr i wasanaeth. Hyd yn oed yng Nghymru, mae Gweinidogion wedi penodi comisiynwyr i gymryd yr awenau gyda Gwasanaeth Tân ac Achub De Cymru, ac fe allan nhw gyfarwyddo neu herio cau ysgolion. Eto, ym Mhowys, fe ofynnir i deuluoedd dderbyn cau gwelyau cymunedol a gofal yn cael ei symud ymhellach o gartref, ac mae'r Llywodraeth yn dweud na all hi fynd ati ac ystyried rhinweddau'r penderfyniad hwn. Gwnsler Cyffredinol, pa gyngor a fyddech chi'n ei roi i Lywodraeth Cymru o ran sut y gall Cymru fod â'r pwerau hynny—pwerau sydd gan Loegr a'r Alban? Diolch yn fawr iawn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: The law is quite clearly stated, as I mentioned before. I'm not being critical of the Member for raising it again. Clearly, there is a perceived problem, according to her, in Powys. But it is really for the local health boards. They are responsible for planning and delivering services for their local populations, including decisions about how services are configured. The Welsh Ministers expect health boards to make these decisions on the basis of evidence, and with proper regard to quality, safety and patient experience. Welsh Ministers do have powers to provide oversight and, where appropriate, intervene in the exercise of health board functions. But whether intervention is appropriate will depend on the particular circumstances, including any concerns about patient safety, governance, statutory compliance and the decision-making process. Those are the criteria. They're hard and fast, and that is the current law.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Fe nodir y gyfraith yn eglur iawn, fel roeddwn i'n dweud o'r blaen. Nid wyf i'n feirniadol o'r Aelod am godi hyn unwaith eto. Yn amlwg, mae yna broblem ganfyddedig, chwedl hi, ym Mhowys. Ond mater yw hwnnw i'r byrddau iechyd lleol, mewn gwirionedd. Y nhw sy'n gyfrifol am gynllunio a darparu gwasanaethau i'w poblogaethau lleol, gan gynnwys penderfyniadau ynghylch sut caiff gwasanaethau eu cyflunio. Mae Gweinidogion Cymru yn disgwyl i fyrddau iechyd wneud y penderfyniadau hyn ar sail tystiolaeth, a rhoi sylw priodol i ansawdd, diogelwch a phrofiad cleifion. Mae gan Weinidogion Cymru bwerau i ddarparu goruchwyliaeth, a lle bo hynny'n briodol, i ymyrryd yn ymarferiad swyddogaethau'r bwrdd iechyd. Ond fe fydd priodoledd unrhyw ymyrraeth yn dibynnu ar yr amgylchiadau penodol, gan gynnwys unrhyw bryderon ynglŷn â diogelwch cleifion, llywodraethu, cydymffurfiaeth statudol a'r broses o wneud penderfyniadau. Y rhain yw'r meini prawf. Maen nhw'n bendant iawn, a honno yw'r gyfraith bresennol.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Like so many residents across Powys, I'm very concerned regarding the current health board proposals. But unlike other Members, I am more focused on ensuring residents respond to the consultation process than scoring political points. The day-to-day running of healthcare services is the legal responsibility of health boards. Does the Counsel General therefore agree with me that Ministers intervening in this work is legally unviable, inappropriate at a time when the consultation process is ongoing, and risks undermining the authority of the clinicians and healthcare experts who are entrusted to design these services?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Fel llawer iawn o'r trigolion ledled Powys, rwy'n bryderus iawn ynglŷn â chynigion cyfredol y bwrdd iechyd. Ond yn wahanol i Aelodau eraill, rwy'n canolbwyntio mwy ar sicrhau bod trigolion yn ymateb i'r broses ymgynghori yn hytrach nag ar sgorio pwyntiau gwleidyddol. Cyfrifoldeb cyfreithiol y byrddau iechyd yw rhedeg gwasanaethau gofal iechyd o ddydd i ddydd. Felly, a yw'r Cwnsler Cyffredinol yn cytuno â mi ei bod hi'n annichonadwy yn gyfreithiol i Weinidogion ymyrryd yn y gwaith hwn, yn amhriodol ar adeg pan fo'r broses ymgynghori yn mynd rhagddi, ac yn peryglu tanseilio awdurdod y clinigwyr a'r arbenigwyr gofal iechyd sy'n gyfrifol am ddylunio'r gwasanaethau hyn?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: As I said just now, the Welsh Ministers' powers to provide oversight and, where appropriate, to intervene are very strictly delineated. They are intended to deal with issues such as governance, performance, patient safety or compliance with statutory duties. They do not ordinarily place Ministers in the role of determining the merits of local service change proposals. Responsibility for developing service change proposals, consulting affected communities, considering representations and reaching a decision rests with the relevant health board. Consulting on service proposals and reaching those decisions is exactly what the health board is there to do. Ministers would not ordinarily seek to pre-empt or to direct the outcome of a live consultation or decision-making process.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Fel dywedais i nawr, mae pwerau Gweinidogion Cymru o ran goruchwyliaeth ac ymyrryd, pan fo hynny'n briodol, wedi eu nodi yn bendant iawn. Eu bwriad yw ymdrin â materion fel llywodraethu, perfformiad, diogelwch cleifion neu gydymffurfio â dyletswyddau statudol. Nid ydyn nhw'n rhoi'r swyddogaeth i Weinidogion o benderfynu ar rinweddau cynigion i newid gwasanaethau yn lleol fel arfer. Mae'r cyfrifoldeb am ddatblygu cynigion newid i wasanaeth, ymgynghori â'r cymunedau yr effeithir arnynt, ystyried sylwadau a dod i benderfyniad yn aros gyda'r bwrdd iechyd perthnasol. Ymgynghori ar gynigion gwasanaeth a chyrraedd y penderfyniadau hynny yw'r union bethau mae'r bwrdd iechyd yno i'w cyflawni. Ni fyddai gweinidogion fel arfer yn ceisio achub y blaen neu gyfarwyddo canlyniad ymgynghoriad byw neu broses o wneud penderfyniadau.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: It's probably no surprise, but as a Member with Powys in my constituency, I'm going to be asking the same kinds of questions. Counsel General, when a health board proposes cutting hospital beds in rural communities, despite serious concerns from patients, families and local representatives, surely Welsh Ministers should have the power to step in and stop it. That's exactly what we're seeing here with Powys Teaching Health Board at the moment and their proposals affecting hospitals in Ystradgynlais and Llandrindod Wells. These decisions can have devastating consequences for communities that already struggle to access healthcare. If Ministers don't have sufficient powers to intervene, isn't it time they were given them? This Welsh Government cannot keep ducking and diving and telling people that health boards make these decisions independently while expecting the public to hold you to account for the NHS. Surely accountability must come with the power to act.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae'n debyg nad yw hi'n syndod, ond a minnau'n Aelod sy'n cynnwys Powys yn fy etholaeth i, fy mod innau am ofyn cwestiynau o'r un math. Gwnsler Cyffredinol, pan fydd bwrdd iechyd yn cynnig lleihau niferoedd y gwelyau ysbyty mewn cymunedau gwledig, er gwaethaf pryderon difrifol gan gleifion, teuluoedd a chynrychiolwyr lleol, yn sicr fe ddylai Gweinidogion Cymru fod â phwerau i gamu i mewn ac atal hynny. Dyna'r union beth a welwn ni yma ar hyn o bryd gyda Bwrdd Iechyd Addysgu Powys a'i gynigion sy'n effeithio ar ysbytai yn Ystradgynlais a Llandrindod. Fe all y penderfyniadau hyn fod â chanlyniadau dinistriol i gymunedau sydd eisoes yn cael anhawster wrth geisio gofal iechyd. Os nad oes gan Weinidogion ddigon o bwerau i ymyrryd yn hynny, onid ydyw hi'n hen bryd iddyn nhw gael y rhain? Ni all Llywodraeth Cymru ddal i ddweud wrth bobl mai'r byrddau iechyd sy'n gwneud y penderfyniadau hyn yn annibynnol gan ddisgwyl i'r cyhoedd eich dal i gyfrif am y GIG. Yn sicr, mae'n rhaid i atebolrwydd ddod gyda'r pŵer i weithredu.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I can but, again, relate the law. The law is there, it is clear: Welsh Ministers cannot intervene except in those specific examples that I've already referred to twice this afternoon. I understand the Member's concern—of course I do. There is always concern when there is talk of reconfiguration. That is always the case. What is vitally important is that the consultation is allowed to take its course. People should respond in their thousands to the consultation if they feel strongly about it. People from all walks of life have a right to be consulted and they should make their views known. At the conclusion of the consultation process, some decisions will be arrived at. At that time, there will be consideration of whether the consultation was full and fair, as expected, and within the usual guidelines. More than that, I really cannot say. As for the need for changing the law, with regret, I cannot answer that—that would be speculation outside the purview of my office.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Ni allaf ond dweud beth yw'r gyfraith unwaith eto. Mae'r gyfraith yno, mae hi'n bendant: ni all Gweinidogion Cymru ymyrryd oni bai am yr enghreifftiau penodol hynny yr wyf i wedi cyfeirio atyn nhw ddwywaith yn barod y prynhawn yma. Rwy'n deall pryder yr Aelod—wrth gwrs felly. Mae yna bryder bob amser pan fydd yna sôn am gyflunio gwasanaethau o'r newydd. Mae hynny'n wir bob amser. Yr hyn sy'n hanfodol bwysig yw bod yr ymgynghoriad yn cael llonydd i gymryd ei gwrs. Fe ddylai pobl ymateb i'r ymgynghoriad yn eu miloedd os oes barn gref ganddyn nhw amdano. Mae gan bobl o bob cefndir hawl i ymgynghori ac fe ddylen nhw wneud eu barn yn hysbys. Ar ddiwedd y broses ymgynghori, fe fydd rhai penderfyniadau yn cael eu gwneud. Ar yr adeg honno, fe fydd yna ystyriaeth a oedd yr ymgynghoriad yn llawn ac yn deg, fel y disgwyl, ac yn unol â'r canllawiau arferol. Mwy na hynny, ni allaf i ddweud mewn gwirionedd. O ran yr angen i newid y gyfraith, gyda thristwch, ni allaf ateb hynny—dyfalu am bethau sydd y tu hwnt i gylch fy swydd i fyddai hynny.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Cwestiynau Heb Rybudd gan Lefarwyr y Pleidiau
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Questions Without Notice from Party Spokespeople

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Galwaf yn awr ar lefarwyr y pleidiau i holi'r Cwnsler Cyffredinol. Llefarydd Reform UK, Adrian Mason.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I now call the party spokespeople to question the Counsel General. Reform UK spokesperson, Adrian Mason.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Lywydd. Good afternoon, Counsel General. The two-week time frame required under Standing Order 29.2 is not merely an administrative suggestion. It's in place to ensure that proper scrutiny of the relevant provisions of UK legislation can be conducted by committees. The Welsh Government's repeated failure to adhere to this time frame impedes proper scrutiny. Counsel General, in light of this, can you provide the Senedd with an update on the clear action planned to be taken by the Welsh Government to ensure that committees are able to effectively scrutinise legislation made by your Government in the interest of fair and accountable governance?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Lywydd. Prynhawn da, Gwnsler Cyffredinol. Nid awgrym gweinyddol yn unig yw'r amserlen o bythefnos sy'n ofynnol dan Reol Sefydlog 29.2. Mae honno ar waith i sicrhau bod pwyllgorau yn gallu craffu'n briodol ar ddarpariaethau perthnasol deddfwriaeth y DU. Mae methiant parhaus Llywodraeth Cymru i gadw at yr amserlen hon yn atal craffu priodol. Gwnsler Cyffredinol, yng ngoleuni hyn, a wnewch chi roi'r wybodaeth ddiweddaraf i'r Senedd am y camau eglur y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn bwriadu eu cymryd i sicrhau bod pwyllgorau yn gallu craffu yn effeithiol ar ddeddfwriaeth a wnaeth eich Llywodraeth chi ar gyfer llywodraethu teg ac atebol?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I share the Member's concern. I have been before a scrutiny committee when I heard very clearly this concern. The point is not lightly made; it's a good point, and I hear what he says. The problems of late have probably been because of the King's Speech. A bundle of 16 or 17 different Bills were proposed, many of which affected Wales. There has been a bit of a backlog. It's not a sufficient answer that I'm giving you. We must improve, because if we stymie the work that these committees do, then the whole process in this place will grind to a halt. Now, I fully hear what he says. We are taking active steps to improve the situation. It has not been good over the past couple of months—that, I fully accept. I don't make any excuses, but part of the reason was the election coming so soon, in conjunction with the King's Speech, and that is a big part of the problem. But things are now improving, they will improve, and we have our eye on this matter, because otherwise, as I've said, it will be damaging to the processes within this Senedd.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwyf innau'n bryderus fel yr Aelod. Rwyf i wedi bod gerbron pwyllgor craffu pan glywais i fynegiant pendant iawn o'r pryder hwn. Ni chafodd y pwynt hwn ei wneud yn ysgafn; mae'n bwynt da, ac rwy'n clywed yr hyn y mae ef yn ei ddweud. Mae hi'n debyg bod problemau diweddar o achos Araith y Brenin. Fe gynigiwyd bwndel o 16 neu 17 o wahanol Filiau, llawer ohonyn nhw'n effeithio ar Gymru. Mae yna ôl-groniad bychan wedi bod. Nid yw'r ateb yr wyf i'n ei roi i chi'n ddigonol. Mae'n rhaid i ni wella, oherwydd os byddwn ni'n rhwystro'r gwaith y mae'r pwyllgorau hyn yn ei wneud, yna fe fydd y broses yn y lle hwn yn dod i ben yn gyfan gwbl. Nawr, rwy'n clywed yr hyn y mae ef yn ei ddweud yn iawn. Rydym ni'n cymryd camau gweithredol i wella'r sefyllfa. Nid yw pethau wedi bod yn rhy dda dros y misoedd diwethaf—rwy'n derbyn hynny'n llawn. Nid wyf i'n gwneud unrhyw esgusodion, ond rhan o'r rheswm oedd bod yr etholiad wedi dod mor fuan, ar yr un pryd ag Araith y Brenin, a dyna sydd wedi achosi'r broblem i raddau helaeth. Ond mae pethau yn gwella nawr, fe fyddan nhw'n gwella, ac rydym ni'n cadw llygad ar y mater hwn, oherwydd fel arall, fel dywedais i, fe fyddai'n niweidiol i'r prosesau yn y Senedd hon.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you, Counsel General. I know you wouldn't stand there making excuses—I'm quite fully aware of that. But considering Plaid Cymru's fierce commitment to promoting and preserving the Welsh language, which has rightly received support across the Chamber, of course, it remains unclear why the Welsh language versions of statutory texts are repeatedly attracting reporting points concerning inconsistencies between the English and Welsh texts. So, going forward, Counsel General, what is the Welsh Government doing to ensure that translation of statutory texts into the Welsh language are accurate, clear and contribute positively to the accessibility of Welsh law?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch i chi, Gwnsler Cyffredinol. Rwy'n gwybod na fyddech chi'n sefyll fan acw yn gwneud esgusodion—rwy'n ymwybodol iawn o hynny. Ond o ystyried ymrwymiad ffyrnig Plaid Cymru i hyrwyddo a gwarchod y Gymraeg, sydd wedi derbyn cefnogaeth ar draws y Siambr, wrth gwrs, mae hi'n parhau i fod yn aneglur pam y mae'r fersiynau Cymraeg o destunau statudol yn denu sylwadau adrodd dro ar ôl tro ynglŷn ag anghysonderau rhwng y testunau Cymraeg a Saesneg. Felly, wrth symud ymlaen, Gwnsler Cyffredinol, beth mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn ei wneud i sicrhau bod cyfieithiadau testunau statudol i'r Gymraeg yn gywir, yn eglur ac yn cyfrannu at hygyrchedd cyfraith Cymru mewn ffordd gadarnhaol?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: There again, I regret to say that the Member is right. There have been problems on that score as well. We are redoubling our efforts now to ensure that there is, obviously, a better service provided. There have been several problems. Some of them, by the way, were nuanced. In other words, the translation may well have been correct, although translation is never as good as the original language—and that's not an excuse being put forward. Yes, there have been failings over the past year or so and we are putting them right. We are going through the various matters that need to be put right, and, looking to the future, we wish to assure the Senedd that we are really looking at this carefully and we will not be countenancing a repeat of what has happened over the last 12 months or so.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Unwaith eto, mae'n ddrwg gennyf i ddweud bod yr Aelod yn iawn. Fe fu yna broblemau yn hynny o beth hefyd. Rydym ni'n cynyddu ein hymdrechion nawr i sicrhau bod yna wasanaeth gwell yn cael ei ddarparu, yn amlwg. Fe fu sawl problem. Roedd rhai ohonyn nhw'n wahaniaethau bychain iawn, gyda llaw. Mewn geiriau eraill, efallai fod y cyfieithiad yn gywir, er nad yw cyfieithiad fyth cystal â'r iaith wreiddiol—ac nid cyflwyno esgus mo hynny. Do, fe fu yna fethiannau dros y flwyddyn ddiwethaf ac rydym ni'n eu hunioni nhw. Rydym ni'n mynd trwy'r materion amrywiol y mae angen eu cywiro, ac wrth edrych i'r dyfodol, rydym ni'n dymuno rhoi sicrwydd i'r Senedd ein bod ni'n ystyried hyn yn ofalus ac na fyddwn ni'n caniatáu ailadrodd yr hyn sydd wedi digwydd dros y 12 mis diwethaf.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I thank you again for your honesty, Counsel General. In light of the often elusive nature of inter-governmental communications between the Welsh and UK Governments, can you commit to ensuring that, where it is appropriate, the Legislation Committee is provided with a clear record of discussions, negotiations and agreements reached on draft legislation? Whilst I do recognise, Counsel General, that the Welsh Government may consider these discussions are subject to privilege, there must be some exceptions to facilitate proper scrutiny. So, basically, to ensure that draft legislation can be scrutinised, of course, it is vital that both the Legislation Committee and the wider Senedd understands the context of these negotiations. So, Counsel General, transparency is of paramount importance if we intend to collaboratively create a clear, cohesive body of Welsh law for the remainder of the seventh Senedd. Would you agree?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n diolch i chi unwaith eto am eich gonestrwydd, Gwnsler Cyffredinol. Yng ngoleuni natur cyfathrebu rhynglywodraethol, sy'n anniffiniadwy yn aml, rhwng Llywodraethau Cymru a'r DU, a wnewch chi ymrwymo i sicrhau, lle bo'n briodol, fod y Pwyllgor Deddfwriaeth yn cael cofnod clir o drafodaethau a chytundebau a gytunwyd ar ddeddfwriaeth ddrafft? Er fy mod i'n cydnabod, Gwnsler Cyffredinol, y gall Llywodraeth Cymru ystyried bod y trafodaethau hyn yn destun cyfrinachedd, mae'n rhaid bod yna rhai eithriadau ar gyfer hwyluso craffu priodol. Felly, yn y bôn, i sicrhau bod modd craffu ar ddeddfwriaeth ddrafft, wrth gwrs, mae hi'n hanfodol bod y Pwyllgor Deddfwriaeth a'r Senedd yn fwy eang yn deall cyd-destun y trafodaethau hyn. Felly, Gwnsler Cyffredinol, mae tryloywder yn hollbwysig os ydym ni'n bwriadu creu corff eglur, cydlynol o gyfraith Cymru ar gyfer gweddill y seithfed Senedd. A fyddech chi'n cytuno?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Obviously, as the Member says quite rightly, there is some privilege involved, but I would suggest that I take back what he's just said to the appropriate colleague and speak in detail with them, and hopefully, at some other point, come back with a full answer. I don't want to dismiss this in any way; it's an important point and it therefore deserves important attention.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Yn amlwg, fel mae'r Aelod yn dweud yn berffaith iawn, mae yna elfen o gyfrinachedd ynglŷn â hyn, ond fe fyddwn i'n awgrymu fy mod i'n cael mynd â'r hyn y mae ef newydd ei ddweud at y cydweithiwr priodol a siarad â manylder â hwnnw, ac rwy'n gobeithio, rywbryd eto, y gallaf i ddod yn ôl gydag ateb llawn. Nid wyf i'n dymuno diystyru hyn mewn unrhyw ffordd; mae'n bwynt pwysig ac felly mae'n haeddu sylw pwysig.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch i chi.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Llefarydd Llafur Cymru, Mike Hedges.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: The Welsh Labour spokesperson, Mike Hedges.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch. Counsel General, last month, on level 7 apprenticeships, you said,

'What I can tell him, which may cheer him up slightly, is that level 7 apprenticeships at the bar and also solicitors are uppermost in this Government's mind. We are pushing forward on them and, indeed, I shall be making a speech on them in about a fortnight's time, during the Legal Wales conference.'

What progress has been made?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch. Gwnsler Cyffredinol, y mis diwethaf, o ran prentisiaethau lefel 7, fe wnaethoch chi ddweud,

'Yr hyn y gallaf i ei ddweud wrtho, a allai ei galonogi ychydig, yw bod prentisiaethau lefel 7 wrth y bar a chyfreithwyr hefyd yn uchel iawn yn ystyriaethau'r Llywodraeth hon. Rydym ni'n gwthio ymlaen ar hynny ac, yn wir, fe fyddaf i'n rhoi araith ar hynny ymhen rhyw bythefnos, yn ystod cynhadledd Cymru'r Gyfraith.'

Pa gynnydd sydd wedi bod?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Well, a little progress; I made the speech. But it is an important matter, we are looking at it, but, of course, it comes down, at the end, to finance. There is no lack of will to do what's necessary.
