XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Finance: Taxation (Wales) Bill

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid: Bil Trethiant (Cymru)
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Finance: Taxation (Wales) Bill
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Llywydd, consultation is not a numbers game; it can often be about the detail of the consultation. It's not a surprise to me that there were few responses to this consultation that was held last year. The Bill itself, as I explained, is technical in nature. The people who will be particularly interested in this Bill are going to be those people who are representatives of taxpayers, who deal directly with the Welsh Revenue Authority on a number of the aspects that you've outlined.

The powers that are being sought in this Bill are proportionate to the issues that have raised themselves as issues, both by the Welsh Revenue Authority itself over the last nine years, and by those people representing taxpayers, where there have been inconsistencies in the system that have existed, where there are obviously grey areas and gaps in the legislation, as they are currently. The powers on access, as you've outlined, are, I believe, proportionate, but that's for committees of this Senedd now to test, and I'm sure that these will be issues that will be tested in scrutiny.

Sharing information isn't a bad thing in itself. I think, quite often, that people out there expect public authorities to be sharing information, rather than information needing to be duplicated at all times to different places where they interact with the public sector. But, as you've rightly challenged, it needs to be done in a way that is proportionate to the issues that are at stake and where data and those who hold data are accountable for that. We have tested the proposals in the Bill with the various pieces of legislation that are in place to guard on data protection, and we believe that we have struck the necessary place to provide a system that is more effective for the taxpayer in how they provide information to public authorities and enable a more effective system to be delivered.

That's the purpose of this Bill, to make sure that how we administer and operate taxes in Wales is more efficient for the taxpayers and those who collect taxes in Wales. I think that that's a good thing to aim for, and, hopefully, the scrutiny process on this Bill will enable us to, ultimately, pass a piece of legislation that improves on tax administration in Wales.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Lywydd, nid gêm rhifau yw ymgynghori; yn aml, gall fod yn ymwneud â manylion yr ymgynghoriad. Dydy e ddim yn syndod i mi nad oedd rhyw lawer o ymatebion i'r ymgynghoriad hwn a gynhaliwyd y llynedd. Mae'r Bil ei hun, fel yr esboniais i, yn dechnegol ei natur. Y bobl fydd â diddordeb arbennig yn y Bil hwn fydd y bobl hynny sy'n cynrychioli trethdalwyr, sy'n delio'n uniongyrchol ag Awdurdod Cyllid Cymru ar nifer o'r agweddau rydych wedi'u hamlinellu.

Mae'r pwerau sy'n cael eu ceisio yn y Bil hwn yn gymesur â'r materion sydd wedi codi eu hunain fel materion, gan Awdurdod Cyllid Cymru ei hun dros y naw mlynedd diwethaf, a chan y bobl hynny sy'n cynrychioli trethdalwyr, lle mae anghysondebau wedi bod yn y system sydd wedi bodoli, lle mae ardaloedd llwyd a bylchau yn amlwg yn y ddeddfwriaeth, fel y mae ar hyn o bryd. Mae'r pwerau ar fynediad, fel yr ydych wedi'u hamlinellu, yn gymesur, rwy'n credu, ond mae hynny i bwyllgorau'r Senedd hon nawr ei brofi, ac rwy'n siŵr y bydd y rhain yn faterion a fydd yn cael eu profi wrth graffu.

Dydy rhannu gwybodaeth ddim yn beth drwg ynddo'i hun. Rwy'n credu, yn eithaf aml, bod pobl allan yna yn disgwyl i awdurdodau cyhoeddus fod yn rhannu gwybodaeth, yn hytrach na bod angen dyblygu gwybodaeth bob amser i wahanol leoedd lle maen nhw'n rhyngweithio â'r sector cyhoeddus. Ond, fel rydych chi wedi herio'n iawn, mae angen iddo gael ei wneud mewn ffordd sy'n gymesur â'r materion sydd yn y fantol a lle mae data a'r rhai sy'n dal data yn atebol am hynny. Rydyn ni wedi profi'r cynigion yn y Bil gyda'r gwahanol ddarnau o ddeddfwriaeth sydd ar waith i warchod diogelu data, ac rydyn ni'n credu ein bod ni wedi taro'r lle angenrheidiol i ddarparu system sy'n fwy effeithiol i'r trethdalwr o ran sut mae'n darparu gwybodaeth i awdurdodau cyhoeddus ac i sicrhau bod system fwy effeithiol yn gallu cael ei chyflawni.

Dyna yw pwrpas y Bil hwn, i wneud yn siŵr bod y ffordd rydyn ni'n gweinyddu ac yn gweithredu trethi yng Nghymru yn fwy effeithlon i'r trethdalwyr a'r rhai sy'n casglu trethi yng Nghymru. Rwy'n credu bod hynny'n beth da i anelu ato, a, gobeithio, bydd y broses graffu ar y Bil hwn yn ein galluogi, yn y pen draw, i basio darn o ddeddfwriaeth sy'n gwella'r ffordd y mae treth yn cael ei gweinyddu yng Nghymru.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid: Bil Trethiant (Cymru)
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Finance: Taxation (Wales) Bill
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
In Government, Welsh Labour laid the foundations of Wales's devolved tax system. Our taxation policy was based on the clear principles that Welsh taxes should raise revenue to fund public services as fairly as possible; that they should be clear, stable and simple; that they should be developed through collaboration; and that they should contribute towards the goals of the Well-being of Future Generations (Wales) Act 2015. It is against these principles that Welsh Labour will hold this legislation to account as the Bill progresses.

In Government, we established the Welsh Revenue Authority and introduced land transaction tax and landfill disposals tax in 2018. Since then, as the Minister said, the Welsh Revenue Authority has collected more than £2.7 billion to support public services in Wales. Welsh Labour showed how devolved taxation can be used to deliver progressive outcomes, including driving up rates of recycling, and making the taxation system fairer for people buying homes. And in 2021, we made the promise not to raise Welsh rates of income tax, and we kept that promise. We also recognise that taxation policy needs to evolve, so we welcome the intention of this legislation, to ensure that devolved taxes in Wales can be collected fairly and efficiently.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Yn y Llywodraeth, gosododd Llafur Cymru sylfeini system dreth ddatganoledig Cymru. Roedd ein polisi trethiant yn seiliedig ar yr egwyddorion clir y dylai trethi Cymru godi refeniw i ariannu gwasanaethau cyhoeddus mor deg â phosibl; y dylen nhw fod yn glir, yn sefydlog ac yn syml; y dylen nhw gael eu datblygu trwy gydweithio; ac y dylen nhw gyfrannu tuag at nodau Deddf Llesiant Cenedlaethau'r Dyfodol (Cymru) 2015. Yn erbyn yr egwyddorion hyn y bydd Llafur Cymru yn dwyn y ddeddfwriaeth hon i gyfrif wrth i'r Bil fynd yn ei flaen.

Yn y Llywodraeth, fe wnaethon ni sefydlu Awdurdod Cyllid Cymru a chyflwyno treth trafodiadau tir a threth gwarediadau tirlenwi yn 2018. Ers hynny, fel y dywedodd y Gweinidog, mae Awdurdod Cyllid Cymru wedi casglu mwy na £2.7 biliwn i gefnogi gwasanaethau cyhoeddus yng Nghymru. Dangosodd Llafur Cymru sut y gall trethiant datganoledig gael ei ddefnyddio i gyflawni canlyniadau blaengar, gan gynnwys cynyddu cyfraddau ailgylchu, a gwneud y system drethi yn decach i bobl sy'n prynu cartrefi. Ac yn 2021, fe wnaethon ni'r addewid i beidio â chodi cyfraddau treth incwm Cymru, ac fe wnaethon ni gadw'r addewid hwnnw. Rydyn ni hefyd yn cydnabod bod angen i bolisi trethiant esblygu, felly rydyn ni'n croesawu bwriad y ddeddfwriaeth hon, i sicrhau bod trethi datganoledig yng Nghymru yn gallu cael eu casglu mewn ffordd deg ac effeithlon.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid: Bil Trethiant (Cymru)
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Finance: Taxation (Wales) Bill
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Wrth i'r Bil fynd rhagddo, bydd cyfleoedd pellach i graffu ar fanylion y Bil hwn yn fwy manwl, ond heddiw hoffwn ofyn rhai cwestiynau cychwynnol i'r Gweinidog Cabinet. Ynglŷn â rhannu gwybodaeth, mae'r Bil yn caniatáu i Awdurdod Cyllid Cymru rannu gwybodaeth gydag awdurdodau lleol i gefnogi'r gwaith o gasglu trethi. Bydd y Gweinidog Cabinet yn cytuno ynghylch pwysigrwydd sicrhau bod gan y cyhoedd hyder yn y ffordd y caiff y data ei gasglu a'i ddefnyddio. Pa sicrwydd y gall hi ei roi y bydd y wybodaeth ddim ond yn cael ei rhannu pan fo hynny yn angenrheidiol? Ac a all hi roi enghreifftiau ymarferol o sefyllfaoedd lle gall y wybodaeth honno gael ei rhannu o ganlyniad i'r ddeddfwriaeth newydd? Yna, a all hi amlinellu rhai o'r manteision ymarferol i awdurdodau lleol, a faint o refeniw ychwanegol y mae hi'n disgwyl y bydd yn cael ei gynhyrchu drwy rannu gwybodaeth yn fwy effeithiol? A pha gymorth a fydd yn cael ei ddarparu i awdurdodau lleol i'w hysbysu am y trefniadau newydd ar gyfer rhannu gwybodaeth?

Mae asesiad effaith rheoleiddiol y Llywodraeth yn dangos bod y Bil yn debygol o sicrhau manteision cadarnhaol cyffredinol o ryw £310,000. A all y Gweinidog Cabinet amlinellu mewn termau mor syml â phosibl, termau bob dydd, o ble y daw y manteision hyn, a sut y byddan nhw yn helpu i wella gwasanaethau cyhoeddus yng Nghymru?

Ac yn olaf, a yw'r Gweinidog Cabinet wedi gwneud asesiad o lefelau o osgoi trethi o fewn trefniadau trethi datganoledig Cymru? Ac wrth i system drethi Cymru barhau i ddatblygu, beth arall gall y Llywodraeth ei wneud i roi gwell gwybodaeth i'r cyhoedd am sut mae trethi datganoledig yn gweithredu o fewn Cymru? Diolch yn fawr iawn.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
As the Bill progresses, there will be further opportunities to scrutinise the details of this Bill, but I'd like to ask a few initial questions to the Cabinet Minister. With regard to sharing information, the Bill allows the Welsh Revenue Authority to share information with local authorities to support the work of collecting taxes. The Cabinet Minister will agree about the importance of ensuring that the public has confidence in the way that this data is gathered and used. What assurance can she give that this information will only be shared when that is essential? And can she give practical examples of situations where that data could be shared by as a result of this new legislation? Can she also outline some of the practical advantages to local authorities, and how much additional revenue she expects will be generated through the sharing of information more effectively? And what support will be provided to local authorities to inform them of the new arrangements for sharing information?

The Government's regulatory impact assessment demonstrates that the Bill is likely to lead to general positive impacts of around £310,000. Can the Cabinet Minister outline in as simple terms as possible, everyday terms, from where these benefits will come, and how will they help to improve public services in Wales?

And finally, has the Cabinet Minister undertaken an assessment of the levels of tax avoidance within the devolved taxation arrangements in Wales? And as the taxation system in Wales continues to develop, what else can the Government do to provide better information to the public about how devolved taxes operate in Wales? Thank you very much.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid: Bil Trethiant (Cymru)
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Finance: Taxation (Wales) Bill
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch i'r Aelod am y cwestiynau yna ac am y croeso i hwn fel y Bil cyntaf ar gyfer y Senedd yma. Mae'n ddrwg gyda fi nad yw e'n un o'r rhai mwyaf headline grabbing y gellid bod wedi ei greu, ond mae e'n dangos beth yw gwaith dydd i ddydd Llywodraeth, beth yw gwaith dydd i ddydd ariannu gwasanaethau cyhoeddus yng Nghymru, a sicrhau bod gennym ni'r gyfundrefn fwyaf effeithiol i weithredu ein trethi ni a'n casglu trethi ni, er mwyn gallu ariannu'n gwasanaethau cyhoeddus ni. Dyna yw pwrpas y Bil yma. Fe fydd y craffu manwl rŷch chi wedi sôn amdano, fydd yn dilyn nawr ar ôl y datganiad yma heddiw, yn ffordd o destio rhai o'r materion rŷch chi wedi'u codi yn eich cyfraniad fanna, a'r un mater a godwyd ynghynt hefyd, ar sut mae diogelu'r data yna fydd yn cael ei rannu rhwng awdurdodau perthnasol er mwyn sicrhau bod popeth yn cydymffurfio â'r ddeddfwriaeth sydd eisoes mewn lle i ddiogelu data, ond hefyd o ran yr hyn y byddai'r rhai sy'n rhannu eu manylion personol yn ei ddisgwyl oddi wrth awdurdodau cyhoeddus. Dwi'n credu bod yr hyn sydd yn y Bil yma, o ran sicrhau taw dim ond at ddibenion penodol iawn y gellir rhannu gwybodaeth o'r math yma, fod hynny yn diogelu'r hyn y byddai trethdalwyr yn ei ddisgwyl ohonom ni.

Wrth gwrs, un o'r enghreifftiau cynnar yna o rannu data, a phwysigrwydd gwneud hynny o ran y trethi yn ymarferol, fydd wrth gyflwyno'r levy twristiaeth, a'r bartneriaeth yna sydd rhwng Awdurdod Cyllid Cymru ac awdurdodau lleol, neu un awdurdod lleol yn benodol. Felly, bydd honno'n enghraifft o'r defnydd o rannu gwybodaeth. Mae'r rhannu gwybodaeth yma nid dim ond er mwyn hwylustod i'r awdurdodau cyhoeddus eu hunain sydd yn gweinyddu yn y cyd-destun yma, ond bydd e hefyd o fudd i'r trethdalwyr oherwydd byddan nhw wedyn ddim ond yn gorfod cyflwyno gwybodaeth mewn ffordd sy'n fwy effeithiol iddyn nhw hefyd. Felly, mae hynna'n bwysig.

Ar rai o'r cwestiynau manwl ynglŷn â'r costau sy'n deillio o rannu gwybodaeth, ac yn y blaen, byddai'n rhaid imi gyfeirio yn fanwl at y regulatory impact assessment sydd wrth fy ochr i fan hyn ar gyfer yr atebion hynny. Mae'n siŵr, wrth graffu ar yr angen i gyllido'r darn yma o ddeddfwriaeth—sydd ddim angen llawer o gyllid, hyd yn oed o sefydlu'r cyfundrefnau newydd yma—y cawn ni fwy o drafodaeth ar hynny yn y pwyllgorau.

O ran y gwaith ar sut mae'r Llywodraeth yma neu a ydy'r Llywodraeth wedi gwneud asesiad o faint o osgoi ar dalu treth sy'n digwydd yng Nghymru, dwi ddim yn ymwybodol o waith penodol rŷm ni wedi ei wneud yn ddiweddar ar hynny, a byddai'n rhaid imi edrych ymhellach yn ôl cyn fy nghyfnod i ar unrhyw waith ychwanegol.

Ond dwi'n meddwl efallai taw'r neges bwysig yn y darn yma o ddeddfwriaeth yn ei chyfanrwydd yw taw beth rŷm ni'n treial ei roi mewn lle fan hyn yw system sy'n fwy tryloyw i bawb—y rhai sy'n talu'r dreth a'r rhai sy'n casglu'r dreth—sydd yn deg i bawb, fel bod y wybodaeth yn glir ac yn gryno i bawb o beth yw'r anghenion. A phan fo'r system angen her neu ad-dalu, bod y gofynion o gwmpas hynna hefyd yn glir i bawb.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
I thank the Member for those questions and for welcoming this as the first Bill in this Senedd. I'm sorry that it isn't the most headline grabbing Bill that could have been introduced, but it does show the day-to-day work of Government, the day-to-day work of funding public services in Wales, and ensuring that we have the most efficient regime in order to collect our taxes and administer our taxes, in order to fund our public services. And that's the purpose of this Bill. The detailed scrutiny that you mentioned, which will now follow today's statement, will be a means of testing some of the issues that you have raised in your contribution, and the same issue that was raised earlier too, in terms of how we safeguard the data that will be shared between relevant authorities in order to ensure that everything complies with the legislation that is already in place in terms of data protection, but also in terms of what those sharing their personal details would expect from public authorities. I believe that what's contained within this Bill, in terms of ensuring that it's only for very specific purposes that that data can be shared, that that does safeguard what taxpayers would expect of us.

Of course, one of the early examples in terms of data sharing, and the importance of doing that in relation to taxation on a practical level, will be on the introduction of the tourism levy, and that partnership between the Welsh Revenue Authority and local authorities, or one local authority specifically in this context. So, that will be an early example of the use of information sharing. That information sharing isn't done just for the convenience of the public authorities themselves who administrate in this context, but it will also benefit the taxpayers because they will then only have to present information in a way that is more efficient for them too. So, that's important.

On some of the detailed questions on the costs emerging from information sharing, and so on, I would have to refer in detail to the regulatory impact assessment that I have by my side here in order to provide those responses. I'm sure that as we scrutinise the need to fund this Bill—which doesn't need a great deal of funding, even in establishing these new regimes—that we will have more discussion on that in committees.

In terms of the work on how this Government or whether this Government has carried out an assessment in terms of how much tax avoidance happens in Wales, I am not aware of specific work that we've done recently on that, and I would have to look further back to before I came into post for any additional work that's been done in that area.

But I think that the important message in this piece of legislation as a whole is that what we're seeking to put in place here is a system that is more transparent for everyone—those paying taxes and those collecting taxes—a system that is fair for everyone, so that the information is clear and concise for everyone in terms of the requirements. And when the system needs challenge or repayment, that the requirements of that too are clear for everyone.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid: Bil Trethiant (Cymru)
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Finance: Taxation (Wales) Bill

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid: Bil Trethiant (Cymru)
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Finance: Taxation (Wales) Bill
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you, Cabinet Minister, for advance sight of your statement here today, and for a briefing with your officials earlier today as well. Of course, it's the first piece of legislation that this new Government has laid so far in this Senedd, and I appreciate Members may not be clamouring for passionate debates on this particular Bill here today, but I think both the letter and the spirit of what is being intended is really important to understand.

In your statement a few moments ago, the words that you used were that this Bill

'delivers a package of narrowly targeted technical and administrative changes' 

to the relevant Welsh tax Acts. This seems slightly at odds with the First Minister's statements in July, when he described this Bill as continuing Wales's tax devolution journey. And I was a little surprised to hear your second sentence today say that

'this package of changes represents the next stage in Wales's tax devolution journey.'

So, I wonder if you'll be able to respond in a moment to outline how you see the spirit of this Bill. Is it, as you opened up by saying, the next stage in Wales's tax devolution journey, or is it, as you later described, a package of narrowly targeted technical and administrative changes? I think understanding the spirit of this is important to understand how you see the future of taxation and taxation Bills here in Wales.

I wanted to pick up the point that Huw Thomas mentioned in regards to some of these savings. I had the joy of reading through the RIA recently as well and noted some of the potential savings that this Bill will produce—or efficiencies, whatever word you'd like to use. But I wonder if you could respond as to your expectations as to how any savings may be used. Would it be to reinvest in similar services or similar pressure points within Government, or would you expect that saving to be used elsewhere within Government? Because, of course, delivering on value for money is an important part of your role here in the Welsh Government.

Also, Cabinet Minister, I’ll pick up a point that Cai Parry-Jones mentioned in regard to unannounced inspections. Forgive me if you responded specifically on this, but I'm not sure that I heard it. I wonder if you are able to clarify my understanding that the proposals would bring the WRA in line with powers available to HM Revenue and Customs in England around those unannounced inspections for LDT sites in Wales. Diolch yn fawr iawn.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Weinidog Cabinet, am gael gweld eich datganiad yma heddiw ymlaen llaw, ac am sesiwn friffio gyda'ch swyddogion yn gynharach heddiw hefyd. Wrth gwrs, dyma'r darn cyntaf o ddeddfwriaeth mae'r Llywodraeth newydd hon wedi'i osod hyd yma yn y Senedd hon, ac rwy'n gwerthfawrogi efallai nad yw'r Aelodau yn gweiddi am ddadleuon angerddol ar y Bil penodol hwn yma heddiw, ond rwy'n credu bod llythyren ac ysbryd yr hyn sy'n cael ei fwriadu yn bwysig iawn i'w deall.

Yn eich datganiad ychydig funudau yn ôl, y geiriau a ddefnyddiwyd gennych oedd bod y Bil hwn

'yn cyflwyno pecyn o newidiadau technegol a gweinyddol wedi'u targedu'n fanwl'

i'r Deddfau trethi Cymreig perthnasol. Mae hyn yn ymddangos ychydig yn groes i ddatganiadau'r Prif Weinidog ym mis Gorffennaf, pan ddisgrifiodd y Bil hwn fel un sy'n parhau â thaith datganoli treth Cymru. Ac roeddwn i'n synnu ychydig o glywed eich ail frawddeg heddiw yn dweud 

'y pecyn hwn o newidiadau sy'n gam ar hyd taith datganoli trethi Cymru.'

Felly, tybed a fyddwch chi'n gallu ymateb mewn eiliad i amlinellu sut rydych chi'n gweld ysbryd y Bil hwn. Ai dyma'r cam nesaf yn nhaith datganoli trethi Cymru, fel y dywedoch chi i ddechrau, neu ai pecyn o newidiadau technegol a gweinyddol wedi'u targedu'n fanwl ydyw, fel a ddisgrifiwyd gennych yn ddiweddarach? Rwy'n credu bod deall ysbryd hyn yn bwysig er mwyn deall sut rydych chi'n gweld dyfodol trethiant a Biliau trethiant yma yng Nghymru.

Roeddwn i eisiau codi'r pwynt y soniodd Huw Thomas amdano mewn perthynas â rhai o'r arbedion hyn. Fe ges i'r pleser o ddarllen trwy'r RIA yn ddiweddar hefyd a nodais rai o'r arbedion posibl y bydd y Bil hwn yn eu cynhyrchu—neu effeithlonrwydd, pa air bynnag yr hoffech chi ei ddefnyddio. Ond tybed a allech chi ymateb o ran eich disgwyliadau ynghylch sut all unrhyw arbedion gael eu defnyddio. A fydden nhw'n cael eu hailfuddsoddi mewn gwasanaethau tebyg neu bwyntiau pwysau tebyg o fewn y Llywodraeth, neu a fyddech chi'n disgwyl i'r arbedion hynny gael eu defnyddio mewn mannau eraill o fewn y Llywodraeth? Oherwydd, wrth gwrs, mae sicrhau gwerth am arian yn rhan bwysig o'ch rôl yma yn Llywodraeth Cymru.

Hefyd, Weinidog Cabinet, hoffwn godi pwynt y soniodd Cai Parry-Jones amdano o ran archwiliadau dirybudd. Maddeuwch i mi os gwnaethoch chi roi ymateb penodol ar hyn, ond dydw i ddim yn siŵr a wnes i ei glywed. Tybed a allwch chi gadarnhau'r hyn rwy'n ei ddeall sef y byddai'r cynigion yn sicrhau bod gan Awdurdod Cyllid Cymru yr un pwerau ag sydd gan Cyllid a Thollau EF yn Lloegr o ran yr archwiliadau dirybudd hynny ar gyfer safleoedd treth gwarediadau tirlenwi yng Nghymru. Diolch yn fawr iawn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid: Bil Trethiant (Cymru)
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Finance: Taxation (Wales) Bill

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid: Bil Trethiant (Cymru)
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Finance: Taxation (Wales) Bill
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you for those issues. I probably over-egged it in my second sentence in trying to seek that headline in describing this piece of legislation, because I see it primarily as a piece of legislation that reflects on what's happened over the last 10 years, as we've introduced taxation and used devolved taxes in Wales, as we've set up the operation of the Welsh Revenue Authority, and about how, over that period, there has been a recognition of where amendments need to be made in order to operate the tax system more effectively. So, it is about the operation of the current taxes that we have in place.

There will be many here who believe, as I do, that there should be further devolution of pieces of taxation powers to this Senedd, but this Bill is not about that. This Bill is about the effective administration of the taxation powers that we do hold. I hope that, whatever our different views in this Chamber would be on devolution of further taxation powers, in the effective administration of the current taxation powers that we have, we can all unite to try and create a system that is as effective as it possibly can be.

In terms of any savings and any more effective work that would release more savings into the system, my initial reaction to the question from you is to think that they are minor in significance of money that would be provided by those savings, so I suspect that, in the main, they will be part of strengthening and reinvesting in the means of effective collection of taxes.

On unannounced inspections, you are right that the powers that we are seeking in this Bill on unannounced inspections for LDT would merely bring us in line with the powers currently in place in England under HMRC, and also in Scotland, so we are merely replicating those powers.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch am y materion hynny. Fe wnes i orliwio, fwy na thebyg, yn fy ail frawddeg wrth geisio nodi'r pennawd hwnnw i ddisgrifio'r darn hwn o ddeddfwriaeth, oherwydd rwy'n ei weld yn bennaf fel darn o ddeddfwriaeth sy'n adlewyrchu'r hyn sydd wedi digwydd dros y 10 mlynedd diwethaf, wrth i ni gyflwyno trethiant a defnyddio trethi datganoledig yng Nghymru, wrth i ni roi Awdurdod Cyllid Cymru ar waith, ac am sut, dros y cyfnod hwnnw, mae cydnabyddiaeth wedi bod ynghylch ble mae angen gwneud diwygiadau er mwyn gweithredu'r system dreth yn fwy effeithiol. Felly, mae'n ymwneud â gweithredu'r trethi presennol sydd gennym ar waith.

Bydd yna lawer yma sy'n credu, fel fi, y dylai rhagor o ddarnau o bwerau trethiant gael eu datganoli i'r Senedd hon, ond dydy'r Bil hwn ddim yn ymwneud â hynny. Mae'r Bil hwn yn ymwneud â gweinyddu'r pwerau trethiant sydd gennym ni yn effeithiol. Rwy'n gobeithio, beth bynnag fyddai ein safbwyntiau gwahanol yn y Siambr hon ar ddatganoli rhagor o bwerau trethiant, yn y broses effeithiol o weinyddu'r pwerau trethiant presennol sydd gennym, y gallwn ni i gyd uno i geisio creu system sydd mor effeithiol ag y gall fod.

O ran unrhyw arbedion ac unrhyw waith mwy effeithiol a fyddai'n rhyddhau mwy o arbedion i'r system, fy ymateb cychwynnol i'r cwestiwn gennych yw meddwl eu bod nhw'n fach o ran arwyddocâd yr arian a fyddai'n cael ei ddarparu gan yr arbedion hynny, felly rwy'n amau y byddan nhw, yn bennaf, yn rhan o gryfhau ac ailfuddsoddi yn y modd y caiff trethi eu casglu'n effeithiol.

O ran archwiliadau dirybudd, rydych chi'n iawn y byddai'r pwerau rydyn ni'n eu ceisio yn y Bil hwn ar archwiliadau dirybudd ar gyfer LDT ond yn rhoi'r un pwerau i ni ag sydd ar waith ar hyn o bryd yn Lloegr o dan CThEF, a hefyd yn yr Alban, felly dim ond ailadrodd y pwerau hynny ydym.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid: Bil Trethiant (Cymru)
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Finance: Taxation (Wales) Bill
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Symudwn yn awr at gyfraniadau un funud. Yn gyntaf, Peredur Owen Griffiths.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: We now move to one-minute contributions. First of all, Peredur Owen Griffiths.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid: Bil Trethiant (Cymru)
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Finance: Taxation (Wales) Bill
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr, Lywydd. Dwi'n croesawu'r Bil yma a'r camau i foderneiddio a chryfhau'r system drethi datganoledig yng Nghymru. Fel cyn-Gadeirydd y Pwyllgor Cyllid, dwi'n ymwybodol o bwysigrwydd llywodraethu effeithiol a deddfwriaeth sydd yn ymateb i brofiad ymarferol. Felly, mae gennyf gwpl o gwestiynau. Un o'r cwestiynau yna roedd Huw wedi'i ofyn yn barod, felly dwi ddim am ailofyn hwnna, gan eich bod chi wedi'i ateb yn barod. Mae gen i ddau gwestiwn arall. Pa waith sydd wedi cael ei wneud gydag HMRC i wneud yn siŵr bod y WRA rŵan yn alinio efo systemau yn Lloegr, i wneud yn siŵr bod y systemau hynny yn alinio? Ac wedyn, yn ail, rydyn ni wedi galw ers blynyddoedd am ddatganoli pwerau i gyflwyno treth ar dir gwag—vacant land tax. A oes diweddariad ar hwn, ac a fydd y ddeddfwriaeth newydd yn hwyluso gweinyddu trethi datganoledig fel y rheini pan ddôn nhw i lawr y lein?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much, Llywydd. I welcome this Bill and the steps to modernise and strengthen the system of devolved taxes in Wales. As former Chair of the Finance Committee, I'm aware of the importance of effective governance and legislation that is responsive to practical experience. So, I do have a couple of questions. One of those has been covered by Huw, so I don't want to ask that again, because you have responded to it. But I have a couple of other questions. What work has been done with HMRC to ensure that the WRA now aligns with the systems over the border in England, to ensure that those systems are aligned? And secondly, we have been calling for several years for the devolution of powers to enable us to introduce a vacant land tax. Is there an update on this, and will the new legislation facilitate the administration of other devolved taxes such as these when they come down the line?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid: Bil Trethiant (Cymru)
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Finance: Taxation (Wales) Bill

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid: Bil Trethiant (Cymru)
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Finance: Taxation (Wales) Bill
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
O ran y gwaith gydag alinio prosesau a sicrhau bod yna weithdrefnau sy'n galluogi unrhyw groesgyffwrdd sydd ei angen rhwng HMRC ac Awdurdod Cyllid Cymru, mae'r gwaith yna yn mynd yn ei flaen lle mae angen i hynny ddigwydd. Felly, mae hwnnw'n fater sy'n rhan o waith beunyddiol Awdurdod Cyllid Cymru.

O ran y vacant land tax, y dreth ar dir gwag, fel y dywedais i wrth Sam Rowlands, dyw'r Mesur penodol yma ddim yn Fesur sy'n cael ei ragdybio neu ei gynllunio mewn unrhyw ffordd i baratoi ar gyfer trethi newydd i Gymru. Mae gwaith y Bil yma yn sefyll yn ei hawl ei hun, ac yng nghyd-destun y trethi sydd eisoes yn weithredol yng Nghymru, ac yn eu gwneud nhw yn fwy effeithiol.

O'n safbwynt ni fel Llywodraeth, yn sicr, rŷn ni'n parhau i ddisgwyl oddi wrth Lywodraeth San Steffan am y cadarnhad terfynol o ddatganoli'r dreth tir gwag, y vacant land tax. Mae'r ymrwymiad yna wedi’i roi gan Lywodraeth San Steffan, ond mae'r cadarnhad terfynol i ddatganoli hwnnw yn dal yn cael ei ddisgwyl gan y Llywodraeth. Rydym ni yn dal yn pwyso ar hynny, ac rydw i wedi gwneud hynny yn fy ymwneud i gyda'r Trysorlys yn ystod y misoedd diwethaf. Mae cyfle gyda nhw, hyd yn oed yn y gyllideb yr wythnos nesaf gan y Canghellor, i fod yn cyhoeddi penderfyniad ar hyn. Cawn weld a fydd hynny yn y gyllideb.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
In terms of the work of aligning processes and ensuring that there are systems in place that would allow any overlap required between HMRC and the WRA, that work is progressing where that needs to happen. That is an issue that is part of the day-to-day work of the WRA.

In relation to the vacant land tax, as I told Sam Rowlands, this particular Bill is not one that has been planned in any way to prepare for any new taxes for Wales. This Bill exists in its own right in the context of the taxes already in operation in Wales, and making them more effective and efficient.

In terms of our view, as a Government, we continue to await final confirmation from the Westminster Government in relation to the devolution of the vacant land tax. That commitment has been made by the Westminster Government, but the final confirmation of devolution is still being awaited. We are still pressing for that, and I've done that in my engagement with the Treasury over the past few months. They have an opportunity, even in next week's budget from the Chancellor, to announce their decision on this. We will wait and see if that is included in the budget.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid: Bil Trethiant (Cymru)
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Finance: Taxation (Wales) Bill
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Minister, thank you for your statement today. Section 4 would allow the Welsh Revenue Authority to withhold certain tax repayments while an inquiry is ongoing. Your own explanatory memorandum acknowledges that some inquiries can take months, or even years, potentially creating cash flow difficulties for taxpayers. Beyond the existing appeal right, will you commit to clear, published service standards for these inquiries, and to reporting how long repayments are being withheld, so that small businesses and taxpayers are not left facing prolonged uncertainty?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Weinidog, diolch am eich datganiad heddiw. Byddai adran 4 yn caniatáu i Awdurdod Cyllid Cymru atal rhai ad-daliadau treth tra bod ymchwiliad yn mynd rhagddo. Mae eich memorandwm esboniadol eich hun yn cydnabod bod rhai ymchwiliadau yn gallu cymryd misoedd, neu hyd yn oed flynyddoedd, gan greu anawsterau llif arian posibl i drethdalwyr. Y tu hwnt i'r hawl bresennol i apelio, a wnewch chi ymrwymo i safonau gwasanaeth clir, cyhoeddedig ar gyfer yr ymchwiliadau hyn, ac i adrodd pa mor hir y mae ad-daliadau yn cael eu hatal, fel nad yw busnesau bach a threthdalwyr yn cael eu gadael yn wynebu cyfnod hir o ansicrwydd?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid: Bil Trethiant (Cymru)
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Finance: Taxation (Wales) Bill
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: The power to withhold payment pending investigation is a power that the WRA has sought in order to enable it to withhold, if it deems that necessary, while an investigation is being conducted. On the point that you have made in terms of ensuring that there is good and effective clarity and guidance as to when and how that power to withhold will be used, I think that that's a very sensible point. I'm sure that it's one that has already been considered. I'll certainly take it away in terms of asking the right questions on your behalf in terms of how a power such as this would then be put into use.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae'r pŵer i atal taliad tra bod ymchwiliad yn mynd rhagddo yn bŵer y mae Awdurdod Cyllid Cymru wedi ceisio er mwyn ei alluogi i'w atal, os yw'n ystyried bod hynny'n angenrheidiol, tra bod ymchwiliad yn cael ei gynnal. Ar y pwynt rydych chi wedi'i wneud o ran sicrhau bod eglurder ac arweiniad da ac effeithiol ynghylch pryd a sut y bydd y pŵer hwnnw i atal yn cael ei ddefnyddio, rwy'n credu bod hwnnw'n bwynt synhwyrol iawn. Rwy'n siŵr ei fod yn un sydd eisoes wedi'i ystyried. Fe wnaf i, yn sicr, ei ystyried o ran gofyn y cwestiynau cywir ar eich rhan ynghylch sut y byddai pŵer fel hwn yn cael ei ddefnyddio wedyn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Finance: Taxation (Wales) Bill
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Ac yn olaf, Iain McIntosh.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: And finally, Iain McIntosh.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid: Bil Trethiant (Cymru)
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Finance: Taxation (Wales) Bill
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Lywydd. Cabinet Minister, your Government's own impact assessment estimates that this Bill will cost an additional £422,000 over 10 years, while claiming only £2.6 million in benefits. But much of those supposed savings are simply staff time being freed up, rather than actual money being saved for taxpayers. And when it comes to additional inspections of businesses, your assessment dismisses the disruption as negligible, without even putting a financial figure on it.

Can you tell us how much of that £2.6 million will actually translate into reduced public spending? What assessment have you made of whether those additional powers and administrative costs are genuinely necessary? Because taxpayers deserve real savings, not just theoretical efficiencies on what appears to be a spreadsheet whilst the cost of government keeps growing.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Lywydd. Weinidog Cabinet, mae asesiad effaith eich Llywodraeth eich hun yn amcangyfrif y bydd y Bil hwn yn costio £422,000 yn ychwanegol dros 10 mlynedd, gan sicrhau £2.6 miliwn yn unig mewn buddion. Ond amser staff sy'n cael ei ryddhau yw llawer o'r arbedion tybiedig hynny, yn hytrach nag arian gwirioneddol sy'n cael ei arbed i drethdalwyr. A phan ddaw hi i archwiliadau ychwanegol o fusnesau, mae'r aflonyddwch yn cael ei ddiystyru'n ddibwys yn eich asesiad, heb hyd yn oed rhoi ffigur ariannol arno.

Allwch chi ddweud wrthym faint o'r £2.6 miliwn hwnnw fydd yn arwain at lai o wariant cyhoeddus mewn gwirionedd? Pa asesiad ydych chi wedi'i wneud ynghylch a yw'r pwerau ychwanegol a'r costau gweinyddol hynny yn wirioneddol angenrheidiol? Oherwydd mae trethdalwyr yn haeddu arbedion gwirioneddol, nid effeithlonrwydd damcaniaethol yn unig ar yr hyn sy'n edrych, yn ôl pob golwg, fel taenlen tra bod cost y llywodraeth yn parhau i dyfu.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Finance: Taxation (Wales) Bill

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid: Bil Trethiant (Cymru)
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Finance: Taxation (Wales) Bill
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
This is about making the tax system that we have clearer for all concerned, so that the rights that people have in the context of a tax system are made clear, as well as the responsibilities that they have to pay tax in accordance with the law of the land.

As I explained earlier, in terms of the unannounced inspections that I think you were referring to, that is a power that's already operational in England and in Scotland under their taxation regimes on LDT, and therefore I think it's a proportionate measure that we're taking. The costs involved in this legislation are minimal, as are the benefits: £2.6 million you referred to, over 10 years; they're not significant amounts of money. The purpose of this legislation is not to raise funding for public services further than currently, but it is to make a tax system that is more rigorous and more operationally effective than it currently is.

These kinds of changes in the tax system, in the context of the UK Government, are introduced as part of the orderly rota of UK finance Bills that come every year, every budget, and these types of small changes are put into the annual UK finance Bill. In this context, we've created a Bill that has happened now, and it's the first time, in the first nine years of this Senedd's responsibility for taxation, and therefore it's a collection of various aspects of work that both the WRA and taxpayers themselves, or those people representing taxpayers, have found to be areas that need to be either strengthened, clarified or changed as a result of the practice of taxation in Wales over the past nine years.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Mae hyn yn ymwneud â gwneud y system dreth sydd gennym yn gliriach i bawb dan sylw, fel bod yr hawliau sydd gan bobl yng nghyd-destun system dreth yn cael eu gwneud yn glir, yn ogystal â'r cyfrifoldebau sydd ganddyn nhw i dalu treth yn unol â chyfraith y wlad.

Fel yr esboniais yn gynharach, o ran yr arolygiadau dirybudd roeddech chi'n cyfeirio atyn nhw, dwi'n meddwl, mae hynny'n bŵer sydd eisoes yn weithredol yn Lloegr ac yn yr Alban o dan eu cyfundrefnau trethiant ar LDT, ac felly rwy'n credu ei fod yn fesur cymesur rydyn ni'n ei gymryd. Mae'r costau sy'n gysylltiedig â'r ddeddfwriaeth hon yn fach, fel y mae'r manteision: £2.6 miliwn y gwnaethoch chi gyfeirio ato, dros 10 mlynedd; dydyn nhw ddim yn symiau sylweddol o arian. Nid codi mwy o arian ar gyfer gwasanaethau cyhoeddus nag a wneir ar hyn o bryd yw diben y ddeddfwriaeth hon, ond yn hytrach gwneud system dreth sy'n fwy trylwyr ac yn fwy gweithredol effeithiol nag y mae ar hyn o bryd.

Mae'r mathau hyn o newidiadau yn y system dreth, yng nghyd-destun Llywodraeth y DU, yn cael eu cyflwyno fel rhan o'r rota trefnus o Filiau cyllid y DU sy'n dod bob blwyddyn, pob cyllideb, ac mae'r mathau hyn o newidiadau bach yn cael eu rhoi ym Mil cyllid blynyddol y DU. Yn y cyd-destun hwn, rydyn ni wedi creu Bil sydd wedi digwydd nawr, a dyma'r tro cyntaf, yn y naw mlynedd gyntaf y mae'r Senedd hon wedi bod yn gyfrifol am drethiant, ac felly mae'n gasgliad o wahanol agweddau ar waith y mae Awdurdod Cyllid Cymru a'r trethdalwyr eu hunain, neu'r bobl hynny sy'n cynrychioli trethdalwyr, wedi canfod eu bod yn feysydd sydd naill ai angen eu cryfhau, eu hegluro neu eu newid o ganlyniad i'r arfer o drethu yng Nghymru dros y naw mlynedd diwethaf.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Finance: Taxation (Wales) Bill
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr iawn i chi, Weinidog.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much, Minister.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Item 6, a statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health, an update on the national care service programme. I call on the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health, Delyth Jewell.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Gwasanaeth Gofal Cenedlaethol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health: Update on the National Care Service Programme
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Member_job_title_English: Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Member_job_title_Welsh: Y Dirprwy Weinidog Gofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Mae gofal cymdeithasol yn helpu plant a theuluoedd trwy gyfnodau anodd, yn galluogi pobl anabl i fyw'n annibynnol, yn cefnogi pobl hŷn i aros yn y lle maen nhw'n ei alw'n gartref, ac yn helpu gofalwyr di-dâl i allu parhau i roi'r gofal amhrisiadwy maen nhw'n ei ddarparu bob dydd. Mae gofal cymdeithasol yn hanfodol i lesiant ein cenedl. Ond dyw gofal cymdeithasol, a'r bobl ymroddedig sy'n gweithio yn y sector, ddim bob amser wedi cael y gydnabyddiaeth maen nhw'n ei haeddu.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you, Dirprwy Lywydd. Social care helps children and families through difficult times, enables disabled people to live independently, supports older people to remain in the place they call home, and helps unpaid carers sustain the invaluable care they provide every day. Social care is fundamental to the well-being of our nation. Yet social care, and the dedicated people who work within it, have not always received the recognition they deserve.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Gwasanaeth Gofal Cenedlaethol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health: Update on the National Care Service Programme
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Social care is too often treated as a hidden service, appreciated only by people whose families or lives have reached a point of crisis. Only then do people come to realise the value of care work—work that keeps our society afloat, the hours dedicated by carers, both paid and unpaid, that make people’s lives better, allowing them to live full and fulfilled lives. It isn’t always easy to capture in graphs or spreadsheets, but millions of actions every day make miracles of the daily lives of people living around us. Too often, it isn’t noticed. That has to change. I'm determined that it will change. I'm pleased today to set out the next stage of our journey towards a national care service for Wales—a stronger, fairer and more consistent system of care and support, built around people and their lives.

It's vital that we do this, because demand for adult social care continues to increase at unprecedented levels, with more people seeking support and with needs becoming increasingly complicated. In July this year, local authorities recorded 20,149 social care contacts: the highest number of contacts on record, representing a 23 per cent increase on the number of contacts reported in July last year, a 67 per cent increase on the number of contacts in July of the year before that.

Yet, despite these challenges, local authorities and partners across Wales continue to support growing numbers of people. The dedication of our social care workforce is clear to us all. But this also shows why sustained change is needed if we are to meet future demand. The national care service programme is about strengthening social care, reducing unacceptable variation, supporting our workforce and improving outcomes and experiences for people and communities across Wales. Above all, it's about creating a system that works around people, rather than expecting people to work around the system.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Yn rhy aml, mae gofal cymdeithasol yn cael ei drin fel gwasanaeth cudd, sydd ond yn cael ei werthfawrogi gan bobl y mae eu teuluoedd neu eu bywydau wedi cyrraedd pwynt o argyfwng. Dim ond wedyn y mae pobl yn dod i sylweddoli gwerth gwaith gofal—gwaith sy'n cadw ein cymdeithas i fynd, yr oriau sy'n cael eu rhoi gan ofalwyr, cyflogedig a di-dâl, sy'n gwneud bywydau pobl yn well, sy'n caniatáu iddyn nhw fyw bywydau llawn a bodlon. Dydy e ddim bob amser yn hawdd ei ddangos mewn graffiau neu daenlenni, ond mae miliynau o weithredoedd bob dydd yn gwneud gwyrthiau o fywydau beunyddiol pobl sy'n byw o'n cwmpas. Yn rhy aml, dydy e ddim yn cael sylw. Mae'n rhaid i hynny newid. Rwy'n benderfynol y bydd yn newid. Rwy'n falch heddiw o nodi cam nesaf ein taith tuag at wasanaeth gofal cenedlaethol i Gymru—system gofal a chymorth gryfach, decach a mwy cyson, wedi'i hadeiladu o amgylch pobl a'u bywydau.

Mae'n hanfodol ein bod ni'n gwneud hyn, oherwydd mae'r galw am ofal cymdeithasol i oedolion yn parhau i gynyddu ar lefelau digynsail, gyda mwy o bobl yn ceisio cymorth ac anghenion yn dod yn fwyfwy cymhleth. Ym mis Gorffennaf eleni, cofnododd awdurdodau lleol 20,149 o gysylltiadau gofal cymdeithasol: y nifer uchaf o gysylltiadau ar gofnod, sy'n gynnydd o 23 y cant ar nifer y cysylltiadau a adroddwyd ym mis Gorffennaf y llynedd, cynnydd o 67 y cant ar nifer y cysylltiadau ym mis Gorffennaf y flwyddyn gynt.

Eto, er gwaethaf yr heriau hyn, mae awdurdodau lleol a phartneriaid ledled Cymru yn parhau i gefnogi nifer cynyddol o bobl. Mae ymroddiad ein gweithlu gofal cymdeithasol yn glir i ni i gyd. Ond mae hyn hefyd yn dangos pam mae angen newid parhaus os ydym am gwrdd â'r galw yn y dyfodol. Mae'r rhaglen gwasanaeth gofal cenedlaethol yn ymwneud â chryfhau gofal cymdeithasol, lleihau amrywiadau annerbyniol, cefnogi ein gweithlu a gwella canlyniadau a phrofiadau i bobl a chymunedau ledled Cymru. Yn anad dim, mae'n ymwneud â chreu system sy'n gweithio o amgylch pobl, yn hytrach na disgwyl i bobl weithio o amgylch y system.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Gwasanaeth Gofal Cenedlaethol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health: Update on the National Care Service Programme

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Gwasanaeth Gofal Cenedlaethol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health: Update on the National Care Service Programme
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Ddirprwy Lywydd, gall y Llywodraeth ddim gwneud hyn ar ei phen ei hun. Heddiw, rŷn ni'n cyhoeddi camau sy'n esbonio ein huchelgais, y camau rŷn ni'n bwriadu eu cymryd yn ystod tymor y Senedd hon a beth gall hyn ei olygu i bobl. Mae hyn yn nodi dechrau sgwrs genedlaethol ehangach am ddyfodol gofal cymdeithasol yng Nghymru, nid ymarfer ymgynghori unigol. Rŷn ni am i'r sgwrs honno fod yn agored, yn gynhwysol a chael ei llywio gan ystod eang o leisiau, gan gynnwys pobl â phrofiad bywyd, gofalwyr di-dâl, y gweithlu, partneriaid ar draws iechyd a llywodraeth leol, darparwyr a chynrychiolwyr gwleidyddol o bob rhan o'r Senedd. Trwy gynnal y trafodaethau hynny, dŷn ni'n gobeithio meithrin gwell dealltwriaeth o'r heriau sy'n wynebu gofal cymdeithasol a nodi meysydd lle y gallai fod uchelgais gyffredin ar gyfer dyfodol gofal a chymorth yng Nghymru.

Dylai pobl allu disgwyl cymorth o ansawdd uchel ble bynnag maen nhw'n byw yng Nghymru, tra bod gwasanaethau'n parhau i gael eu darparu'n lleol, wrth gwrs, ac yn cael eu siapio gan eu cymunedau. Mae sefydlu'r swyddfa genedlaethol gofal a chymorth o dan arweiniad y prif swyddog gofal cymdeithasol wedi rhoi llwyfan cryfach o ran arweinyddiaeth genedlaethol, gwella a chydweithio.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Dirprwy Lywydd, the Government cannot deliver this alone. Today, we are publishing information explaining our ambition, the actions we intend to take during this Senedd term and what they could mean for people. This marks the beginning of a wider national conversation about the future of social care in Wales, not a single consultation exercise. We want that conversation to be open, inclusive and informed by a broad range of voices, including people with lived experience, unpaid carers, the workforce, partners across health and local government, providers and political representatives from all parts of the Senedd. Through having these discussions, we hope to build greater understanding of the challenges facing social care and to identify areas where there may be shared ambition for the future of care and support in Wales.

People should be able to expect high-quality support wherever they live in Wales, while services remain locally delivered, of course, and shaped by their communities. The establishment of the national office for care and support, under the leadership of the chief social care officer, has created a stronger platform for national leadership, improvement and collaboration.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Gwasanaeth Gofal Cenedlaethol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health: Update on the National Care Service Programme
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Our programme is built around six key foundations. First, we will implement clear national leadership, accountability and safeguarding. We will work with partners across Wales to improve consistency, strengthen accountability and take forward our ambitions for a national conversation on shaping our social care services. 

Secondly, I turn to fair funding and reliable care. We will strengthen commissioning, improve market oversight and build the evidence needed to inform future funding policy decisions. We will work towards fairer and more consistent arrangements across Wales, helping to improve affordability and access to care and support. This will help create greater consistency, transparency and confidence in how care and support are planned, commissioned and delivered.

Thirdly, Dirprwy Lywydd, is a valued and sustainable workforce. Social care workers support thousands of people every day through their commitment, their professionalism, their compassion. Care is not always something easily caught in traditional metrics or measures, because it surpasses them all. The work of care workers is what gives people's lives meaning. They bring companionship, solace and, yes, joy, to thousands upon thousands of people. They deserve more than thanks. They deserve their work to be recognised in how they're paid, the career progression and development that's available to them, and in how they're esteemed by society. This Government is committed to strengthening recruitment and retention for social care, maintaining the real living wage as the minimum rate paid to the workforce and progressing our ambitions for fairer pay. We will also develop a national social care academy to help people enter the profession, develop their skills and progress their careers. Now, Wales is ahead of our neighbours in this work. It is something we should take pride in.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Mae ein rhaglen wedi'i hadeiladu o amgylch chwe sylfaen allweddol. Yn gyntaf, byddwn ni'n gweithredu arweinyddiaeth, atebolrwydd a diogelu cenedlaethol clir. Byddwn ni'n gweithio gyda phartneriaid ledled Cymru i wella cysondeb, cryfhau atebolrwydd a bwrw ymlaen â'n huchelgeisiau i gael sgwrs genedlaethol ar lunio ein gwasanaethau gofal cymdeithasol.

Yn ail, rwy'n troi at gyllid teg a gofal dibynadwy. Byddwn ni'n cryfhau comisiynu, yn gwella goruchwyliaeth o'r farchnad ac yn adeiladu'r dystiolaeth sydd ei hangen i lywio penderfyniadau polisi cyllido yn y dyfodol. Byddwn ni'n gweithio tuag at drefniadau tecach a mwy cyson ledled Cymru, gan helpu i wella fforddiadwyedd a mynediad at ofal a chymorth. Bydd hyn yn helpu i greu mwy o gysondeb, tryloywder a hyder yn y ffordd y mae gofal a chymorth yn cael eu cynllunio, eu comisiynu a'u darparu.

Yn drydydd, Ddirprwy Lywydd, mae gweithlu gwerthfawr a chynaliadwy. Mae gweithwyr gofal cymdeithasol yn cefnogi miloedd o bobl bob dydd trwy eu hymrwymiad, eu proffesiynoldeb, eu tosturi. Dydy gofal ddim bob amser yn rhywbeth y gellir ei ddangos yn hawdd mewn metrigau neu fesurau traddodiadol, oherwydd mae'n rhagori arnyn nhw i gyd. Gwaith gweithwyr gofal yw'r hyn sy'n rhoi ystyr i fywydau pobl. Maen nhw'n dod â chwmnïaeth, cysur ac, ie, llawenydd, i filoedd ar filoedd o bobl. Maen nhw'n haeddu mwy na diolch. Maen nhw'n haeddu bod eu gwaith yn cael ei gydnabod yn y ffordd maen nhw'n cael eu talu, y dilyniant a'r datblygiad gyrfa sydd ar gael iddyn nhw, ac yn y ffordd maen nhw'n cael eu parchu gan gymdeithas. Mae'r Llywodraeth hon wedi ymrwymo i gryfhau recriwtio a chadw ar gyfer gofal cymdeithasol, gan gynnal y cyflog byw gwirioneddol fel yr isafswm sy'n cael ei dalu i'r gweithlu a hyrwyddo ein huchelgeisiau am gyflog tecach. Byddwn ni hefyd yn datblygu academi gofal cymdeithasol genedlaethol i helpu pobl i fynd i mewn i'r proffesiwn, datblygu eu sgiliau a chamu ymlaen yn eu gyrfa. Nawr, mae Cymru ar y blaen i'n cymdogion o ran y gwaith hwn. Mae'n rhywbeth y dylem ni ymfalchïo ynddo.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Gwasanaeth Gofal Cenedlaethol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health: Update on the National Care Service Programme
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Mae dadansoddiad yn dangos bod pob £1 sy'n cael ei fuddsoddi mewn gofal cymdeithasol i oedolion yng Nghymru yn cynhyrchu tua £2.78 mewn gwerth cymdeithasol ac economaidd. 

Yn bedwerydd, Ddirprwy Lywydd, byddwn ni'n cryfhau data, technoleg ddigidol a chanlyniadau. Mae penderfyniadau da yn dibynnu ar wybodaeth sy'n dda. Os ydym am wella gwasanaethau, adnabod pwysau yn gynnar a chynllunio'n effeithiol ar gyfer y dyfodol, mae angen dealltwriaeth gryfach o brofiadau pobl a'r heriau sy'n wynebu'r system. Byddwn ni'n sefydlu hwb gwybodaeth gofal cymdeithasol o fewn y swyddfa genedlaethol, yn gwella ansawdd a chysondeb data gofal ac yn cryfhau adroddiadau cenedlaethol a goruchwyliaeth o'r farchnad. Bydd gwell deallusrwydd yn ein helpu i adnabod risg yn gynharach, targedu gweithgarwch gwella yn fwy effeithiol a darparu mwy o dryloywder ynghylch lle mae'r system yn gweithio'n dda a lle mae angen gweithredu pellach. Ochr yn ochr â hyn, byddwn ni'n parhau i gefnogi'r defnydd o ddatrysiadau digidol a thechnolegol sy'n helpu i wella canlyniadau i bobl, cefnogi'r gweithlu a galluogi darparu gofal a chymorth yn fwy effeithiol.

Yn bumed, byddwn ni'n rhoi pwyslais o'r newydd ar atal, diogelu a chymunedau cryfach. Byddwn ni'n datblygu dull cenedlaethol cryfach ar gyfer atal ac ymyrryd yn gynnar, yn bwrw ymlaen â'r strategaeth 10 mlynedd ar gyfer atal ac ymateb i gam-drin plant yn rhywiol ac yn cyhoeddi strategaeth genedlaethol newydd ar gyfer gofalwyr di-dâl. Rhaid i hynny wneud gwahaniaeth ymarferol trwy sicrhau cefnogaeth gynharach, gwell cydnabyddiaeth ar gyfer gofalwyr di-dâl a gwasanaethau cymunedol cryfach sy'n helpu pobl i gynnal eu hannibyniaeth a'u llesiant.

Ac yn olaf, mae gofal cymdeithasol a chymorth di-dor.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Analysis indicates that every £1 invested in adult social care in Wales generates approximately £2.78 in social and economic value.

Fourth, Dirprwy Lywydd, we will strengthen data, digital technology and outcomes. Good decisions depend on good information. If we are to improve services, identify pressures early and plan effectively for the future, we need a stronger understanding of people's experiences and the challenges facing the system. We will establish a social care intelligence hub within the national office, improve the quality and consistency of social care data and strengthen national reporting and market oversight. Better intelligence will help us identify risk earlier, target improvement activity more effectively and provide greater transparency about where the system is working well and where further action is needed. Alongside this, we will continue supporting the use of digital and technological solutions that help improve outcomes for people, support the workforce and enable more effective delivery of care and support.

Fifth, we will place renewed emphasis on prevention, safeguarding and stronger communities. We will develop a stronger national approach to early intervention, take forward our 10-year strategy for preventing and responding to child sexual abuse and publish a new national strategy for unpaid carers. All of this must make a practical difference through earlier support, better recognition of unpaid carers and stronger community-based services that help people maintain their independence and their well-being.

And finally, there's seamless social care and support.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health: Update on the National Care Service Programme

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Gwasanaeth Gofal Cenedlaethol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health: Update on the National Care Service Programme
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
People don't experience their lives in silos through separate organisations, budgets or professional boundaries. They should not have to navigate those boundaries to receive the right support. We will take forward the Ynghyd 2030 programme for children and families, strengthening pathways of care and continuing to improve integration between health and social care through our integrated community care system. We'll also encourage innovative models of care that support communities and improve people’s experiences of care and support.

Dirprwy Lywydd, over this Senedd term, we intend to make substantial progress across the programme. This will include taking forward Stronger Safeguarding for a Safer Wales, developing the national social care academy, strengthening commissioning and regional collaboration, improving intelligence and market oversight, enhancing support for unpaid carers, progressing fair pay ambitions and developing the evidence needed to inform future decisions. This programme will not complete our journey towards a national care service, but it sets out practical steps we can take now and provides the foundations and the evidence needed to continue that journey with confidence.

Ultimately, its success will not be measured by the structures we create or the documents we publish. It will be measured by whether people can access the right support at the right time, whether unpaid carers feel recognised and supported, whether our workforce feels valued and whether people can live independently, safely and with dignity for longer. That is our ambition: a people-centred national care service, shaped by Welsh values and built with the people and communities it exists to serve.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Dydy pobl ddim yn byw eu bywydau mewn seilos trwy gyllidebau, ffiniau proffesiynol neu sefydliadau ar wahân. Dylen nhw ddim gorfod llywio'r ffiniau hynny i gael y cymorth cywir. Byddwn ni'n bwrw ymlaen â rhaglen Ynghyd 2030 ar gyfer plant a theuluoedd, gan gryfhau llwybrau gofal a pharhau i wella integreiddio rhwng iechyd a gofal cymdeithasol drwy ein system gofal cymunedol integredig. Byddwn ni hefyd yn annog modelau gofal arloesol sy'n cefnogi cymunedau ac yn gwella profiadau pobl o ofal a chymorth.

Ddirprwy Lywydd, dros dymor y Senedd hon, rydyn ni'n bwriadu gwneud cynnydd sylweddol ar draws y rhaglen. Bydd hyn yn cynnwys bwrw ymlaen â Diogelu Cryfach ar gyfer Cymru Fwy Diogel, datblygu'r academi gofal cymdeithasol genedlaethol, cryfhau comisiynu a chydweithredu rhanbarthol, gwella gwybodaeth a goruchwyliaeth o'r farchnad, gwella cymorth i ofalwyr di-dâl, hyrwyddo uchelgeisiau cyflog teg a datblygu'r dystiolaeth sydd ei hangen i lywio penderfyniadau yn y dyfodol. Fydd y rhaglen hon ddim yn cwblhau ein taith tuag at wasanaeth gofal cenedlaethol, ond mae'n nodi'r camau ymarferol y gallwn ni eu cymryd nawr ac yn darparu'r sylfeini a'r dystiolaeth sydd eu hangen i barhau â'r daith honno yn hyderus.

Yn y pen draw, fydd ei llwyddiant ddim yn cael ei fesur yn ôl y strwythurau rydyn ni'n eu creu na'r dogfennau rydyn ni'n eu cyhoeddi. Bydd yn cael ei fesur yn ôl a all pobl gael mynediad at y cymorth cywir ar yr adeg gywir, a yw gofalwyr di-dâl yn teimlo eu bod yn cael eu cydnabod a'u cefnogi, a yw ein gweithlu yn teimlo eu bod yn cael eu gwerthfawrogi ac a all pobl fyw'n annibynnol, yn ddiogel a chydag urddas am gyfnod hwy. Dyna ein huchelgais: gwasanaeth gofal cenedlaethol sy'n canolbwyntio ar bobl, wedi'i lunio gan werthoedd Cymreig ac wedi'i adeiladu gyda'r bobl a'r cymunedau y mae'n bodoli i'w gwasanaethu.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Gwasanaeth Gofal Cenedlaethol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health: Update on the National Care Service Programme
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you, Deputy Presiding Officer. Can I thank the Minister for her statement this afternoon? As you're very well aware, I have always been against the establishment of a national care service, for reasons I won't go over again because you've heard them 100 times and they are a matter for the record.

You mentioned the people who work in social care, and I absolutely agree with you, they do deserve more than thanks. You've celebrated, along with a lot of politicians in here, that we pay social care staff the real living wage. We need to go further than that. If we want to see more social care staff in the system, they need to be paid more than the real living wage. So, I'd like to know from you, when is this Government going to put a proper pay structure in place to make sure that our social care staff are paid appropriately? One way in which we think you could do that is by integrating social care into the health system, something that I've advocated for for a long time. I'd like to hear: is that something that you and the Cabinet Minister for health are looking closely at?

Your statement also highlighted equitable and high-quality support across the country, and I think it is very important that we do have equitable care across the country, but we all know the challenges of delivering social care in rural areas, and that didn't come through in your speech. Can you explain to me and the rest of the Members in this Chamber what is the Government doing to ensure that we have good-quality social care in rural areas? We know that is an exceptionally difficult place to recruit our social care staff, so I'd like to know what the Government is doing around that.

You did mention in your statement fair funding, but one thing I didn't hear right the way through it was how much funding you're actually going to provide as well, so it would be quite useful to know, as part of the budget discussions that are going on with the Cabinet Minister for Finance, how much money you're allocating to the national care service, as the Cabinet Minister walks in through the door. [Laughter.] We're going to find out how much money you're going to give, Cabinet Minister, to the national care service, and how much you're allocating to this area of policy, because I think that's something that is very interesting to know and not something that you raised in your statement.

You also raised unpaid carers as well, and I think they are actually the unsung heroes of our care system across the country. We all know that they save our NHS, not just millions but billions of pounds, and if we actually had to start paying them for the work that they're doing looking after their loved ones, it would bankrupt the Welsh Government, and I'm pretty sure it would bankrupt the UK Government as well. So, I'm interested to know what extra support you're going to put in place for them, because you did mention, as you went through, community-based services, and I'm sure I'm not the only Member in my area that has actually seen those day-centre services being removed from local government control because they can't afford to run them anymore. So, there is a bit of joined-up thinking that needs to happen here, isn't there? If you talk about strengthening community-based services, that means our local authorities have to be funded properly to provide those services as well, because if they haven't got the money to provide them, it puts more pressure back on the people who are caring for people at home.

You also mentioned prevention, and it is important that we keep people in their homes for as long as possible, because we do know that that does take pressure off the care service. But as someone who was a local government cabinet minister in a previous life, I also know about the disabled facilities grant, which is actually always overspent in local government. And I'm just interested, from your perspective, how much money, working with the Cabinet Minister for local government, you're putting into this area, because if you are talking about prevention, you need to make sure the measures are in place in people's homes to make sure they can stay there for longer and to make sure they can actually get around their own home.

What else did you talk about? You talked about an awful lot today. You raised also the national social care academy. This is something that's actually quite an exciting piece of work—I think there is something that could be developed here—but I'd like to actually know when this academy is going to be developed, because the contract is still on Sell2Wales, and we all know how long things take to move through the sausage machine in Welsh Government, and it's probably going to take an awful long time for this to be developed. So, from yourself, I'd like to know, when do you see that national care academy coming online? Because if there's anything to go by by Government contracting, we're actually not probably going to see it for another three to four years, which I'd actually think would be a big shame, if we're trying to get more people into the profession.

And finally, about Senedd scrutiny, I think it is very important, as this piece of work goes through, that the Senedd is given more opportunity to scrutinise this. I know the Chairman of the health committee is in the Chamber here, and I'm sure this is a piece of work they will be looking into. So, I'd just like to know, will you be committed to providing regular updates to the Senedd on the development of this national care service to make sure all Members across the Chamber have got the opportunity to scrutinise you about the accountability, the funding that's going to go into it, and ultimately the delivery? Because that's the way—. I keep saying to this Government, 'Talk is cheap, but delivery is more', and you said at the start that our social care staff across the country deserve more than warm words, and they need action, and they do need it now. So, if you can answer some of my questions, I'd be very grateful. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. A gaf fi ddiolch i'r Gweinidog am ei datganiad y prynhawn yma? Fel y gwyddoch chi'n iawn, rwyf bob amser wedi bod yn erbyn sefydlu gwasanaeth gofal cenedlaethol, am resymau wnaf i ddim mynd drostyn nhw eto am eich bod chi wedi eu clywed 100 o weithiau ac maen nhw'n fater i'r cofnod.

Fe wnaethoch chi sôn am y bobl sy'n gweithio ym maes gofal cymdeithasol, ac rwy'n cytuno'n llwyr â chi, maen nhw'n haeddu mwy na diolch. Rydych chi wedi dathlu, ynghyd â llawer o wleidyddion yn y fan yma, ein bod ni'n talu'r cyflog byw gwirioneddol i staff gofal cymdeithasol. Mae angen i ni fynd ymhellach na hynny. Os ydym am weld mwy o staff gofal cymdeithasol yn y system, mae angen iddyn nhw gael eu talu mwy na'r cyflog byw gwirioneddol. Felly, hoffwn wybod gennych chi, pryd mae'r Llywodraeth hon yn mynd i roi strwythur cyflog priodol ar waith i wneud yn siŵr bod ein staff gofal cymdeithasol yn cael eu talu'n briodol? Un ffordd y gallech chi wneud hynny, yn ein barn ni, yw trwy integreiddio gofal cymdeithasol yn y system iechyd, rhywbeth rwyf wedi eirioli drosto ers amser maith. Fe hoffwn i glywed: a yw hynny'n rhywbeth rydych chi a'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros iechyd yn edrych yn fanwl arno?

Fe wnaeth eich datganiad hefyd dynnu sylw at gymorth teg ac o ansawdd uchel ledled y wlad, ac rwy'n credu ei bod yn bwysig iawn bod gennym ni ofal teg ledled y wlad, ond rydyn ni i gyd yn gwybod am yr heriau sy'n gysylltiedig â darparu gofal cymdeithasol mewn ardaloedd gwledig, a daeth hynny ddim trwodd yn eich araith. Allwch chi esbonio i mi a gweddill yr Aelodau yn y Siambr hon beth mae'r Llywodraeth yn ei wneud i sicrhau bod gennym ofal cymdeithasol o ansawdd da mewn ardaloedd gwledig? Rydyn ni'n gwybod ei fod yn lle eithriadol o anodd i recriwtio ein staff gofal cymdeithasol, felly hoffwn i wybod beth mae'r Llywodraeth yn ei wneud o ran hynny.

Fe wnaethoch chi sôn yn eich datganiad am gyllid teg, ond un peth wnes i ddim ei glywed yr holl ffordd drwyddo oedd faint o gyllid rydych chi'n mynd i'w ddarparu hefyd, felly byddai'n eithaf defnyddiol gwybod, fel rhan o'r trafodaethau ar y gyllideb sy'n digwydd gyda'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid, faint o arian rydych chi'n ei ddyrannu i'r gwasanaeth gofal cenedlaethol, wrth i'r Gweinidog Cabinet gerdded i mewn drwy'r drws. [Chwerthin.] Rydyn ni'n mynd i ddarganfod faint o arian rydych chi'n mynd i'w roi, Weinidog Cabinet, i'r gwasanaeth gofal cenedlaethol, a faint rydych chi'n ei ddyrannu i'r maes polisi hwn, oherwydd rwy'n credu bod hynny'n rhywbeth sy'n ddiddorol iawn i'w wybod a dydy e ddim yn rhywbeth y gwnaethoch chi ei godi yn eich datganiad.

Fe sonioch chi hefyd am ofalwyr di-dâl, ac rwy'n credu mai nhw, mewn gwirionedd, yw arwyr di-glod ein system gofal ledled y wlad. Rydyn ni i gyd yn gwybod eu bod nhw'n arbed, nid yn unig miliynau ond biliynau o bunnoedd i'n GIG, a phe bai'n rhaid i ni ddechrau eu talu am y gwaith maen nhw'n ei wneud yn gofalu am eu hanwyliaid, byddai Llywodraeth Cymru yn mynd i'r wal, ac rwy'n eithaf siŵr y byddai Llywodraeth y DU yn mynd i'r wal hefyd. Felly, mae gen i ddiddordeb mewn gwybod pa gymorth ychwanegol rydych chi'n mynd i'w roi ar waith ar eu cyfer, oherwydd fe wnaethoch chi sôn, wrth i chi fynd yn eich blaen, am wasanaethau cymunedol, ac rwy'n siŵr nad fi yw'r unig Aelod yn fy ardal sydd wedi gweld y gwasanaethau canolfan ddydd hynny yn cael eu cymryd oddi ar ddwylo llywodraeth leol oherwydd dydyn nhw ddim yn gallu fforddio eu rhedeg mwyach. Felly, mae angen rhywfaint o feddwl cydgysylltiedig yn y fan yma, onid oes e? Os ydych chi'n sôn am gryfhau gwasanaethau cymunedol, mae hynny'n golygu bod yn rhaid i'n hawdurdodau lleol gael eu hariannu'n briodol i ddarparu'r gwasanaethau hynny hefyd, oherwydd os nad oes ganddyn nhw'r arian i'w darparu, mae'n rhoi mwy o bwysau yn ôl ar y bobl sy'n gofalu am bobl gartref.

Fe sonioch chi hefyd am atal, ac mae'n bwysig ein bod ni'n cadw pobl yn eu cartrefi cyn hired â phosibl, oherwydd rydyn ni'n gwybod bod hynny yn tynnu pwysau oddi ar y gwasanaeth gofal. Ond fel rhywun a oedd yn weinidog cabinet llywodraeth leol mewn bywyd blaenorol, rwy'n gwybod hefyd am y grant cyfleusterau i bobl anabl, sydd wastad yn cael ei orwario mewn llywodraeth leol. Ac mae gen i ddiddordeb, o'ch persbectif chi, faint o arian, gan weithio gyda'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros lywodraeth leol, rydych chi'n ei roi i'r maes hwn, oherwydd os ydych chi'n sôn am atal, mae angen i chi wneud yn siŵr bod y mesurau ar waith yng nghartrefi pobl i wneud yn siŵr eu bod nhw'n gallu aros yno'n hirach ac i wneud yn siŵr eu bod nhw'n gallu symud o gwmpas eu cartref eu hunain.

Beth arall wnaethoch chi sôn amdano? Fe wnaethoch chi sôn am lawer o bethau heddiw. Fe sonioch chi hefyd am yr academi gofal cymdeithasol genedlaethol. Mae hwn yn rhywbeth sydd, mewn gwirionedd, yn ddarn eithaf cyffrous o waith—rwy'n credu bod yna rywbeth y gellid ei ddatblygu yma—ond hoffwn i wybod pryd y bydd yr academi hon yn cael ei datblygu, oherwydd mae'r contract yn dal i fod ar GwerthwchiGymru, ac rydyn ni i gyd yn gwybod pa mor hir y mae pethau'n ei gymryd i symud drwy'r peiriant selsig yn Llywodraeth Cymru, ac mae'n mynd i gymryd amser hir iawn i hyn gael ei datblygu, fwy na thebyg. Felly, hoffwn wybod oddi wrthych chi, pryd ydych chi'n gweld yr academi gofal genedlaethol honno yn dod yn weithredol? Oherwydd os yw proses gontractio'r Llywodraeth yn brawf o unrhyw beth, mae'n debyg nad ydym ni'n mynd i'w gweld am dair i bedair blynedd arall, ac fe fyddai hynny'n drueni mawr, yn fy marn i, os ydym ni'n ceisio cael mwy o bobl i mewn i'r proffesiwn.

Ac yn olaf, o ran craffu'r Senedd, rwy'n credu ei bod hi'n bwysig iawn, wrth i'r darn hwn o waith fynd rhagddo, bod y Senedd yn cael mwy o gyfle i graffu ar hyn. Rwy'n gwybod bod Cadeirydd y pwyllgor iechyd yma yn y Siambr, ac rwy'n siŵr bod hwn yn ddarn o waith y byddan nhw'n edrych arno. Felly, hoffwn i wybod, a fyddwch chi'n ymrwymo i ddarparu diweddariadau rheolaidd i'r Senedd ar y gwaith o ddatblygu'r gwasanaeth gofal cenedlaethol hwn er mwyn sicrhau bod yr holl Aelodau ar draws y Siambr yn cael cyfle i graffu arnoch o ran yr atebolrwydd, y cyllid sy'n mynd i fynd i mewn iddo ac, yn y pen draw, y broses gyflawni? Oherwydd dyna'r ffordd—. Rwy'n dweud o hyd wrth y Llywodraeth hon, 'mae gwneud yn well na dweud', ac fe ddywedoch chi ar y dechrau bod ein staff gofal cymdeithasol ledled y wlad yn haeddu mwy na geiriau cynnes, a bod angen gweithredu arnyn nhw, ac mae angen e arnyn nhw nawr. Felly, os gallwch chi ateb rhai o'm cwestiynau, byddwn i'n ddiolchgar iawn. Diolch.

And the individual parts here—. I would hope, from what you've said, there would be support for some of those, regardless of how they're packaged, the individual elements—
