XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Gwasanaeth Gofal Cenedlaethol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health: Update on the National Care Service Programme
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
You asked about the workforce, certainly, and I certainly agree with you that the real living wage must be the minimum that we should be paying. I think it's 84 per cent—well, the most recent figures, which obviously aren't completely up to date, suggest that 84 per cent of the workforce currently is being paid the real living wage. Obviously, there's more still to do. I think it's 60,000 social care workers, including personal assistants, that are scoped to receive the real living wage. We want to go beyond that, so we are progressing fair pay agreements for the workforce, and we've worked really closely with the UK Government to ensure that provisions in the Employment Rights Act 2025 were extended to Wales for that.

And you had mentioned that we need to make sure that social care workers are not at a disadvantage compared with their counterparts in the NHS, and I think that's something that certainly we would be looking to address through those bodies, because, often, social care workers are competing with sectors like retail and hospitality in terms of the pay that they currently get, and those professions would be far less intensive in terms of the roles, and so we need to be making sure that we are truly valuing this vital work.

You mentioned as well the need to make sure that rural areas are—. Basically, that there isn't a postcode lottery, which is, obviously, something that we would all agree with. In terms of some of the elements of what I've announced today that would help to address that concern, which I think is a really worthy concern, well, for example, the social care intelligence hub, that's going to help strengthen planning and to identify risks and pressures in different parts of Wales to see, 'Okay, so what needs to be addressed here in terms of strengthening commissioning as well?', again to spot different patterns to make sure that there is more of a truly national envelope of support that is available, because, at the moment, too many people are at the mercy of just individual decisions, which will vary hugely in different parts of the country, and we want to streamline as far as possible. I've said this before: anyone designing the social care system from scratch would not design it as we have it at the moment, but, obviously, we need to work with partners in local government, work with partners in the Association of Directors of Social Services. Everyone wants to work together to see what we can do to make this better.

You asked about unpaid carers as well, and, yes, certainly, we owe them far more than just words. We owe them a better life, because they do save government and they save society billions of pounds. We are going to be publishing the new national strategy for unpaid carers in November, which is going to be setting out a number of areas, including tying in our response to the previous Senedd's Health and Social Care Committee's report. That's going to be looking at improving carers' assessments, access to respite, support for carers to stay in paid employment, and there'll be a particular focus on young carers as well. The day centre services—it's something I've been really concerned about in the past as well. And I know, obviously, that this is a decision for individual local authorities. It is something I'm very interested in, and I've certainly heard testimony from a number of people about the effect that that can have on their lives.

You asked about prevention and the ways in which my colleague the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care and I would be working with the Cabinet Minister for local government. There are a number of grants, like the regional integration fund and other grants, that look at how we can invest in a greater way in prevention, and it's something that we are really keen to take forward.

And finally—oh, no, penultimately—on the academy, there will, certainly, and I'll be able to publish more information on this shortly, I hope, in terms of the elements of this that are going to be coming—I don't like the phrase 'coming online'—that are going to be becoming delivered then, as this progresses. It is something really exciting though, and it's something where we are leading the way. There are already lots of local academies across Wales, so lots of this already exists; we just want to bring it together into a national system, delivered locally.

And finally, yes, I am very happy to commit to regular updates on this. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Fe ofynnoch chi am y gweithlu, yn sicr, ac rwy'n sicr yn cytuno â chi mai'r cyflog byw gwirioneddol ddylai fod yr isafswm y dylem ni fod yn ei dalu. Rwy'n credu ei fod yn 84 y cant—wel, mae'r ffigurau diweddaraf, sydd ddim yn hollol gyfredol, yn amlwg, yn awgrymu bod 84 y cant o'r gweithlu yn cael y cyflog byw gwirioneddol ar hyn o bryd. Yn amlwg, mae mwy i'w wneud o hyd. Rwy'n credu mai 60,000 o weithwyr gofal cymdeithasol, gan gynnwys cynorthwywyr personol, sydd o fewn y cwmpas i gael y cyflog byw gwirioneddol. Rydyn ni eisiau mynd y tu hwnt i hynny, felly rydyn ni'n bwrw ymlaen â chytundebau cyflog teg i'r gweithlu, ac rydyn ni wedi gweithio'n agos iawn gyda Llywodraeth y DU i sicrhau bod darpariaethau yn Neddf Hawliau Cyflogaeth 2025 yn rhychwantu Gymru ar gyfer hynny.

Ac roeddech chi wedi sôn bod angen i ni wneud yn siŵr nad yw gweithwyr gofal cymdeithasol dan anfantais o gymharu â'u cymheiriaid yn y GIG, ac rwy'n credu bod hynny'n rhywbeth y bydden ni'n sicr yn edrych i fynd i'r afael ag ef trwy'r cyrff hynny, oherwydd, yn aml, mae gweithwyr gofal cymdeithasol yn cystadlu â sectorau fel manwerthu a lletygarwch o ran y cyflog maen nhw'n ei gael ar hyn o bryd, a byddai'r proffesiynau hynny'n llawer llai dwys o ran y rolau, ac felly mae angen i ni fod yn gwneud yn siŵr ein bod ni wir yn gwerthfawrogi'r gwaith hanfodol hwn.

Fe sonioch chi hefyd am yr angen i wneud yn siŵr bod ardaloedd gwledig yn—. Yn y bôn, bod yna ddim loteri cod post, sydd, yn amlwg, yn rhywbeth y bydden ni i gyd yn cytuno ag ef. O ran rhai o elfennau'r hyn rwyf wedi'i gyhoeddi heddiw a fyddai'n helpu i fynd i'r afael â'r pryder hwnnw, sy'n bryder teilwng iawn, yn fy marn i, wel, er enghraifft, yr hwb gwybodaeth gofal cymdeithasol, sy'n mynd i helpu i gryfhau cynllunio ac i nodi risgiau a phwysau mewn gwahanol rannau o Gymru er mwyn gweld, 'Iawn, felly beth sydd angen mynd i'r afael ag ef yn y fan yma o ran cryfhau comisiynu hefyd?', unwaith eto i adnabod gwahanol batrymau i wneud yn siŵr bod yna fwy o amlen wirioneddol genedlaethol o gymorth ar gael, oherwydd, ar hyn o bryd, mae gormod o bobl ar drugaredd penderfyniadau unigol, a fydd yn amrywio'n fawr mewn gwahanol rannau o'r wlad, ac rydym am symleiddio cyn belled â phosibl. Rwyf wedi dweud hyn o'r blaen: fyddai unrhyw un sy'n dylunio'r system gofal cymdeithasol o'r dechrau ddim yn ei dylunio fel y mae hi ar hyn o bryd, ond, yn amlwg, mae angen i ni weithio gyda phartneriaid mewn llywodraeth leol, gweithio gyda phartneriaid yng Nghymdeithas Cyfarwyddwyr Gwasanaethau Cymdeithasol. Mae pawb eisiau gweithio gyda'i gilydd i weld beth allwn ni ei wneud i wneud hyn yn well.

Fe ofynnoch chi am ofalwyr di-dâl hefyd, ac, oes, yn sicr, mae arnom fwy iddyn nhw na geiriau yn unig. Mae arnom fywyd gwell iddyn nhw, oherwydd maen nhw'n arbed biliynau o bunnoedd i'r llywodraeth ac i gymdeithas. Rydyn ni'n mynd i fod yn cyhoeddi'r strategaeth genedlaethol newydd ar gyfer gofalwyr di-dâl ym mis Tachwedd, sy'n mynd i fod yn nodi nifer o feysydd, gan gynnwys cysylltu ein hymateb ag adroddiad Pwyllgor Iechyd a Gofal Cymdeithasol y Senedd flaenorol. Mae honno'n mynd i fod yn edrych ar wella asesiadau gofalwyr, mynediad at seibiant, cymorth i ofalwyr aros mewn cyflogaeth â thâl, ac fe fydd yna ffocws penodol ar ofalwyr ifanc hefyd. Y gwasanaethau canolfan ddydd—mae'n rhywbeth rwyf wedi bod yn bryderus iawn amdano yn y gorffennol hefyd. Ac rwy'n gwybod, yn amlwg, bod hwn yn benderfyniad i awdurdodau lleol unigol. Mae'n rhywbeth mae gen i ddiddordeb mawr ynddo, ac rydw i'n sicr wedi clywed tystiolaeth gan nifer o bobl am yr effaith y gall hynny ei chael ar eu bywydau.

Fe ofynnoch chi am atal a'r ffyrdd y byddai fy nghyd-Aelod, y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal, a minnau'n gweithio gyda'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros lywodraeth leol. Mae yna nifer o grantiau, fel y gronfa integreiddio ranbarthol a grantiau eraill, sy'n edrych ar sut allwn ni fuddsoddi mwy mewn atal, ac mae'n rhywbeth rydyn ni'n awyddus iawn i'w ddatblygu.

Ac yn olaf—o, na, yn olaf ond un—ar yr academi, fe fydd, yn sicr, ac fe fyddaf yn gallu cyhoeddi mwy o wybodaeth am hyn yn fuan, gobeithio, o ran yr elfennau o hyn sy'n mynd i fod yn dod— dydw i ddim yn hoffi'r ymadrodd 'dod ar-lein'—sy'n mynd i gael eu cyflawni wedyn, wrth i hyn fynd yn ei flaen. Ond mae'n rhywbeth cyffrous iawn, ac mae'n rhywbeth lle rydyn ni'n arwain y ffordd. Mae yna lawer o academïau lleol ledled Cymru yn barod, felly mae llawer o hyn yn bodoli yn barod; rydyn ni jyst eisiau dod ag ef at ei gilydd mewn system genedlaethol sy'n cael ei chyflwyno'n lleol.

Ac yn olaf, ydw, rydw i'n hapus iawn i ymrwymo i roi diweddariadau rheolaidd ar hyn. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health: Update on the National Care Service Programme

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Gwasanaeth Gofal Cenedlaethol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health: Update on the National Care Service Programme
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Deputy Minister, for your statement today, and this is something that so many of us in this Chamber care so deeply about. Care and support services should enable people to live their best possible lives and most independent lives. And with that in mind, I want to recognise the extraordinary contribution made, day in, day out, by our social care workforce and the army of unpaid carers. Their compassion, their dedication and their hard work cannot be overstated.

Minister, your announcement does build on a long-standing commitment by Welsh Governments to move resources in health and social care from acute hospital services towards preventative services in the community. We recognise the need for action to meet rising demand and to offer dignity in care to vulnerable adults and children, and this has to be a priority for the Government.

Minister, you'll be pleased to hear that Welsh Labour does share your aspirations to build a national health and care service fit for the future, as laid out in the programme for government. We share key principles for social care, that social care should be free at the point of need and not based on ability to pay or which institution is commissioning or providing care and, wherever possible, enable people to live independently in their own home, to be delivered by a well-trained and remunerated workforce whose skills and commitment are valued as a vocation for care. And we too recognise that more support is needed for unpaid carers. And I hope that we can agree that unpaid carers are struggling to balance work and caring responsibilities. They are our unsung heroes, and unpaid carers of all ages do deserve more than warm words.

Deputy Minister, we're all pleased, I think, to see the emphasis put on caring and social care by the Prime Minister and him starting a national conversation in England, and I read in the statement and hear today the national conversation that you are starting. So, I'm very pleased that's happening, but I would like to have some more detail on when that will start and what form that will take. As your statement recognises, Wales is ahead of our neighbours, such as in the work of the national social care academy, which was started under the last Government, so I'm happy to see that moving forward. The Welsh Labour Government kept the capital limit at £50,000 so that people can keep more of their own money before they pay for care, and we also maintained the cap on domiciliary care charges so that no-one pays more than £100 a week for care in their own home. They do say, Deputy Minister, that imitation is the best form of flattery, so it's pleasing to see that Welsh Labour policies are continuing from the last Labour Government in your announcement today.

In Government, Welsh Labour made available funding for the real living wage to be implemented for the workforce in the social care sector, so, therefore, you will have whatever support you need from Welsh Labour to improve the pay, skills and career progression of the social care workforce. So, we welcome the proposed national social care academy, as I've said, and we do really need to promote that as a valued vocation, with high-quality training and status in our society.

I do have a number of questions, and I know that we'll all have these questions for you, but, Minister, how will you lead the care sector to meet the challenges of rising demand and complexity that you so rightly highlight in your statement, and how will you build more capacity in the care market to meet future demand so that hospitals can discharge patients to appropriate domiciliary and residential care? The problem with delayed discharge of care is a shortage of capacity in the domiciliary and residential care sectors, so how are you expanding the market and putting additional resources into the care market so that there are more places for the growing number of those needing care?

Minister, your long-term vision of a 10-year plan is a big ambition, but people will need to see action soon, and I know that councils in every annual budget round evidence to the Government that their social care costs are escalating rapidly. We do know that we have a growing older population and there's greater complexity of need, and the pressure on those budgets, then, are very focused. But—
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Ddirprwy Weinidog, am eich datganiad heddiw, ac mae hyn yn rhywbeth sydd mor bwysig i gynifer ohonom ni yn y Siambr hon. Fe ddylai gwasanaethau gofal a chymorth alluogi pobl i fyw eu bywydau gorau posibl a'u bywydau mwyaf annibynnol. A chyda hynny mewn golwg, rwyf eisiau cydnabod y cyfraniad rhyfeddol sy'n cael ei wneud, o ddydd i ddydd, gan ein gweithlu gofal cymdeithasol a'r fyddin o ofalwyr di-dâl. Ni ellir gorbwysleisio eu tosturi, eu hymroddiad a'r gwaith caled maen nhw'n ei wneud.

Weinidog, mae eich cyhoeddiad yn adeiladu ar ymrwymiad hirsefydlog gan Lywodraethau Cymru i symud adnoddau ym maes iechyd a gofal cymdeithasol o wasanaethau ysbytai acíwt tuag at wasanaethau ataliol yn y gymuned. Rydyn ni'n cydnabod bod angen gweithredu i ateb y galw cynyddol ac i gynnig urddas mewn gofal i oedolion a phlant sy'n agored i niwed, ac mae'n rhaid i hyn fod yn flaenoriaeth i'r Llywodraeth.

Weinidog, fe fyddwch chi'n falch o glywed bod Llafur Cymru yn rhannu eich dyheadau i adeiladu gwasanaeth iechyd a gofal cenedlaethol sy'n addas ar gyfer y dyfodol, fel y nodir yn y rhaglen lywodraethu. Rydyn ni'n rhannu egwyddorion allweddol ar gyfer gofal cymdeithasol, y dylai gofal cymdeithasol fod yn rhad ac am ddim ar yr adeg y mae ei angen a ddim yn seiliedig ar y gallu i dalu neu pa sefydliad sy'n comisiynu neu'n darparu gofal ac y dylai, lle bynnag y bo'n bosibl, alluogi pobl i fyw'n annibynnol yn eu cartref eu hunain, i'w ddarparu gan weithlu hyfforddedig â thâl y mae ei sgiliau a'i ymrwymiad yn cael eu gwerthfawrogi ar gyfer swydd ym maes gofal. Ac rydyn ni hefyd yn cydnabod bod angen mwy o gymorth i ofalwyr di-dâl. Ac rwy'n gobeithio y gallwn ni gytuno bod gofalwyr di-dâl yn ei chael hi'n anodd cydbwyso gwaith a chyfrifoldebau gofalu. Nhw yw ein harwyr di-glod, ac mae gofalwyr di-dâl o bob oed yn haeddu mwy na geiriau cynnes.

Ddirprwy Weinidog, rydyn ni i gyd yn falch, rwy'n credu, i weld y pwyslais sy'n cael ei roi ar ofalu a gofal cymdeithasol gan Brif Weinidog y DU a'r sgwrs genedlaethol y mae e wedi dechrau yn Lloegr, ac rwy'n darllen yn y datganiad ac yn clywed heddiw y sgwrs genedlaethol rydych chi'n ei dechrau. Felly, rwy'n falch iawn bod hynny'n digwydd, ond hoffwn i gael mwy o fanylion ynghylch pryd y bydd hynny'n dechrau a pha ffurf y bydd hynny'n ei chymryd. Fel y mae eich datganiad yn cydnabod, mae Cymru ar y blaen i'n cymdogion, megis o ran gwaith yr academi gofal cymdeithasol genedlaethol, a ddechreuwyd o dan y Llywodraeth ddiwethaf, felly rwy'n falch o weld hynny'n symud ymlaen. Fe gadwodd Llywodraeth Lafur Cymru y terfyn cyfalaf ar £50,000 fel bod pobl yn gallu cadw mwy o'u harian eu hunain cyn iddyn nhw dalu am ofal, ac fe wnaethon ni hefyd gadw'r cap ar ffioedd gofal cartref fel nad oes neb yn talu mwy na £100 yr wythnos am ofal yn eu cartref eu hunain. Maen nhw yn dweud, Ddirprwy Weinidog, mai dynwared yw'r ffurf fwyaf didwyll o wenieithu, felly mae'n braf gweld bod polisïau Llafur Cymru yn parhau o'r Llywodraeth Lafur ddiwethaf yn eich cyhoeddiad heddiw.

Yn y Llywodraeth, fe sicrhaodd Llafur Cymru fod cyllid ar gael i roi'r cyflog byw gwirioneddol ar waith ar gyfer y gweithlu yn y sector gofal cymdeithasol, felly, fe fydd gennych chi pa gymorth bynnag y bydd ei angen arnoch gan Lafur Cymru i wella cyflogau, sgiliau a dilyniant gyrfa'r gweithlu gofal cymdeithasol. Felly, rydyn ni'n croesawu'r academi gofal cymdeithasol genedlaethol arfaethedig, fel y dywedais i, ac mae angen i ni hyrwyddo hynny fel galwedigaeth werthfawr, gyda statws a hyfforddiant o ansawdd uchel yn ein cymdeithas.

Mae gen i nifer o gwestiynau, ac rwy'n gwybod y bydd gennym ni i gyd y cwestiynau hyn i chi, ond, Weinidog, sut fyddwch chi'n arwain y sector gofal i ateb yr heriau o ran galw a chymhlethdod cynyddol yr ydych chi, yn gywir ddigon, yn tynnu sylw atyn nhw yn eich datganiad, a sut fyddwch chi'n adeiladu mwy o gapasiti yn y farchnad gofal i ateb y galw yn y dyfodol fel bod ysbytai yn gallu rhyddhau cleifion i ofal cartref a phreswyl priodol? Y broblem gydag oedi cyn rhyddhau i ofal yw prinder capasiti yn y sectorau gofal cartref a phreswyl, felly sut ydych chi'n ehangu'r farchnad ac yn rhoi adnoddau ychwanegol i'r farchnad ofal fel bod mwy o leoedd ar gyfer y nifer cynyddol o'r rheini sydd angen gofal?

Weinidog, mae eich gweledigaeth hirdymor o gynllun 10 mlynedd yn uchelgais fawr, ond fe fydd angen i bobl weld gweithredu yn fuan, ac rwy'n gwybod bod cynghorau ym mhob cylch cyllideb blynyddol yn dangos i'r Llywodraeth bod eu costau gofal cymdeithasol yn cynyddu'n gyflym. Rydyn ni'n gwybod bod gennym ni boblogaeth hŷn sy'n tyfu a bod anghenion yn fwy cymhleth, ac mae'r pwysau ar y cyllidebau hynny, felly, yn benodol iawn. Ond—

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Gwasanaeth Gofal Cenedlaethol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health: Update on the National Care Service Programme
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Jayne. And before I start, I realised there was one thing I didn't answer James on, which was the funding. I can confirm that it's £3.6 million on top of the package of existing funding streams that is involved in this.

Diolch, Jayne, for your comments and your questions. And as you said at the start, this isn't about structures alone, is it? It's about people being able to live their most fulfilled lives possible—people being able to live as independently as they can for as long as possible. It is about making people's lives better. And I am really glad and grateful for your signal of support for the general vision here. And, again, I know that there will be individual areas where Members from across the Senedd of all parties will want to be interrogating, and that's you doing your jobs. I want you to be doing this; I want you to be pushing us to be more ambitious and seeing what things are working well and what we need to be improving. But where we can have unity of support for that overarching vision, whether it is the package or the individual elements within it, then I think that that is something, actually, really valuable.

I know that unpaid carers are a particular concern and passion for you and I'm really looking forward to being able to publish more of that detail in the strategy in November. And as I've said already, the Welsh Government has invested £13 million to help ensure carers receive the support they need in 2026-27, funding the short breaks scheme, carers support fund; an extra £7.35 million—sorry—that was included through the regional integration fund. There are lots of, as I say, individual ways in which the Government continues to support these vitally important people in our society, but we need to go further, of course.

I do welcome, as you have welcomed, Prime Minister Andy Burnham's focus on this. And yes, Wales has been ahead, but it doesn't matter who announced things first. The fact is that there is a moment here for us to be able to work together, and I really hope that that will be taken up. I've written to Yvette Cooper, the Secretary of State for Health and Social Care, to seek a bilateral ministerial discussion on social care reform, because I think we need to maximise this moment and the opportunities. And I know that a number of Members in this Chamber have already been involved in a cross-party discussion on the future of social care in Wales, and I again extend that invitation to representatives from all parties for those discussions to continue.

In terms of the maximum charges, as you set out, for care and support, Wales, again, is ahead of England here, but that isn't enough. We shouldn't rest on our laurels, of course. We need to be making sure—. Because every time I answer a letter saying, 'Oh, well, actually, this is the situation at the moment, and we're in a more advantageous position', it doesn't make it easier, though, does it, for the families who are having to lose so much money in order to give care to the people that they love.

And finally, in terms of the demographic picture that we have in Wales, in terms of the fact that people are living longer, that people are living, as you said, with more complex health and care needs, more families are balancing work, family life, caring responsibilities—we need to modernise the system. This isn't something that is going to go away. It's only going to get more serious and more needed. And you had asked me about how we can improve integration and make sure that the integration between health and care is working well. So, our pathways of care delay data is being used to understand the system-wide discharge challenges, the capacity constraints, variations in performance across Wales. I know that, in 2025-26, £30 million has been invested through the pathways of care transformation grant to support those improvements. We want to drive that further, and I really hope that there'll be cross-party support for that work.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Jayne. A chyn i mi ddechrau, fe wnes i sylweddoli bod un peth wnes i ddim ateb James arno, sef y cyllid. Gallaf gadarnhau ei fod yn £3.6 miliwn ar ben y pecyn o ffrydiau cyllido presennol sy'n ymwneud â hyn.

Diolch, Jayne, am eich sylwadau a'ch cwestiynau. Ac fel y dywedoch chi ar y dechrau, dydy hyn ddim yn ymwneud â strwythurau yn unig, nagyw? Mae'n ymwneud â phobl yn gallu byw eu bywydau mwyaf bodlon posibl—pobl yn gallu byw mor annibynnol ag y gallan nhw am gyhyd â phosibl. Mae'n ymwneud â gwneud bywydau pobl yn well. Ac rwy'n falch ac yn ddiolchgar iawn am eich arwydd o gefnogaeth i'r weledigaeth gyffredinol yma. Ac, unwaith eto, rwy'n gwybod y bydd yna feysydd unigol lle bydd Aelodau o bob rhan o'r Senedd o bob plaid eisiau mynd ati i gwestiynu, a chi yn gwneud eich gwaith yw hynny. Rwyf am i chi fod yn gwneud hyn; rwyf am i chi fod yn ein gwthio i fod yn fwy uchelgeisiol ac i weld pa bethau sy'n gweithio'n dda a beth sydd angen i ni fod yn ei wella. Ond lle gallwn ni gael undod o ran cefnogaeth i'r weledigaeth gyffredinol honno, p'un ai'r pecyn neu'r elfennau unigol oddi mewn iddo, yna rwy'n credu bod hynny, mewn gwirioneddol, yn rhywbeth gwerthfawr iawn.

Rwy'n gwybod bod gofalwyr di-dâl yn bryder penodol i chi ac yn rhywbeth rydych chi'n teimlo'n angerddol yn ei gylch ac rwy'n edrych ymlaen yn fawr at allu cyhoeddi mwy o'r manylion hynny yn y strategaeth ym mis Tachwedd. Ac fel rwyf wedi'i ddweud eisoes, mae Llywodraeth Cymru wedi buddsoddi £13 miliwn er mwyn helpu i sicrhau bod gofalwyr yn cael y cymorth sydd ei angen arnyn nhw yn 2026-27, gan ariannu'r cynllun seibiant byr, y gronfa cymorth i ofalwyr; £7.35 miliwn ychwanegol—mae'n ddrwg gen i—fe gafodd hwnnw ei gynnwys drwy'r gronfa integreiddio ranbarthol. Fel y dywedais, mae'r Llywodraeth yn parhau i gefnogi'r bobl hanfodol bwysig hyn yn ein cymdeithas mewn llawer o ffyrdd unigol, ond mae angen i ni fynd ymhellach, wrth gwrs.

Rwy'n croesawu, fel yr ydych chi wedi croesawu, ffocws Prif Weinidog y DU, Andy Burnham, ar hyn. Ac ydy, mae Cymru wedi bod ar y blaen, ond does dim ots pwy wnaeth gyhoeddi pethau gyntaf. Y gwir amdani yw bod yna foment yma i ni allu gweithio gyda'n gilydd, ac rwy'n gobeithio'n fawr y bydd hynny'n digwydd. Rwyf wedi ysgrifennu at Yvette Cooper, yr Ysgrifennydd Gwladol dros Iechyd a Gofal Cymdeithasol, i geisio trafodaeth weinidogol ddwyochrog ar ddiwygio gofal cymdeithasol, oherwydd rwy'n credu bod angen i ni wneud y mwyaf o'r foment hon a'r cyfleoedd. Ac rwy'n gwybod bod nifer o Aelodau yn y Siambr hon eisoes wedi bod yn rhan o drafodaeth drawsbleidiol ar ddyfodol gofal cymdeithasol yng Nghymru, ac rwy'n estyn y gwahoddiad hwnnw unwaith eto i gynrychiolwyr o bob plaid i'r trafodaethau hynny barhau.

O ran y taliadau uchaf, fel y nodwyd gennych, ar gyfer gofal a chymorth, mae Cymru, unwaith eto, ar y blaen i Loegr yn hyn o beth, ond dydy hynny ddim yn ddigon. Ddylen ni ddim gorffwys ar ein rhwyfau, wrth gwrs. Mae angen i ni fod yn gwneud yn siŵr—. Oherwydd bob tro rwy'n ateb llythyr gan ddweud, 'O, wel, mewn gwirionedd, dyma'r sefyllfa ar hyn o bryd, ac rydyn ni mewn sefyllfa fwy buddiol', dydy e ddim yn ei gwneud hi'n haws, nac ydy, i'r teuluoedd sy'n gorfod colli cymaint o arian er mwyn rhoi gofal i'r bobl maen nhw'n eu caru.

Ac yn olaf, o ran y darlun demograffig sydd gennym ni yng Nghymru, o ran y ffaith bod pobl yn byw'n hirach, bod pobl yn byw, fel y dywedsoch, gydag anghenion iechyd a gofal mwy cymhleth, bod mwy o deuluoedd yn cydbwyso gwaith, bywyd teuluol, cyfrifoldebau gofalu—mae angen i ni foderneiddio'r system. Dydy hyn ddim yn rhywbeth sy'n mynd i ddiflannu. Mae'n mynd i fynd yn fwy difrifol ac yn fwy angenrheidiol. Ac roeddech chi wedi gofyn i mi sut allwn ni wella integreiddio a gwneud yn siŵr bod yr integreiddio rhwng iechyd a gofal yn gweithio'n dda. Felly, mae ein data oedi o fewn llwybrau gofal yn cael ei ddefnyddio i ddeall yr heriau o ran rhyddhau ar draws y system gyfan, y cyfyngiadau o ran capasiti, yr amrywiadau mewn perfformiad ledled Cymru. Rwy'n gwybod bod £30 miliwn wedi'i fuddsoddi yn 2025-26 drwy'r grant trawsnewid llwybrau gofal i gefnogi'r gwelliannau hynny. Rydyn ni eisiau ysgogi hynny ymhellach, ac rwyf wir yn gobeithio y bydd cefnogaeth drawsbleidiol i'r gwaith hwnnw.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Gwasanaeth Gofal Cenedlaethol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health: Update on the National Care Service Programme
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Can I thank the Deputy Minister for this afternoon's statement? For me, this is another week, another statement from the Welsh Government that, quite frankly, doesn't say or do a great deal. There's a lot of warm words here, but little detail on how this is actually going to be achieved going forward.

Deputy Presiding Officer, I'm sure there's not a single person in this Chamber who doesn't agree that we need major improvements when it comes to social care. Recognising a problem is one thing. Delivering a serious solution is another. And my Welsh Conservative colleagues and I do not believe a national care system is going to be the answer. Because I cannot simply see right now how it's going to tackle the issue of capacity, recruitment and hospital discharge delays. We need immediate improvements in existing services, Deputy Minister, not wasting time focusing on a care service that's going to be years in the making. Closed community hospital wards need to be reopened, capacity needs to be expanded, recruitment and retention must be a top priority, which is something we're hearing consistently in this Chamber.

The Welsh Conservatives believe that there is a practical alternative, and that is improving social care through sustainable funding, stronger co-operation between the NHS and local authorities, greater personal choice and better support for those who provide care. So, I'd like to know what the Welsh Government's doing now to improve social care, Deputy Minister, as your ambition for social care is going to be years away by what I've been reading today. Funding will be crucial for any care service plan. So, Deputy Minister, your Government tells us it wants social care to be free at the point of use, just like the NHS, yet we have no detail of how much this initiative will cost. You mentioned to James Evans earlier £3.6 million extra on top of the current package, but has the Plaid Cymru Government found a magic money tree somewhere? Because is this just a case of overpromising and underdelivering, because where is the detailed assessment of the long-term costs? We have an ageing population, Deputy Minister, so the bill will undoubtedly rise year by year. Those are questions that taxpayers deserve to have answered.

Outcomes are another concern that I have when it comes to the care service, and, ultimately, I think it's outcomes that the people of Wales care about the most. How confident are you, Deputy Minister, that your care service will bring about these genuinely big benefits? What are you doing to ensure it results in that a family looking after loved ones with dementia can actually access respite care easily? And how exactly are you going to ensure it results in a fall in the number of bedblocking incidents, which remain far too high? Also, how are you going to ensure that it results in an older person receiving quicker support when they can no longer manage to live at home safely? How will the Government ensure its care service actually delivers its aims and goals and isn't just another Government quango that adds another layer of bureaucracy?

Workforce is another cause of concern for me, Deputy Minister. How are you going to ensure there are enough staff to successfully implement and sustain this national care service? We all know the sector is already under immense pressure when it comes to recruitment and retention, and I must pay tribute to those working tirelessly in the field. In 2025, there were more than 6,100 estimated vacancies within the sector—June 2025—up drastically from the previous year. Not only that, but according to a survey from Social Care Wales, 20 per cent of staff said they were aiming to leave the sector within an average of 14 months. So, not only is getting workers through the door in the first place a major problem but keeping them in the job itself is a serious challenge right now. How is that going to be addressed, Deputy Minister?

In your statement, you talk about establishing a national social care academy again. The details were light for me. When will this be created? Where will this be created? How much is this costing? What is the anticipated capacity? These are all questions that I would really like to have the answers for. Deputy Minister, if the Plaid Government is going to push ahead with plans to create a national care service, these questions have to be addressed before that happens. Those residents across Wales who depend on our social care sector need more than just a pipe dream. They need a costed, detailed and credible plan. Thank you.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
A gaf fi ddiolch i'r Dirprwy Weinidog am y datganiad y prynhawn yma? I mi, mae hon yn wythnos arall, yn ddatganiad arall gan Lywodraeth Cymru sydd ddim yn dweud nac yn gwneud rhyw llawer, a bod yn onest. Mae yna lawer o eiriau cynnes yma, ond ychydig iawn o fanylion ynghylch sut mae hyn yn mynd i gael ei gyflawni wrth symud ymlaen.

Ddirprwy Lywydd, rwy'n siŵr nad oes un person yn y Siambr hon nad yw'n cytuno bod angen gwelliannau mawr arnom o ran gofal cymdeithasol. Mae cydnabod problem yn un peth. Mae darparu ateb difrifol yn un arall. A dydy fy nghyd-Aelodau Ceidwadol Cymreig a minnau ddim yn credu mai system gofal genedlaethol yw'r ateb. Oherwydd allaf i ddim gweld ar hyn o bryd sut mae'n mynd i fynd i'r afael â'r mater o gapasiti, recriwtio ac oedi cyn rhyddhau o'r ysbyty. Mae angen gwelliannau ar unwaith i wasanaethau sy'n bodoli eisoes, Ddirprwy Weinidog, yn lle gwastraffu amser yn canolbwyntio ar wasanaeth gofal y mae'n mynd i gymryd blynyddoedd i'w roi ar waith. Mae angen ailagor wardiau ysbytai cymunedol sydd wedi cau, mae angen ehangu capasiti, mae'n rhaid i recriwtio a chadw fod yn brif flaenoriaeth, rhywbeth rydyn ni'n ei glywed yn gyson yn y Siambr hon.

Mae'r Ceidwadwyr Cymreig yn credu bod dewis arall ymarferol, a hynny yw gwella gofal cymdeithasol drwy gyllid cynaliadwy, cydweithredu cryfach rhwng y GIG ac awdurdodau lleol, mwy o ddewis personol a gwell cefnogaeth i'r rhai sy'n darparu gofal. Felly, hoffwn i wybod beth mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn ei wneud nawr i wella gofal cymdeithasol, Ddirprwy Weinidog, gan fod eich uchelgais ar gyfer gofal cymdeithasol yn mynd i gymryd blynyddoedd yn ôl yr hyn rwyf wedi bod yn ei ddarllen heddiw. Bydd cyllid yn hanfodol ar gyfer unrhyw gynllun gwasanaeth gofal. Felly, Ddirprwy Weinidog, mae eich Llywodraeth yn dweud wrthym ei bod eisiau i ofal cymdeithasol fod yn rhad ac am ddim ar yr adeg y caiff ei ddefnyddio, yn union fel y GIG, ond nid oes gennym unrhyw fanylion am faint y bydd y fenter hon yn ei gostio. Fe sonioch chi wrth James Evans yn gynharach y byddai £3.6 miliwn yn ychwanegol ar ben y pecyn presennol, ond a yw Llywodraeth Plaid Cymru wedi dod o hyd i goeden arian hud yn rhywle? Oherwydd ydy hyn yn achos o or-addo a thangyflawni, oherwydd ble mae'r asesiad manwl o'r costau hirdymor? Mae gennym ni boblogaeth sy'n heneiddio, Ddirprwy Weinidog, felly bydd y bil yn sicr yn codi flwyddyn ar ôl blwyddyn. Mae'r rheini'n gwestiynau y mae trethdalwyr yn haeddu cael ateb iddyn nhw.

Mae canlyniadau'n bryder arall sydd gen i o ran y gwasanaeth gofal, ac, yn y pen draw, rwy'n credu mai canlyniadau y mae pobl Cymru yn poeni amdanyn nhw fwyaf. Pa mor hyderus ydych chi, Ddirprwy Weinidog, y bydd eich gwasanaeth gofal yn cyflawni'r buddion gwirioneddol fawr hyn? Beth ydych chi'n ei wneud i sicrhau y bydd teulu sy'n gofalu am anwyliaid â dementia yn gallu cael mynediad at ofal seibiant yn hawdd o ganlyniad i hyn? A sut yn union ydych chi'n mynd i sicrhau ei fod yn arwain at lai o achosion o flocio gwelyau, sy'n parhau i fod yn llawer rhy uchel? Hefyd, sut ydych chi'n mynd i sicrhau y bydd person hŷn yn derbyn cymorth yn gyflymach pan na all fyw gartref yn ddiogel mwyach? Sut fydd y Llywodraeth yn sicrhau bod ei gwasanaeth gofal yn cyflawni ei nodau a'i amcanion go iawn ac nad yw'n gwango arall y Llywodraeth sy'n ychwanegu haen arall o fiwrocratiaeth?

Mae'r gweithlu yn achos arall o bryder i mi, Ddirprwy Weinidog. Sut ydych chi'n mynd i sicrhau bod digon o staff i weithredu a chynnal y gwasanaeth gofal cenedlaethol hwn yn llwyddiannus? Rydyn ni i gyd yn gwybod bod y sector eisoes o dan bwysau enfawr o ran recriwtio a chadw, ac mae'n rhaid i mi dalu teyrnged i'r rhai sy'n gweithio'n ddiflino yn y maes. Yn 2025, amcangyfrifwyd bod mwy na 6,100 o swyddi gwag yn y sector—Mehefin 2025—i fyny'n sylweddol o'r flwyddyn flaenorol. Nid yn unig hynny, ond yn ôl arolwg gan Gofal Cymdeithasol Cymru, fe ddywedodd 20 y cant o staff eu bod yn anelu at adael y sector o fewn 14 mis ar gyfartaledd. Felly, nid yn unig mae cael gweithwyr drwy'r drws yn y lle cyntaf yn broblem fawr ond mae eu cadw yn y swydd yn her fawr ar hyn o bryd. Sut ydych chi'n mynd i fynd i'r afael â hynny, Ddirprwy Weinidog?

Yn eich datganiad, rydych chi'n sôn am sefydlu academi gofal cymdeithasol genedlaethol eto. Doedd yna ddim digon o fanylion i mi. Pryd fydd hon yn cael ei chreu? Ble bydd hon yn cael ei chreu? Faint mae hyn yn ei gostio? Beth yw'r capasiti disgwyliedig? Mae'r rhain i gyd yn gwestiynau yr hoffwn i gael yr atebion iddyn nhw. Ddirprwy Weinidog, os yw Llywodraeth Plaid yn mynd i fwrw ymlaen â chynlluniau i greu gwasanaeth gofal cenedlaethol, mae'n rhaid mynd i'r afael â'r cwestiynau hyn cyn i hynny ddigwydd. Mae angen mwy na breuddwyd ar y trigolion hynny ledled Cymru sy'n dibynnu ar ein sector gofal cymdeithasol. Mae angen cynllun manwl a chredadwy wedi'i gostio arnyn nhw. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Gwasanaeth Gofal Cenedlaethol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health: Update on the National Care Service Programme

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Gwasanaeth Gofal Cenedlaethol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health: Update on the National Care Service Programme
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Natasha. I'm sorry that you think that it's weak. We're talking about stuff here that we can't afford not to do. This is about making people's lives better. It's about making sure that people can have a better quality of life. What on earth are we here for if not to do something like this? But I'll move on to the questions that you have asked.

I'll talk you through some of the ways in which the package that I have announced today is going to be making real differences to people's lives. In terms of the social care academy, that will help recruitment. It will help with the retention of care workers. And it will help to build esteem for that workforce, because one of the things—and it's come up already a few times today—one of the things that is maddening is that during the COVID pandemic, everyone had this moment of appreciating care workers. And we all went out into the streets, we applauded them. And somehow in our collective psyche as society, people have allowed themselves to forget that importance. These are the people who keep our society going.

So, that academy is going to be, yes, about giving that career progression, but it's also going to be about giving that greater gravitas and esteem to the profession too. And again, I'm looking forward to being able to announce further detail on that. But that is something that I hope we would have cross-party support on. And I know that there's a lot of interest from our neighbouring countries about how the local academies are already working and how we're going to be bringing that through to a national picture.

On the social care intelligence hub, that's going to, again, help strengthen planning, help to identify risks and pressures. The work of the pathways of care intelligence, that's going to improve discharge processes from hospital to address capacity constraints. The work on unpaid carers is going to improve how early people are identified as unpaid carers, how well they're assessed in terms of the support that they're going to get. Each of these actions is going to make a material improvement in people's lives. Every single one of these things will make a difference.

In terms of assessing what we're doing and finding better ways of how things could work, all of this work is fundamental, because otherwise we will be trying to build a castle on sand—and not just sand, but quicksand, because it is moving under our feet all the time. We have to make sure that the foundations dig deep into the ground. That's why this planning work is so vitally important.

But you asked some other questions too. On dementia, I won't repeat what I've already said in terms of the pathways of care. You did ask about future funding, which is a fair question, certainly. We're going to be carrying out detailed modelling work to understand how the changes to care charging could affect people in the future, and that's going to be assessing the financial, distributional, operational impacts of different charging and funding options. Where more sophisticated analysis will be required, we're going to be commissioning that through specialist external expertise. And so, from April 2027, a dedicated social care intelligence hub is going to be strengthening that modelling, that analytical capacity. 

A number of the other questions that you had asked in terms of the workforce, in terms of how we're going to be making sure that that capacity is driven up, the social care academy is going to be doing an awful lot of that work. I hope very much that I and other Members will be able to convince you of the really important need for this work. But I thank you for your questions.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Natasha. Mae'n ddrwg gen i eich bod chi'n meddwl ei fod e'n wan. Rydyn ni'n siarad am bethau yn y fan yma allwn ni ddim fforddio peidio â'u gwneud. Mae hyn yn ymwneud â gwneud bywydau pobl yn well. Mae'n ymwneud â gwneud yn siŵr bod pobl yn gallu cael gwell ansawdd bywyd. Pam ar y ddaear ydyn ni yma os nad i wneud rhywbeth fel hyn? Ond fe symudaf ymlaen at y cwestiynau rydych chi wedi'u gofyn.

Fe wnaf i siarad am rai o'r ffyrdd mae'r pecyn rydw i wedi'i gyhoeddi heddiw yn mynd i wneud gwahaniaethau gwirioneddol i fywydau pobl. O ran yr academi gofal cymdeithasol, bydd honno'n helpu recriwtio. Bydd yn helpu i gadw gweithwyr gofal. A bydd yn helpu i feithrin parch at y gweithlu hwnnw, oherwydd un o'r pethau—ac mae wedi cael ei godi sawl gwaith yn barod heddiw—un o'r pethau gwallgof yw bod pawb wedi cael y foment hon o werthfawrogi gweithwyr gofal yn ystod pandemig COVID. Ac fe aethon ni i gyd allan i'r strydoedd, fe wnaethon ni eu cymeradwyo. A rhywsut yn ein psyche cyfunol fel cymdeithas, mae pobl wedi caniatáu iddyn nhw eu hunain anghofio'r pwysigrwydd hwnnw. Dyma'r bobl sy'n cadw ein cymdeithas i fynd.

Felly, ydy, mae'r academi honno yn mynd i fod yn ymwneud â rhoi'r dilyniant gyrfa hwnnw, ond mae hefyd yn mynd i fod yn ymwneud â rhoi mwy o gravitas a pharch i'r proffesiwn hefyd. Ac eto, rwy'n edrych ymlaen at allu cyhoeddi rhagor o fanylion ar hynny. Ond mae hynny'n rhywbeth rwy'n gobeithio y byddwn ni'n cael cefnogaeth drawsbleidiol arno. Ac rwy'n gwybod bod yna lawer o ddiddordeb gan ein gwledydd cyfagos yn y ffordd mae'r academïau lleol eisoes yn gweithio a sut rydyn ni'n mynd i ddod â hynny drwodd i ddarlun cenedlaethol.

O ran yr hwb gwybodaeth gofal cymdeithasol, mae hwnnw, unwaith eto, yn mynd i helpu i gryfhau cynllunio, helpu i nodi risgiau a phwysau. Mae'r wybodaeth am lwybrau gofal, mae'r gwaith hwnnw'n mynd i wella prosesau rhyddhau o'r ysbyty i fynd i'r afael â chyfyngiadau o ran capasiti. Mae'r gwaith ar ofalwyr di-dâl yn mynd i wella pa mor gynnar mae pobl yn cael eu hadnabod fel gofalwyr di-dâl, pa mor dda maen nhw'n cael eu hasesu o ran y cymorth maen nhw'n mynd i'w gael. Mae pob un o'r camau hyn yn mynd i wneud gwelliant sylweddol i fywydau pobl. Bydd pob un o'r pethau hyn yn gwneud gwahaniaeth.

O ran asesu'r hyn rydyn ni'n ei wneud a dod o hyd i ffyrdd gwell o sut y gallai pethau weithio, mae'r holl waith hwn yn sylfaenol, oherwydd fel arall fe fyddwn ni'n ceisio adeiladu castell ar dywod—ac nid dim ond tywod, ond tywod byw, oherwydd mae'n symud o dan ein traed drwy'r amser. Mae'n rhaid i ni wneud yn siŵr bod y sylfeini yn ddwfn yn y ddaear. Dyna pam mae'r gwaith cynllunio hwn mor hanfodol bwysig.

Ond fe ofynnoch chi rai cwestiynau eraill hefyd. O ran dementia, wnaf i ddim ailadrodd yr hyn rwyf eisoes wedi'i ddweud o ran y llwybrau gofal. Fe ofynnoch chi am gyllid yn y dyfodol, sy'n gwestiwn teg, yn sicr. Rydyn ni'n mynd i fod yn gwneud gwaith modelu manwl i ddeall sut y gallai'r newidiadau i daliadau gofal effeithio ar bobl yn y dyfodol, ac mae hwnnw'n mynd i fod yn asesu effeithiau ariannol, dosbarthiadol, gweithredol gwahanol opsiynau codi tâl a chyllido. Lle bydd angen dadansoddi mwy soffistigedig, rydyn ni'n mynd i fod yn comisiynu hynny trwy arbenigedd allanol arbenigol. Ac felly, o fis Ebrill 2027, mae hwb gwybodaeth gofal cymdeithasol pwrpasol yn mynd i fod yn cryfhau'r gwaith modelu hwnnw, y gallu dadansoddol hwnnw.

Nifer o'r cwestiynau eraill yr oeddech wedi'u gofyn o ran y gweithlu, o ran sut rydyn ni'n mynd i fod yn gwneud yn siŵr bod y capasiti hwnnw'n cael ei gynyddu, mae'r academi gofal cymdeithasol yn mynd i fod yn gwneud llawer iawn o'r gwaith hwnnw. Rwy'n gobeithio'n fawr y byddaf i ac Aelodau eraill yn gallu eich argyhoeddi o'r angen gwirioneddol bwysig am y gwaith hwn. Ond diolch i chi am eich cwestiynau.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Gwasanaeth Gofal Cenedlaethol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health: Update on the National Care Service Programme

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Gwasanaeth Gofal Cenedlaethol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health: Update on the National Care Service Programme
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Dwi'n gorfod datgan diddordeb: dwi wedi gweithio yn y maes ac mae gen i aelod o’r teulu yn gweithio yn y maes.

Diolch am y datganiad. Dwi'n croesawu’n fawr ymrwymiad Llywodraeth Plaid Cymru i wneud y sector yma yn fwy deniadol drwy well cyflogau, hyfforddiant, llwybrau gyrfa a sefydlu academi gofal cenedlaethol. Mae hefyd yn dangos y gwahaniaeth rhwng dull Plaid Cymru o weithredu drwy ddiwygio gwasanaethau nawr a'r dull a welwn gan Lywodraeth Lafur y Deyrnas Unedig, lle mae addewidion am ddiwygio yn parhau i gael eu gohirio. 

Fel cyn-weithiwr yn y sector, credaf fod pedair colofn allweddol i ofal cymdeithasol: gweithwyr gofal, gweithwyr cymdeithasol, therapyddion galwedigaethol ac eiriolwyr. Mae’n bwysig i mi fod holl leisiau'r colofnau hyn yn cael eu clywed yn y broses hon. Gyda hynny mewn golwg, a fyddai’r Dirprwy Weinidog yn barod i gyfarfod â mi, fel darpar gadeirydd y grŵp trawsbleidiol ar ofal cymdeithasol, i drafod y materion hyn ymhellach?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
I must declare an interest: I've worked in this area and I have a member of my family who also works in the sector.

Thank you for the statement. I very much welcome the Plaid Cymru Government’s commitment to making the sector more attractive through better wages, training, career pathways and establishing a national care academy. It also shows the difference between Plaid Cymru's approach of reforming services now and the approach that we see from the UK Labour Government, whose promised reforms are constantly being postponed.

As a former worker in the sector, I believe that there are four key pillars of social care: care workers, social workers, occupational therapists and advocates. It's important to me that the voices of all four of these cornerstones are heard during the process. With that in mind, would the Deputy Minister be willing to meet with me, as chair-elect of the cross-party group on social care, to discuss these matters further?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Gwasanaeth Gofal Cenedlaethol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health: Update on the National Care Service Programme
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch i chi, Elfed. Mae'n flin gen i fy mod i'n gorfod cael fy nghefn tuag atoch chi wrth ymateb. Dwi'n cytuno y dylem ni sicrhau bod y system yn un llawer mwy deniadol ar gyfer cael mwy o bobl i mewn i'r gweithlu, a dwi'n cytuno hefyd y bydd angen i'r holl leisiau rŷch chi newydd fod yn sôn amdanyn nhw i gael eu clywed yn rhan o'r foment yma, achos mae yna gyfle. Ac eto, dwi'n gobeithio y bydd y cyfuniad o'r gwaith rŷn ni wedi'i wneud yn barod yng Nghymru, y gwaith rŷn ni'n parhau i'w wneud, a'r momentwm sydd yn cael ei hybu oherwydd beth sy'n digwydd ar lefel San Steffan—. Oes, mae lot o ohirio, ond dal, dylem ni gymryd mantais o'r foment yma, a dwi'n gobeithio bydd y ddau beth yn gallu plethu mewn ffordd fydd yn dda ar gyfer pawb, a buaswn i'n croesawu'r drafodaeth gyda chi fel cadeirydd y grŵp trawsbleidiol, yn sicr. Felly, diolch i chi, a diolch am eich gwaith yn y maes.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you, Elfed. I apologise that I'll have my back to you as I respond. I agree that we should ensure that the system is far more attractive in order to attract people into the workforce, and I agree that all of the voices that you've just mentioned need to be heard at this very moment, because there is an opportunity. And again, I hope that the combination of the work that we have done already in Wales, the work that we continue to do, and the momentum happening because of what's happening in Westminster—. Yes, there have been some postponements, but still, we should take advantage of this moment, and I very much hope that the two things can dovetail in a way that benefits everyone, and I would welcome a discussion with you as chair of the cross-party group, certainly. So, thank you very much, and thank you for your work in this area.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Gwasanaeth Gofal Cenedlaethol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health: Update on the National Care Service Programme
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I'd like to reiterate my praise for the hard work of carers right across Wales, and unpaid carers as well. We keep hearing ambitious promises about a national care and support service, yet front-line social care in places such as Flintshire and Wrexham remains under severe pressure. Around 1,300 to 1,400 patients across Wales are waiting in hospital despite being medically fit for discharge because the care packages and supported accommodation they need are simply not available. In north Wales, those pressures are felt particularly acutely as Betsi Cadwaladr continues to face significant challenges. While care providers struggle with workforce shortages, rising demand and commissioning pressures cause problems.

Deputy Minister, much of your statement, as stated by Natasha Asghar, focuses on new structures, leadership arrangements, intelligence hubs, academies and national conversations, but for the families waiting for support and patients stuck in hospital beds, those initiatives will mean little unless they deliver real improvements on the ground. So, my question is: given that you say success should be measured not by structures you created, but by whether people can access the right support at the right time, when can older and vulnerable people across Wales expect to see a measurable increase in the front-line care capacity, a reduction in delayed hospital discharges and better access to the care and support they need, rather than more administration, new bodies and further planning?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Hoffwn ganmol unwaith eto waith caled gofalwyr ledled Cymru, a gofalwyr di-dâl hefyd. Rydyn ni'n parhau i glywed addewidion uchelgeisiol am wasanaeth gofal a chymorth cenedlaethol, ond mae gofal cymdeithasol rheng flaen mewn llefydd fel sir y Fflint a Wrecsam yn parhau i fod dan bwysau difrifol. Mae tua 1,300 i 1,400 o gleifion ledled Cymru yn aros yn yr ysbyty er eu bod yn ddigon iach yn feddygol i gael eu rhyddhau oherwydd dydy'r pecynnau gofal a'r llety â chymorth sydd eu hangen arnyn nhw ddim ar gael. Yn y gogledd, mae'r pwysau hynny'n cael eu teimlo'n ddifrifol  wrth i Betsi Cadwaladr barhau i wynebu heriau sylweddol. Tra bod darparwyr gofal yn ei chael hi'n anodd ymdopi gyda phrinder gweithlu, mae galw cynyddol a phwysau comisiynu yn achosi problemau.

Ddirprwy Weinidog, mae llawer o'ch datganiad, fel y nodwyd gan Natasha Asghar, yn canolbwyntio ar strwythurau newydd, trefniadau arweinyddiaeth, hybiau gwybodaeth, academïau a sgyrsiau cenedlaethol, ond i'r teuluoedd sy'n aros am gymorth a'r cleifion sy'n sownd mewn gwelyau ysbyty, fydd y mentrau hynny ddim yn golygu rhyw lawer oni bai eu bod yn cyflawni gwelliannau gwirioneddol ar lawr gwlad. Felly, fy nghwestiwn yw: o ystyried eich bod chi'n dweud y dylai llwyddiant gael ei fesur nid yn ôl y strwythurau a grëwyd gennych, ond yn ôl a all pobl gael mynediad at y cymorth cywir ar yr adeg gywir, pryd all pobl hŷn a bregus ledled Cymru ddisgwyl gweld cynnydd mesuradwy yng nghapasiti gofal rheng flaen, llai o achosion o oedi wrth ryddhau o ysbytai a gwell mynediad at y gofal a'r cymorth sydd eu hangen arnyn nhw, yn hytrach na mwy o weinyddiaeth, cyrff newydd a chynllunio pellach?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Gwasanaeth Gofal Cenedlaethol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health: Update on the National Care Service Programme
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Nigel. In terms of the final challenge that you put to me there, it is of course a fair one: we shouldn't ever be, and I would never want to be, measuring the work that we are doing here in terms of just structures or what's written down on a piece of paper. It has to be in what difference it makes to the reality of people's lives—people who are really struggling in society and need this support. As you've said, our front-line workers are under tremendous pressure and there are far too many people who are able to leave hospital and are not leaving hospital because of delayed discharges. It is not good enough and we need to do better. I do agree with you.

In terms of these structures that I've been announcing, each of these is going to be necessary in order to encompass the work that we are doing. I don't want us to be measuring just the structures, but they are more than just bodies. They are about making sure that the work that we do, that it works together properly. When we talk about a national intelligence hub, that's not just for the sake of having a national intelligence hub. It's to make sure that we can see the patterns of, 'Okay, so, where could these discharges be improved here? What is'—sorry, I'm not in front of the microphone—'happening in this local health board area? Is this happening somewhere else? Is this a national problem? Is this something where we need to be targeting support?'

I go again back to the point that it is greater than the sum of its parts, but it only will be greater if it truly delivers for people. There will be demonstrable ways in which people will be able to see improvements over the course of this Senedd term. It's similar to the safeguarding announcement that I made a few weeks ago. Okay, there are some elements—. For example, the hub will be coming in in April 2027. I hope that, certainly within months of that coming live, we would be able to see demonstrable improvements. I would really welcome Members' thoughts, both from the committee and Members more generally, about what would be the best ways for the Senedd to continuing scrutinising how this develops. This is something that goes beyond any Government and goes beyond any party. We have to get this right for our society, so I would welcome further conversations on that. Thank you.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Nigel. O ran yr her olaf a roesoch i mi yn y fan yna, mae'n un deg, wrth gwrs: ddylen ni byth fod, a fydden i byth eisiau bod yn mesur y gwaith rydyn ni'n ei wneud yma o ran strwythurau yn unig neu'r hyn sydd wedi'i ysgrifennu ar ddarn o bapur. Mae'n rhaid iddo gael ei fesur yn ôl y gwahaniaeth mae'n ei wneud i realiti bywydau pobl—pobl sydd wir yn ei chael hi'n anodd mewn cymdeithas ac sydd angen y cymorth hwnnw. Fel y dywedoch chi, mae ein gweithwyr rheng flaen o dan bwysau aruthrol ac mae llawer gormod o bobl sy'n gallu gadael yr ysbyty ac sydd ddim yn gadael yr ysbyty oherwydd oedi wrth eu rhyddhau. Dydy e ddim yn ddigon da ac mae angen i ni wneud yn well. Rwy'n cytuno â chi.

O ran y strwythurau hyn rwyf wedi bod yn eu cyhoeddi, mae pob un o'r rhain yn mynd i fod yn angenrheidiol er mwyn cwmpasu'r gwaith rydyn ni'n ei wneud. Dydw i ddim eisiau i ni fod yn mesur y strwythurau yn unig, ond maen nhw'n fwy na dim ond cyrff. Maen nhw'n ymwneud â gwneud yn siŵr bod y gwaith rydyn ni'n ei wneud, ei fod yn gweithio gyda'i gilydd yn iawn. Pan ydyn ni'n sôn am hwb gwybodaeth cenedlaethol, dydy hynny ddim jyst er mwyn cael hwb gwybodaeth cenedlaethol. Mae hynny er mwyn gwneud yn siŵr ein bod ni'n gallu gweld y patrymau o, 'Iawn, felly, ble gallai'r achosion hyn o ryddhau gael eu gwella yn y fan yma? Beth sy'n'—mae'n ddrwg gen i, dydw i ddim o flaen y meicroffon—'digwydd yn ardal y bwrdd iechyd lleol hwn? Ydy e'n digwydd yn rhywle arall? A yw hyn yn broblem genedlaethol? A yw hyn yn rhywbeth lle mae angen i ni fod yn targedu cymorth?'

Rwy'n mynd yn ôl eto i'r pwynt ei fod yn fwy na chyfanswm ei rannau, ond dim ond bydd yn cyflawni i bobl go iawn y bydd yn fwy. Bydd yna ffyrdd amlwg y bydd pobl yn gallu gweld gwelliannau yn ystod tymor y Senedd hon. Mae'n debyg i'r cyhoeddiad diogelu a wnes ychydig wythnosau yn ôl. Iawn, mae yna rai elfennau—. Er enghraifft, bydd yr hwb yn dod yn weithredol ym mis Ebrill 2027. Rwy'n gobeithio, yn sicr o fewn misoedd iddo ddod yn weithredol, y byddwn ni'n gallu gweld gwelliannau amlwg. Byddwn i wir yn croesawu barn yr Aelodau, o'r pwyllgor a'r Aelodau yn fwy cyffredinol, ynglŷn â beth fyddai'r ffyrdd gorau i'r Senedd barhau i graffu ar y ffordd mae hyn yn datblygu. Mae hyn yn rhywbeth sy'n mynd y tu hwnt i unrhyw Lywodraeth ac yn mynd y tu hwnt i unrhyw blaid. Mae'n rhaid i ni gael hyn yn iawn i'n cymdeithas, felly byddwn i'n croesawu sgyrsiau pellach ar hynny. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Gwasanaeth Gofal Cenedlaethol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health: Update on the National Care Service Programme

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Gwasanaeth Gofal Cenedlaethol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health: Update on the National Care Service Programme
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Deputy Minister, I am concerned that constituents of mine are being, quite frankly, exploited. I met with some homecare workers in my constituency who are sometimes working 12-hour shifts for as little as four hours of pay. They are expected to drive from home to home, from one side of Cardiff to the other, and they are not getting paid for any of that driving time. They are sometimes forced to work weeks on end without a day off, delivering care to our most vulnerable while stressed and exhausted.

These workers are on the health and care skilled worker visas, and when they raise their working conditions with their employers, whom their visas are tied to, the employers threaten their visa status to try and coerce and control the workers. When I heard this, I was actually at a loss for words at how disgusting and shocking this is. These migrant workers are being forced to work without getting paid for their labour.

So, would the Deputy Minister work with counterparts in the UK Government and in local authorities to try and root out these exploitative practices associated with this type of visa, to ensure that working conditions reflect the values that she has set out, rightly so, in today's statement, for both domestic and migrant workers in our social care sector?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Ddirprwy Weinidog, rwy'n pryderu bod etholwyr i mi yn cael eu hecsbloetio, a bod yn onest. Fe wnes i gyfarfod â rhai gweithwyr gofal cartref yn fy etholaeth sydd weithiau'n gweithio shifftiau 12 awr am gyn lleied â phedair awr o dâl. Mae disgwyl iddyn nhw yrru o gartref i gartref, o un ochr i Gaerdydd i'r llall, a dydyn nhw ddim yn cael eu talu am ddim o'r amser gyrru hwnnw. Weithiau maen nhw'n cael eu gorfodi i weithio wythnosau lawer heb ddiwrnod i ffwrdd, gan ddarparu gofal i'r rhai mwyaf agored i niwed tra'n flinedig iawn ac o dan straen.

Mae'r gweithwyr hyn ar fisâu gweithwyr medrus iechyd a gofal, a phan maen nhw'n codi eu hamodau gwaith gyda'u cyflogwyr, y mae eu fisâu yn gysylltiedig â nhw, mae'r cyflogwyr yn bygwth eu statws fisa i geisio gorfodi a rheoli'r gweithwyr. Pan glywais i hyn, roeddwn i methu credu pa mor ffiaidd a chywilyddus yw e. Mae'r gweithwyr mudol hyn yn cael eu gorfodi i weithio heb gael eu talu am eu llafur.

Felly, a fyddai'r Dirprwy Weinidog yn gweithio gyda chymheiriaid yn Llywodraeth y DU ac mewn awdurdodau lleol i geisio dileu'r arferion ecsbloetiol hyn sy'n gysylltiedig â'r math hwn o fisa, er mwyn sicrhau bod amodau gwaith yn adlewyrchu'r gwerthoedd y mae hi wedi'u nodi, yn gywir ddigon, yn y datganiad heddiw, ar gyfer gweithwyr domestig a mudol yn ein sector gofal cymdeithasol?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Gwasanaeth Gofal Cenedlaethol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health: Update on the National Care Service Programme
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Kiera. Yes. The short answer is, yes, certainly I will work with counterparts on this. Overseas workers should be valued. They should be treated no differently from workers who have been recruited domestically. They help make people's lives better. They make such a huge contribution to our society. No employer should be exploiting their status in order to, in some way, save money. I do not blame you for being lost for words.

We have published guidance and resources to help workers understand their rights, but I appreciate that, in many of these situations, these workers will be in a very vulnerable situation and might not feel that they know where to turn. I would implore them to know that a range of assistance is available, including the National Advisory Service for international social care workers. That provides advice, it provides information. We also work very closely with our trade union partners, who provide such important support and advocacy for overseas workers. I am really grateful that you have raised this issue today, because it should shame us all that this is happening.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Kiera. Byddwn. Yr ateb byr yw, byddwn, byddaf yn sicr yn gweithio gyda chymheiriaid ar hyn. Dylai gweithwyr tramor gael eu gwerthfawrogi. Ddylen nhw ddim gael eu trin yn wahanol i weithwyr sydd wedi cael eu recriwtio yn ddomestig. Maen nhw'n helpu i wella bywydau pobl. Maen nhw'n gwneud cyfraniad mor enfawr i'n cymdeithas. Ni ddylai'r un cyflogwr fod yn manteisio ar eu statws er mwyn arbed arian, mewn rhyw ffordd. Dydw i ddim yn eich beio chi am fethu â chredu'r peth.

Rydyn ni wedi cyhoeddi canllawiau ac adnoddau i helpu gweithwyr i ddeall eu hawliau, ond rwy'n gwerthfawrogi, mewn llawer o'r sefyllfaoedd hyn, y bydd y gweithwyr hyn mewn sefyllfa fregus iawn ac efallai na fyddan nhw'n teimlo eu bod nhw'n gwybod ble i droi. Byddwn i'n erfyn arnyn nhw i wybod bod yna ystod o gymorth ar gael, gan gynnwys y Gwasanaeth Cynghori Cenedlaethol ar gyfer gweithwyr gofal cymdeithasol rhyngwladol. Mae hwnnw'n darparu cyngor, mae'n darparu gwybodaeth. Rydyn ni hefyd yn gweithio'n agos iawn gyda'n partneriaid undebau llafur, sy'n darparu cymorth ac eiriolaeth mor bwysig i weithwyr tramor. Rwy'n ddiolchgar iawn eich bod chi wedi codi'r mater hwn heddiw, oherwydd dylai fod cywilydd arnom ni i gyd fod hyn yn digwydd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Gwasanaeth Gofal Cenedlaethol

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Ac yn olaf, Ddirprwy Weinidog, Catherine Cullen.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Gwasanaeth Gofal Cenedlaethol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health: Update on the National Care Service Programme
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Deputy Llywydd. I welcome the Deputy Minister's statement today, but it seems that the statement is doubling down again on this Stronger Safeguarding for a Safer Wales. As you know, I have already expressed serious reservations about this, because while it looks fluffy on the outside, it is not so on the inside.

We already know about the damage that overly burdensome safeguarding procedures can cause in the care and health services. At the moment, it is quite reactive. We only need to listen to some of the stories of people who have been under this to understand what it is like. So, we must ensure that social care does not suffer the same fate. Safeguarding must protect people without drowning front-line workers in paperwork and without placing front-line professionals' lives on hold while they are subject to safeguarding inquiries. How can we recruit and hope to retain in the care sector with these strict safeguarding measures in line? It does not go well.

The statement says that success will not be measured by structures created or documents published, but how exactly, then, are you going to measure success? And what measurable targets, timescales and outcomes will be published to demonstrate improvements in care recruitment and retention? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Rwy'n croesawu datganiad y Dirprwy Weinidog heddiw, ond mae'n ymddangos bod y datganiad unwaith eto yn atgyfnerthu Diogelu Cryfach ar gyfer Cymru Fwy Diogel. Fel y gwyddoch chi, rwyf eisoes wedi mynegi amheuon difrifol am hyn, oherwydd er ei fod yn edrych yn ddigon ysgafn ar y tu allan, nid felly mae hi ar y tu mewn.

Rydyn ni eisoes yn gwybod am y difrod y gall gweithdrefnau diogelu rhy feichus ei achosi yn y gwasanaethau gofal ac iechyd. Ar hyn o bryd, mae'n eithaf adweithiol. Dim ond gwrando ar rai o straeon pobl sydd wedi bod o dan hyn mae'n angen i ni ei wneud i ddeall sut beth ydyw. Felly, mae'n rhaid i ni sicrhau nad yw gofal cymdeithasol yn dioddef yr un tynged. Rhaid i ddiogelu amddiffyn pobl heb foddi gweithwyr rheng flaen mewn gwaith papur a heb roi bywydau gweithwyr proffesiynol rheng flaen ar stop tra eu bod yn destun ymchwiliadau diogelu. Sut allwn ni recriwtio a gobeithio cadw yn y sector gofal pan fo'r mesurau diogelu llym hyn ar waith? Dydy e ddim yn cyd-fynd yn dda.

Yn ôl y datganiad, fydd llwyddiant ddim yn cael ei fesur yn ôl y strwythurau a grëwyd na'r dogfennau a gyhoeddwyd, ond sut yn union, felly, ydych chi'n mynd i fesur llwyddiant? A pha dargedau, amserlenni a chanlyniadau mesuradwy fydd yn cael eu cyhoeddi i ddangos gwelliannau wrth recriwtio a chadw ym maes gofal? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Gwasanaeth Gofal Cenedlaethol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health: Update on the National Care Service Programme
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Catherine, for those questions. I know that there were a few other points that I won't repeat, but I appreciate why you're asking them, of course.

In terms of the safeguarding point—and I appreciate that you've raised this before—the system is very much meant to support some of the most vulnerable people in our society. Of course we wouldn't want to have unintended consequences to come as part of this, and I know that this is something that you're really concerned about. I wonder if you could write to me with the individual concerns that you have, because I'd really like to look into those, to make sure that something that we don't intend isn't going to happen. Would you mind writing to me so that I can look into that in some detail? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Catherine, am y cwestiynau hynny. Rwy'n gwybod, roedd yna ychydig o bwyntiau eraill wnaf i ddim eu hailadrodd, ond rwy'n gwerthfawrogi pam eich bod chi'n eu gofyn, wrth gwrs.

O ran y pwynt diogelu—ac rwy'n gwerthfawrogi eich bod chi wedi codi hyn o'r blaen—bwriad y system yw cefnogi rhai o'r bobl sydd fwyaf agored i niwed yn ein cymdeithas. Wrth gwrs, fydden ni ddim eisiau gweld canlyniadau anfwriadol fel rhan o hyn, ac rwy'n gwybod bod hyn yn rhywbeth rydych chi'n poeni'n fawr amdano. Tybed a allech chi ysgrifennu ataf gyda'r pryderon unigol sydd gennych, oherwydd fe hoffwn i edrych i mewn i'r rheini, i wneud yn siŵr na fydd rhywbeth nad ydym yn bwriadu ei wneud yn digwydd. A fyddech cystal ag ysgrifennu ataf er mwyn i mi allu edrych i mewn i hynny'n fanwl? Diolch.
